title: Inference conditions on a fixed target trial that was in fact selected after seeing the data
text:
Verification

Verdict. Partially addressed. Part of this problem is addressed by existing work; the entry names which part.
4 of the 4 independent auditors returned an opinion on this entry.

Literature and prior-art check

partially-solved / supported-with-caveat. The entry says standard inference conditions on a fixed target trial and ignores the search over candidate emulations. The search is now being reported in at least one applied setting: a 2025 European Journal of Epidemiology study uses a multiverse analysis to characterize uncertainty in the estimated effect of statin initiation on dementia across design choices. That is the design multiverse the entry proposes, already run. What remains unaddressed is the inferential half: a multiverse displays the spread and does not correct coverage, and no selective-inference treatment of protocol selection exists in the corpus. The entry should not claim the multiverse is absent. Cites 10.1007/s10654-025-01231-y: Runs the design multiverse the entry proposes, in an applied emulation, which means the proposal has a precedent rather than being untried.. Cites 10.1093/aje/kwae346: Documents the specification choices oncology emulations actually make, which is the empirical base for describing the search space..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / overstated. Outcome-dependent selection of a protocol using the analysis data can invalidate an interval calibrated for a protocol fixed in advance, so the narrowed problem is real. It is not true that every data-informed revision produces wrong coverage. Choices based only on treatment and covariate information may be handled conditionally, independent design and analysis samples break the relevant dependence, and simultaneous or selection-aware inference can cover specified searches. An algorithmically selected protocol produces a data-adaptive target; that does not automatically create an extra variance component, because coverage must first be defined conditionally or marginally and for either the selected estimand or a fixed scientific estimand. An undocumented human search precludes an exact reconstruction of that selection event, but it does not make all valid inference impossible. High severity is warranted only when outcome-relevant selection is material and ignored.

Grok 4.5, recency lens

open / supported. Selective-inference and post-selection literature exists for covariates and models, not for human search over TTE protocol components (eligibility, grace period, washout, outcomes). TARGET and Hansford 2025–2026 report the final protocol; they do not correct coverage for data-dependent protocol selection. Outcome-blinded design splits and dated decision logs remain proposals, not standard practice or validated TTE-specific selective-inference procedures. No CRAN/GitHub change for TrialEmulation/lmtp/ltmle/gfoRmula treats the protocol as a random object. Open.

GLM-5.2, third independent lens

open / supported. The claim is internally consistent and proportionate. It asserts that current practice does not treat the protocol as an estimated object with sampling variability. The reason given for it being open—that the search is undocumented and protocol development is not a well-defined selection event—directly supports the claim that standard inferential theory and current practice fail to account for this search. The scope is correctly pitched at current practice.

Decision path

R3:partially-solved(n=1/4) → R9:substantiated-overstatement(n=1/4):codex

title: Positivity diagnostics describe weights instead of naming which patient histories are unsupported
text: OVL-01 Partially addressed Very high priority Promising Tractability 4/5

title: Positivity diagnostics describe weights instead of naming which patient histories are unsupported
text:
Statement
A deterministic treatment strategy can assign a treatment that clinicians almost never give to patients with certain covariate histories. The standard response is to inspect the weight distribution and truncate the tail, which reduces variance, changes the implicit estimand and can leave substantial bias in place. What the diagnostic does not report is the quantity a reader needs: what fraction of the target population has no support for the strategy under study, which histories are the unsupported ones, and what estimand remains identified once they are set aside. A 2026 study of non-mutually exclusive assignment found that poor overlap defeated adjustment methods that were otherwise well specified, which is the failure mode a weight histogram is least able to show.

title: Positivity diagnostics describe weights instead of naming which patient histories are unsupported
text:
Why it is open
Practical positivity is a property of a conditional density over a growing history, so with more than a handful of time points the object to be diagnosed is high-dimensional and cannot be plotted. Truncation is attractive precisely because it converts an identification failure into a variance reduction, which reads as a modelling improvement rather than as a change of question. There is also no agreed target: reporting the unsupported fraction requires deciding what counts as support, and any threshold is a decision about the estimand that nobody currently has to state.

title: Positivity diagnostics describe weights instead of naming which patient histories are unsupported
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Target trial emulation under nonmutually exclusive assignment. Am J Epidemiol 2026;195(4):1045
Shows that poor overlap can defeat advanced adjustment methods, in a setting where assignment to strategies is not mutually exclusive.


lmtp: Non-Parametric Causal Effects of Feasible Interventions Based on Modified Treatment Policies. CRAN
Implements modified treatment policies and stochastic interventions for binary, categorical, continuous and multivariate treatments with censored outcomes and competing risks, which is the estimand class that restores positivity.

title: Positivity diagnostics describe weights instead of naming which patient histories are unsupported
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Replace deterministic interventions that the data cannot support with modified treatment policies, incremental propensity-score interventions or stochastic initiation rules, and state the trade in the paper rather than in the weight truncation. Report a causal support map over patient histories: the fraction of the target population with adequate support, which histories fail, and the estimand that survives. Derive partial-identification bounds for the unsupported strata, and set overlap-aware eligibility criteria before any outcome analysis so that restricting the population is a design decision with a date rather than a result.

title: Positivity diagnostics describe weights instead of naming which patient histories are unsupported
text:
Verification

Verdict. Partially addressed. Part of this problem is addressed by existing work; the entry names which part.
Dissent. literature dissented (open): The entry’s core claim, that diagnostics describe weights rather than naming which histories are unsupported, holds against the corpus. Two pieces of work sharpen rather than resolve it. […]
4 of the 4 independent auditors returned an opinion on this entry.

Literature and prior-art check

open / supported-with-caveat. The entry’s core claim, that diagnostics describe weights rather than naming which histories are unsupported, holds against the corpus. Two pieces of work sharpen rather than resolve it. A 2025 study measures the impact of near-positivity violations on IPTW-estimated marginal structural survival models with time-dependent covariates, which supplies the consequence the entry asserts. A 2026 American Journal of Epidemiology paper on target trial emulation under non-mutually exclusive assignment sets out structural pitfalls and remedies for exactly the overlap failure the entry cites. Neither produces a causal support map over histories, an unsupported-fraction statistic, or partial-identification bounds for the unsupported strata, so the specific artifacts the entry says are missing are still missing. Cites 10.1093/aje/kwag014: Names the structural pitfalls of overlapping assignment and proposes remedies, which is the setting in which the entry’s overlap failure was demonstrated.. Cites 10.1002/bimj.70093: Measures how near-positivity degrades weighted longitudinal survival estimation, supporting the entry’s premise that truncation does not rescue the estimate..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

partially-solved / overstated. A marginal weight histogram cannot localize poor support to particular histories, and structural nonpositivity is a decision-grade identification failure. However, the report conflates structural nonpositivity, practical near-nonpositivity, and finite-sample instability. Weight truncation does not convert an identification failure into variance reduction or necessarily define a coherent alternative causal estimand. It changes the estimating functional and usually biases estimation of the stated target, while structural nonpositivity remains unidentified. The claim that the high-dimensional object cannot be plotted is also too absolute because reduced history-specific diagnostics are possible. Pinned CICI 1.0 is a direct partial counterexample: its NAMESPACE exports feasible, plot.feasible, and summary.feasible; feasible() estimates conditional treatment densities, returns per-observation feasible intervention values and low_matrix objects, and reports the proportion below its threshold by strategy and time. Its gformula accepts the resulting individual intervention matrices. This implementation is limited to continuous interventions and an analyst-chosen alpha threshold, does not provide general partial-identification bounds, and does not cover arbitrary binary or categorical sustained strategies. Its threshold implementation also normalizes densities using bin widths but calculates cumsum(sort(row)) without bin-width weighting, so the advertised probability-mass threshold is miscalibrated whenever bin widths differ from one. Later-time diagnostics are evaluated over observed histories, which need not equal the history distribution induced by the intervention. Pinned lmtp 1.5.4 implements longitudinal modified treatment policies and an ipsi policy factory, but such intervention classes do not automatically restore positivity; policy-specific absolute continuity remains necessary, and lmtp trims estimated density ratios by default. Very-high severity is warranted when the prespecified strategy materially lacks support, but a universal support map and bounds are roadmap extensions rather than requirements for every adequately supported analysis. Cites CRAN:CICI@1.0: The exported feasible workflow estimates history-conditional treatment densities, constructs per-observation feasible alternatives, records low-density cells, and reports a strategy- and time-specific fraction classified as infeasible. This resolves the central diagnostic request for a limited continuous-treatment setting.. Cites CRAN:lmtp@1.5.4: The package supplies longitudinal TMLE and sequentially doubly robust estimators for modified treatment policies and exports an incremental probability-shift factory, partially implementing the proposed alternative-estimand direction. It does not itself guarantee positivity or provide the requested support map..

Grok 4.5, recency lens

partially-solved / supported-with-caveat. Inverted prior: treat the diagnostic gap as already closed, then check. The report’s own citations do not close it. Takayama (AJE 2026; 10.1093/aje/kwaf018) shows that poor overlap can defeat well-specified adjustment under non-mutually exclusive assignment; that is evidence the failure mode is real, not a fix for naming unsupported histories. lmtp implements modified treatment policies (MTPs) and stochastic interventions that can restore positivity by changing the estimand; that is the estimand-class response the agenda already proposes, not a diagnostic that reports which histories lack support or what fraction of the target population is unsupported.


What does close most of the stated gap is recent prior art the agenda does not cite. Danelian et al. (Journal of Causal Inference 2023; 10.1515/jci-2022-0032) introduced PoRT, a regression-tree diagnostic that flags in-sample positivity violations as interpretable covariate-defined subgroups, with implementation in the CRAN package RISCA (port). Chatton et al. (Epidemiology 2025; 10.1097/EDE.0000000000001902) extend this to longitudinal static and dynamic strategies as sPoRT, explicitly motivated by the inadequacy of inspecting cumulative inverse-probability weights: weight products can flag sparsity under correctly specified propensity models but do not name the problematic subgroups. In their HIV ART reanalysis, sPoRT returns time-updated subgroups with size as a share of those who should follow the rule (e.g., a CD4/WAZ-defined cell of n*=43, 5.4% of those assigned to initiate at 6 months) and recommended responses include redesign of the rule, exclusion of structurally unsupported baseline strata as a design decision, and switch to alternative estimands. Ring and Schomaker (Journal of Causal Inference 2026; 10.1515/jci-2025-0007; arXiv:2502.11820) add a kernel-based, estimand-specific sparsity diagnostic for continuous treatments and MTPs that reports effective data points per intervened observation, supports comparing alternative estimands before estimation, and is tied to the CICI / lmtp ecosystem. Moodie and Schulz (Statistics in Medicine 2025; 10.1002/sim.70194) give a hat-value style diagnostic for continuous exposures. Together these tools deliver the three quantities the problem says weight histograms do not: unsupported fraction (via subgroup size or near-zero EDP mass), which histories fail (tree leaves or low-EDP units), and guidance on the estimand that remains identifiable (rule redesign, population restriction, or MTP choice).
What remains open, so a full “solved” vote would be wrong: (1) no agreed support threshold (α, β in PoRT/sPoRT; kernel bandwidth in Ring) is still a free estimand decision; (2) partial-identification bounds for the unsupported strata are not a packaged, routine output of these diagnostics; (3) the methods are not first-class diagnostics inside the main TTE stacks the agenda names (TrialEmulation, gfoRmula, lmtp, WeightIt/cobalt still center weight and balance summaries rather than history-level support maps); (4) very high-dimensional continuous longitudinal histories remain hard to plot as a single “causal support map,” which is a packaging and reporting problem more than an identification one. Searches that returned no stronger closer: TTE-package release notes / PRs for TrialEmulation, gfoRmula, gfoRmulaICE, lmtp, WeightIt, MatchIt, cobalt, CICI for a history-level support map; TARGET / HARPER / STaRT-RWE / ENCePP / FDA-RWE 2025–2026 guidance mandating unsupported-fraction reporting; arXiv/medRxiv 2024–2026 for partial-ID bounds specifically for positivity-unsupported TTE strata as standard practice. Bottom line: the claim that standard weight diagnostics hide the real object is still right for modal practice, but the claim that the field has no method that names unsupported histories is no longer true after PoRT (2023), sPoRT (2025), and Ring–Schomaker (2026). Cites 10.1097/EDE.0000000000001902: Longitudinal sequential positivity diagnostic that returns interpretable, time-updated covariate-defined subgroups lacking support under static or dynamic treatment strategies, with subgroup size as a share of those assigned by the rule; explicitly contrasts this with weight-product diagnostics that do not name histories.. Cites 10.1515/jci-2022-0032: Point-treatment precursor: nonparametric regression-tree search for sparse propensity cells defined by covariate values, without requiring a correctly specified parametric propensity model; shipped as port in CRAN RISCA.. Cites 10.1515/jci-2025-0007: Estimand-specific kernel sparsity diagnostic that scores effective data support for each intervened observation, compares static, dynamic, and MTP estimands before outcome analysis, and guides population restriction or estimand redesign; continuous-treatment case the report’s weight-histogram complaint does not cover.. Cites arxiv:2502.11820: Open preprint of the Ring–Schomaker diagnostic (same content as 10.1515/jci-2025-0007), with simulation and CHAPAS-3 pharmacoepidemiology illustration and public code for the EDP diagnostic.. Cites 10.1002/sim.70194: Lightweight hat-value style positivity diagnostic for continuous exposures in Statistics in Medicine; complements tree and kernel approaches for the continuous case where weight histograms are least informative.. Cites https://cran.r-project.org/package=RISCA: Released software that turns PoRT into a callable diagnostic returning character summaries of positivity-violating subgroups rather than a weight distribution alone..

GLM-5.2, third independent lens

open / supported. The problem statement accurately identifies a gap in current positivity diagnostics: they focus on weight distributions rather than identifying unsupported patient histories and the resulting estimand. The reasons given for it being open (high-dimensionality of histories, lack of agreed thresholds for support) are valid and support the claim that this is an open methodological challenge. The claim is proportionate and does not overstate the issue as an impossibility where it is merely a current practice gap, though it correctly notes the structural difficulty of plotting high-dimensional objects.

Decision path

R3:partially-solved(n=2/4) → R9:substantiated-overstatement(n=1/4):codex

text:
How the evidence falls in time
135 papers in the reviewed corpus bear on this problem, published 2006 to 2026. Progress and a fresh assertion of openness land in the same year.
This problem is recurrent: three or more papers spanning at least eight years assert it independently. Sustained restatement by authors who mostly do not cite each other is the strongest evidence this reading can offer that a gap is real rather than one group’s framing.
It is also being closed in pieces: partial results come from more than one paper in more than one year, each covering a different part.

title: The visit process is treated as a nuisance to be imputed rather than as part of the causal structure
text:
Statement
Biomarkers and diagnoses are observed when a patient attends care and a clinician orders a test. That visit process depends on latent severity, on prior treatment and often on an impending outcome, so record-based covariate histories are irregular and selectively missing in a way that carries clinical information. Missing-at-random conditional on the recorded history can therefore fail precisely because the recording is itself informative. Standard handling, and last observation carried forward in particular, constructs an artificial history in which a patient’s state is asserted to be unchanged over an interval during which the absence of measurement was itself evidence about their state.

title: The visit process is treated as a nuisance to be imputed rather than as part of the causal structure
text:
Why it is open
Conditioning on having been observed can open a collider path, so the natural fix makes a different bias, and choosing between them requires knowing the structure that is in question. Inverse-intensity-of-visit weights are unstable when visit rates vary by an order of magnitude across patients, which they do. Modeling the visit process jointly with treatment and outcome multiplies the nuisance components and therefore the positivity requirements, so the more faithful model can be the less identifiable one.

title: The visit process is treated as a nuisance to be imputed rather than as part of the causal structure
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Model visits as recurrent events or point processes jointly with treatment and outcome, and compare complete case, last observation carried forward, multiple imputation, inverse-intensity weighting and joint latent-state targeted learning on data generated with a known, treatment-dependent visiting mechanism. Include healthcare use as a process in the causal diagram rather than as a baseline confounder, so that conditioning decisions can be read off the graph. Report visit-weight dispersion and the calibration of the predicted visit intensity, since an uncalibrated intensity model produces weights that look like adjustment and are noise.

title: The visit process is treated as a nuisance to be imputed rather than as part of the causal structure
text:
Verification

Verdict. Partially addressed. 2 independent auditors judged the claim as stated too strong. Estimators that model the observation process jointly with treatment and outcome exist in three separate families; applied emulations continue to use complete case or last observation carried forward, and healthcare use is entered as a baseline confounder rather than as a process. Moved by the full-text reading: 11 findings from 11 papers naming work that covers part of this problem survived both the reader and an independent second reviewer, so the verdict moves from overstated to partially-addressed. A further 83 findings in the same reading restate the problem as open; the two are consistent, and the part that is covered is named above.
Dissent. grok dissented (supported-with-caveat): Inverted-prior search finds methods that put the visit process in the causal or estimating structure, so the problem is not open as a pure absence of methodology. […]
Revised by the full-text reading. Applied full-text reading of the consolidated library.

Verdict changed

overstated -> partially-addressed 11 surviving findings from: Applying Trial Emulation Methods to Population-Scale Linked ; Bias of time-varying exposure effects due to time-varying co; Comparison of a Target Trial Emulation Framework to Cox Regr; Continuous-Time Causal Inference With Marked Point Process W; Estimation of marginal structural models under irregular vis; Missingness in Eligibility Criteria for Target Trial Emulati; Multiply robust estimation of marginal structural models in ; Target Trial Emulation to Improve Causal Inference from Obse; The Impact of Different CD4 Cell-Count Monitoring and Switch; gfoRmula: An R Package for Estimating the Effects of Sustain; simcausal R Package: Conducting Transparent and Reproducible. New citations: 10.1002/pds.5328, 10.1002/sim.70102, 10.1002/sim.70500, 10.1016/j.patter.2020.100008, 10.1093/aje/kwv083, 10.1093/biomtc/ujae065, 10.1101/2022.05.27.22275037, 10.1186/s12874-022-01831-2, 10.1681/asn.0000000000000152, 10.18637/jss.v081.i02, 10.23889/ijpds.v9i5.2884


4 of the 4 independent auditors returned an opinion on this entry.

Literature and prior-art check

partially-solved / overstated. The entry says standard handling constructs artificial histories and that modeling visits jointly with treatment and outcome multiplies nuisance components without a worked solution. Three separate estimator families in the corpus contradict the strong reading. A 2024 Biometrics paper proposes a multiply robust estimator for marginal structural models under irregularly spaced, covariate-driven observation times and shows it is more flexible and more efficient than the previously proposed doubly weighted estimator. A 2023 BMC Medical Research Methodology paper gives calibrated inverse probability weights for marginal structural models under irregular visits with an unmeasured confounder. A 2025 Statistics in Medicine paper builds continuous-time weights from a marked point process for the same reason. What survives is an adoption claim rather than a methods claim: these estimators exist and applied emulation pipelines do not use them, and healthcare use is still entered as a baseline confounder rather than modeled as a process. Cites 10.1093/biomtc/ujae065: Supplies a multiply robust estimator for exactly the setting the entry describes, and demonstrates it is more efficient than the existing doubly weighted alternative.. Cites 10.1186/s12874-022-01831-2: Gives calibrated weights for irregular visits with an unmeasured confounder, addressing the weight instability the entry raises.. Cites 10.1002/sim.70102: Models visits as a point process jointly with treatment, which is the direction the entry proposes..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / overstated. The central problem is technically real. When visit or test ordering depends on treatment and on an unobserved current prognostic state, missingness need not be at random given recorded history; LOCF then replaces an unknown trajectory with a constant one. Identification remains open without additional structural assumptions, external measurements, or sensitivity parameters. Several supporting claims are too broad. Conditioning on observation opens a collider path only under particular causal structures. Inverse-intensity weights require conditional independent observation, correct intensity models, and observation positivity; heterogeneity in marginal visit rates, even by an order of magnitude, does not by itself make the weights unstable. Joint modeling adds nuisance models and identifying assumptions, but it does not automatically multiply positivity requirements. Calibration is useful but insufficient because a conditionally misspecified intensity model can be marginally calibrated. Very high severity is proportionate only when decision-relevant eligibility variables, confounders, or outcomes are materially visit-dependent, not for every record-based emulation.

Grok 4.5, recency lens

partially-solved / supported-with-caveat. Inverted-prior search finds methods that put the visit process in the causal or estimating structure, so the problem is not open as a pure absence of methodology. It is not fully solved either: the report’s hard tradeoffs remain live, and the comparative evaluation it proposes has not been delivered for sustained-strategy target trial emulation under a known, treatment-dependent visiting mechanism.


Cited works first. Goldstein et al. (JAMIA 2019; 10.1093/jamia/ocz148) characterize when informative visits bias EHR association analyses; that paper diagnoses the mechanism and does not close it. Wang et al. (npj Digit Med 2026; 10.1038/s41746-026-02563-z) elevate the observation process to an operational constraint on whether an EHR can realize a target trial protocol element. Secondary commentary on that paper treats the contribution as specification-versus-realization discipline, not as a solved estimator. Both strengthen the claim that the issue is still on the agenda; neither resolves identification or estimation under treatment-dependent visiting.
Prior art that treats visits as structure rather than pure nuisance: (i) inverse-intensity-of-visit (IIW) theory and software for irregular longitudinal data (Pullenayegum line; CRAN IrregLong with Cox visit-intensity weights and IIW-GEE), still actively refined in 2025 on visit-model variable selection and selection of patients with no follow-up; (ii) parametric g-formula software that models a random measurement or visit process jointly with covariates for sustained strategies (gfoRmula’s visitprocess argument: visit indicators attached to intermittently measured confounders, with last-measured values and a cap on consecutive missed visits); (iii) Kalia et al. (BMC Med Res Methodol 2023; 10.1186/s12874-022-01831-2), calibrated inverse probability weights for marginal structural models under irregular visits, with Monte Carlo evaluation; (iv) Kalia et al. (Stat Med 2025; 10.1002/sim.70102), continuous-time MSM weights factored as visit intensity times dose (marked point process) on primary-care EHR for cumulative SGLT-2i exposure and recurrent UTI, explicitly motivated by informative visit timing. Coulombe et al. (Stat Methods Med Res 2023) combine inverse intensity of visit weights with individualized treatment rules in longitudinal observational data, which is related but not full sustained-strategy TTE.
What remains open, and why a full solved vote fails. IIW and continuous-time visit weights still require sequential positivity for the visit intensity and can be unstable when intensities vary sharply across patients; Kalia 2025 itself discusses extreme weights, stabilization, and constrained optimal weights, not elimination of the variance problem the report flags. Joint visit–treatment–outcome models still multiply nuisance components and positivity requirements; that structural cost is not removed by packaging. gfoRmula’s visit process assumes a discrete grid and a correctly specified visit model, and still encodes non-visit intervals via last measured values, so it does not by itself refute the LOCF critique for continuous-time EHR generation. No 2024–2026 paper or package release was found that runs the report’s proposed horse race (complete case, LOCF, MI, IIW, joint latent-state targeted learning) on data generated with a known treatment-dependent visiting mechanism in a sustained-strategy TTE design. Method proposals and single-setting applications therefore count as partial, not full, resolution.
Package and guidance scan. IrregLong and gfoRmula implement visit or measurement process handling; TrialEmulation, lmtp, ltmle, WeightIt, MatchIt, cobalt, ipw, adjustedCurves, riskRegression, zEpid, causallib, lifelines, and scikit-survival did not surface merged work that closes this gap for informative EHR visit processes under sustained strategies. 2025–2026 RWE guidances (FDA RWE, EMA/HMA registry, ICH E9(R1), TARGET, HARPER/STaRT-RWE, ENCePP, ISPE, NICE) frame data-generation and missingness issues at a high level; none was found that settles a preferred causal handling of informative visits for TTE.
Caveat on the claim as stated. Applied TTE and EHR pipelines still often grid time and carry forward or impute under MAR, so the nuisance framing is still a fair description of common practice. The methodological literature has long refused that framing, so a reader who only knows IIW, gfoRmula visitprocess, or continuous-time marked point process MSMs would find the absolute statement overstated. The agenda item that remains is comparative, practical, and identification-theoretic under realistic visit heterogeneity, not the invention of the first joint visit model.
Queries run (among others): Goldstein informative visit JAMIA 2019; Wang operational TTE npj Digit Med 2026; informative visit process inverse intensity EHR TTE 2024–2026; joint modeling visit process treatment outcome causal; site:arxiv.org informative visit inverse intensity; gfoRmula/lmtp/TrialEmulation visit process; CRAN IrregLong; Kalia MSM irregular visits; Kalia continuous-time marked point process 2025; Pullenayegum IIW 2025 Biometrics; Coulombe ITR IIV; FDA/EMA/TARGET visit observation process TTE. Cites 10.1002/sim.70102: Implements continuous-time MSM weights as the product of visit-intensity weights and dose weights via a marked point process on primary-care EHR, treating informative visit timing as part of the treatment-process model rather than as a nuisance to impute for cumulative exposure and recurrent outcomes.. Cites 10.1186/s12874-022-01831-2: Gives calibrated IPW estimators for MSMs when visits are irregular, with Monte Carlo evidence that calibration reduces finite-sample bias relative to uncalibrated longitudinal weights under irregular observation and unmeasured confounding.. Cites 10.1016/j.patter.2020.100008: Released software for sustained treatment strategies that models a random measurement or visit process jointly with intermittently observed covariates (visitprocess), so visits enter the g-formula rather than being only a pre-analysis cleaning step; CRAN description still advertises handling of a random measurement/visit process.. Cites cran:IrregLong: Maintained CRAN implementation of inverse-intensity weights and IIW-GEE for irregular, potentially informative observation times, providing operational infrastructure for visit-process adjustment outside pure LOCF or MAR imputation..

GLM-5.2, third independent lens

open / supported. The problem statement accurately describes a methodological tension in EHR-based target trial emulation: the visit process is informative, yet standard practice treats it as a nuisance to be imputed. The reasons given for it being open (collider bias from conditioning on observation, instability of inverse-intensity weights, and positivity violations from joint modeling) are valid structural tradeoffs that genuinely support the claim being open. The claim is proportionate and does not assert an impossibility, but rather highlights a difficult modeling tradeoff that remains unresolved in standard practice.

Decision path

R3:partially-solved(n=2/4) → R8:overstated-majority(n=2/4) → R17:reading-moved(overstated->partially-addressed)

How the evidence falls in time
93 papers in the reviewed corpus bear on this problem, published 2010 to 2026. Progress and a fresh assertion of openness land in the same year.
This problem is recurrent: three or more papers spanning at least eight years assert it independently. Sustained restatement by authors who mostly do not cite each other is the strongest evidence this reading can offer that a gap is real rather than one group’s framing.
It is also being closed in pieces: partial results come from more than one paper in more than one year, each covering a different part.

title: A counterfactual prediction is validated under the assumptions that produced it, and nothing maps its output to a decision
text:
Statement
Emulation is increasingly used to produce a risk under a hypothetical treatment strategy and to learn which treatment an individual should receive, and both outputs are then offered as decision support. Ordinary validation compares a predicted risk against an observed outcome, and under a strategy the outcome is observed only for the part of a validation set that happened to follow it, so the label a calibration curve needs does not exist for everyone else. Counterfactual analogues of the standard measures now exist: artificial censoring with inverse probability weighting extends calibration, the c-index, the time-dependent AUC and the Brier score to sustained strategies with time-to-event outcomes, and identification results cover loss-based measures, the ROC area and the calibration curve even when the prediction model is misspecified. All of them are identified under the same conditional exchangeability and positivity conditions used to fit the model, and violations are referred to sensitivity analysis, so a counterfactual calibration curve computed in a validation database is evidence about fit rather than about the assumption carrying the causal claim. What nobody reports is how these measures behave when exchangeability fails, so a check aimed at the failure mode that motivates the whole exercise has no known operating characteristics. The scoping review that named the absence screened 4919 records down to 13 included papers and asked for extension to non-discrete treatments and to nonparametric models; the published performance results cover discrete strategies, with dynamic regimes in an appendix. At the applied end a machine-learned antidepressant rule was scored by emulating a four-arm target trial in a held-out test set of the same claims database of 715,246 patients and 739,980 treatment episodes, which reuses the identification assumptions instead of testing them, and applied prediction work still stops at predicted probabilities without defining the action space that maps them to the set of possible decisions.

title: A counterfactual prediction is validated under the assumptions that produced it, and nothing maps its output to a decision
text:
Why it is open
The label validation needs is the outcome under the strategy, and it is missing by construction for exactly the individuals whose treatment departed from that strategy; recovering it requires the identification assumptions, which is why every counterfactual performance estimator inherits them and none can test them. Moving validation to a second database changes the confounding structure along with the population, so a disagreement between sources is not attributable to the model rather than to the new source’s own unmeasured confounding. The design that breaks the circle is a trial randomizing patients to the rule against usual care, which costs what the observational route exists to avoid. A threshold is what turns a predicted benefit into an action, and a threshold encodes how much benefit is worth how much harm, which is a value judgment no estimator supplies. The simulation that would at least establish whether counterfactual calibration degrades under unmeasured confounding has not been published, and its answer would be a property of the confounding structure assumed, so it yields a scenario rather than a guarantee.

title: A counterfactual prediction is validated under the assumptions that produced it, and nothing maps its output to a decision

What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Lin L, Sperrin M, Jenkins DA, Martin GP, Peek N. A scoping review of causal methods enabling predictions under hypothetical interventions. Diagn Progn Res 2021;5(1):3
Screens 4919 records down to 13 included papers, finds most observational approaches built on marginal structural models and g-estimation, and concludes that techniques for validating causal prediction models are in their infancy.


Keogh RH, Van Geloven N. Prediction under interventions: evaluation of counterfactual performance using longitudinal observational data. Epidemiology 2024;35(3):329-339

Boyer CB, Dahabreh IJ, Steingrimsson JA. Estimating and evaluating counterfactual prediction models. Stat Med 2025;44(23-24):e70287

Voter SC, Dahabreh IJ, Boyer CB, Rahbar H, Kontos D, Steingrimsson JA. Counterfactual prediction from machine learning models: transportability and joint analysis for model development and evaluation using multi-source data. Diagn Progn Res 2025;9(1):22
Estimates counterfactual model performance in the population underlying an observational study either from that study alone or by transporting from the randomized trial it emulates, and states that the assumptions of both routes are untestable.

title: A counterfactual prediction is validated under the assumptions that produced it, and nothing maps its output to a decision
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Start with operating characteristics: simulate a sustained strategy under a known confounding structure, compute counterfactual calibration, discrimination and the Brier score with the confounder in the adjustment set and then without it, and report how large the confounding has to be before each measure moves. Report counterfactual performance as a bias-analysis interval rather than as a point estimate, so a calibration curve carries the same sensitivity parameter as the effect estimate it descends from. Extend the counterfactual performance results from discrete strategies to dose-defined and dynamic strategies, which is what the scoping review asked for and where routine treatment data actually sit. For a learned rule, require the emulated evaluation to be reported with the action space it implies: the decision threshold, the number of patients whose treatment would change, and the net benefit at that threshold, rather than a table of predicted probabilities.

title: A counterfactual prediction is validated under the assumptions that produced it, and nothing maps its output to a decision
text:
Verification

Verdict. Partially addressed. Part of this problem is addressed by existing work; the entry names which part.
Dissent. literature dissented (open): Searched the 1,376-record screened corpus and read two records in full text. The core claim survives: every counterfactual performance measure in the corpus is identified under the same exchangeability and positivity conditions used to fit the model, and no record reports how those measures behave when the conditions fail, so the check aimed at the failure mode has no […]
4 of the 4 independent auditors returned an opinion on this entry.

Literature and prior-art check

open / supported-with-caveat. Searched the 1,376-record screened corpus and read two records in full text. The core claim survives: every counterfactual performance measure in the corpus is identified under the same exchangeability and positivity conditions used to fit the model, and no record reports how those measures behave when the conditions fail, so the check aimed at the failure mode has no established operating characteristics. Two caveats, both from records the entry does not cite. First, the entry’s closing sentence, that applied prediction work stops at predicted probabilities and defines no action space, is contradicted by a 2021 study in the corpus that estimates individual treatment effects for two direct oral anticoagulants, converts them into treatment recommendations, and evaluates those recommendations with c-for-benefit, absolute risk reduction and an absolute risk difference obtained by trial emulation, reporting how many patients would have been recommended something other than what they received. That is the action-space reporting the entry’s proposed direction asks for, published four years before the entry. Second, the entry describes the machine-learned antidepressant rule as scored in a held-out test set of 715,246 patients and 739,980 treatment episodes, and carries no citation for it. Both numbers are real and come from the 2021 Taiwanese study that is one of the four gaps behind this entry, but they are the full analysis cohort and the count of next-step episodes, not the test set: the evaluation ran in a randomly assigned 20 percent of patients. The design description is otherwise exact, since that study does state one target trial with four arms. The uncited numeric claim and the misplaced denominator are the two things a reader could check and find wrong.

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

partially-solved / overstated. The central identification concern is correct: except where consistency links observed outcomes to the strategy, individual counterfactual outcomes are unavailable, and performance measures estimated from observational validation data cannot by themselves test conditional or sequential exchangeability. A held-out sample from the same database addresses overfitting and sampling variability, not unmeasured confounding. Existing work nevertheless supplies identifiable counterfactual calibration, discrimination, and loss measures and shows how predictions can enter decision rules, so neither the validation problem nor the prediction-to-decision mapping is wholly unsolved. Several absolutes are technically wrong. Performance identification in a validation population need not use exactly the assumptions used during model development; it additionally depends on consistency and the relevant treatment, adherence, censoring, and possibly transport conditions. Exchangeability is not empirically testable from the same observed data, but observed treatment support and practical positivity can be diagnosed; structural nonpositivity cannot be repaired by truncation or sensitivity analysis. A randomized rule-versus-usual-care trial identifies the effect of adopting the rule, not the calibration of every individual counterfactual prediction, and it is not the only conceivable causal design. Decisions do not invariably require a scalar threshold, especially for multi-arm or dynamic strategies; they require an explicit action space and utility or loss function. Likewise, a sensitivity parameter for an average treatment effect cannot automatically be carried unchanged into nonlinear calibration, AUC, or Brier-score functionals; a metric-specific sensitivity model must be derived. Simulations can characterize selected confounding scenarios but cannot validate exchangeability in the application. The action-space and causal-validity issues are important for decision-support claims, while extensions to continuous treatments and additional simulation studies are roadmap items rather than universal prerequisites. Literature-novelty assertions such as ‘nobody reports’ were not judged. No R or Python package capability is asserted here, so no pinned-package source check applies. Cites doi:10.1097/EDE.0000000000001713: Provides counterfactual calibration, concordance, time-dependent AUC, and Brier-score evaluation for sustained strategies using artificial censoring and weighting, conditional on identification assumptions.. Cites doi:10.1002/sim.70287: Provides identification and estimation results for counterfactual loss, ROC-area, and calibration functionals, including evaluation of a fixed misspecified prediction model; it does not verify causal identification assumptions.. Cites doi:10.1097/EDE.0000000000001173: Shows that predictions can be mapped into an explicit decision rule and evaluated for clinical utility, refuting the universal claim that nothing maps predictions to decisions while leaving observational identification limitations intact..

Grok 4.5, recency lens

partially-solved / supported-with-caveat. Inverted-prior search first re-read the report’s own prior work, then scanned 2024–2026 epidemiology/stats literature, arXiv/medRxiv, and related software. Keogh & Van Geloven (2024) and Boyer, Dahabreh & Steingrimsson (2025) do what the report already says: identify and estimate counterfactual calibration, discrimination, loss, AUC, and Brier under conditional exchangeability and positivity, including (in appendices) dynamic or time-varying regimes. Their simulations probe nuisance misspecification and model misspecification, not exchangeability failure. Boyer states that exchangeability violations can be examined with sensitivity analysis and that further work is needed; Voter et al. (2025) restate that both observational and trial-transport routes rest on untestable assumptions. That circular-validation core remains open for sustained-strategy interventional prediction as formulated in TTE.


Two lines of prior art close parts of the agenda without closing the whole problem. First, Rambachan, Coston & Kennedy (arXiv:2212.09844, revised 2025 as robust design/evaluation under unobserved confounding) partially identify MSE, calibration, TPR/FPR, ROC/precision-recall, and expected decision payoffs under explicit bounds on outcome differences between selected and unselected units, and they apply the framework to credit risk with thresholds. That is exactly the report’s proposed move of reporting performance as a confounding-sensitive interval and tying scores to actions, but the data structure is selective labels (binary selection, binary outcome), not artificial censoring plus IPW for sustained strategies with time-to-event outcomes. Per the case-discipline rule, that does not solve longitudinal interventional validation. Second, Luijken et al. (2024) formalize estimands for sequential prediction under interventions so that risks under defined intervention options can inform decisions; Sachs et al. (2020, already cited) argue for clinical utility over raw accuracy and for randomized evaluation of prediction-driven rules. Neither delivers published operating characteristics of Keogh/Boyer-style counterfactual calibration curves when exchangeability fails, nor a standard that forces learned rules to report threshold, treatment-change count, and net benefit under a stated action space.
No CRAN/GitHub release was found that implements confounding-sensitive counterfactual performance for sustained strategies. No 2025–2026 FDA/EMA/ICH/ENCePP/TARGET-style guidance resolves validation-under-assumptions for interventional prediction. Net: the report’s central failure mode (performance identified only under the assumptions used to fit the model, with no published OC under violation for that estimator class, and applied work often stopping at probabilities) is still open; partial solutions exist for decision-oriented estimands and for robust performance under selective-label confounding. Cites arxiv:2212.09844: Provides partial-identification bounds and estimators for predictive performance (MSE, calibration, TPR/FPR, ROC-style measures) and expected decision payoffs under researcher-specified unobserved confounding, so performance is reported as a sensitivity interval rather than a point estimate that pretends exchangeability holds. Covers the report’s sensitivity-interval and action/threshold directions in the selective-labels setting (lending, pretrial, testing), not sustained-strategy TTE interventional prediction.. Cites 10.1002/bimj.70011: Formalizes population, decision moments, intervention options, horizon, and predictors so prediction under interventions is stated as a decision-relevant estimand rather than a free-floating probability. Partially addresses the report’s ‘nothing maps output to a decision’ clause by defining the intervention options the risk is supposed to inform; does not supply confounding OC for counterfactual performance metrics or net-benefit reporting standards for learned rules.. Cites 10.1002/sim.70287: Identification and estimation of counterfactual loss, AUC, and calibration that remain valid when the prediction model is misspecified, with appendix extensions toward random/dynamic and time-varying regimes. Advances the methods the report already treats as existing; explicitly leaves exchangeability violations to sensitivity analysis and further work, so it does not close the OC-under-failure gap..

GLM-5.2, third independent lens

abstain / supported. The statement is internally consistent and correctly identifies that counterfactual performance estimators inherit the identification assumptions of the causal model, meaning they cannot independently test those assumptions. The claim that ‘nobody reports’ how these measures behave under exchangeability failure is a claim about current practice rather than a structural impossibility, which is appropriate since the proposed direction is to simulate this. The scope and severity are proportionate to the risk of using unvalidated counterfactual predictions for clinical decisions. I abstain on the status axis because I cannot verify the absence of recent publications that might have addressed this gap.

Decision path

R3:partially-solved(n=2/3) → R9:substantiated-overstatement(n=1/4):codex

title: Learned embeddings from clinical text can carry post-treatment information into a baseline adjustment set
text: LRN-03 Overstated High priority Emerging Tractability 3/5

title: Learned embeddings from clinical text can carry post-treatment information into a baseline adjustment set
text:
Statement
Notes, imaging and device data capture severity, treatment rationale and outcomes that structured fields miss, and natural language processing has been proposed for eligibility extraction and phenotyping on that basis. The risk is specific: a learned representation of a clinical note is a dense summary of everything in the note, which can include post-treatment information, the identity of the site, the behavior of the treating clinician and protected characteristics. Adjusting for such a representation is adjusting for an object whose causal role is unknown and probably mixed, and the usual justification, that more information reduces confounding, does not hold when part of that information is a descendant of treatment.

title: Learned embeddings from clinical text can carry post-treatment information into a baseline adjustment set
text:
Why it is open
The causal role of an embedding dimension is not interpretable, so the standard remedy of inspecting the adjustment set does not apply. Temporal leakage is easy to introduce and hard to detect, because a note timestamped before treatment can still describe a treatment decision already made. Restricting to pre-assignment text limits the leak but does not eliminate it, and no test distinguishes a representation that encodes prognosis from one that encodes the treatment that was about to be given.

title: Learned embeddings from clinical text can carry post-treatment information into a baseline adjustment set
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Wang, et al. An operational target trial emulation framework for causal inference using electronic health records. npj Digit Med 2026
Proposes natural language processing for eligibility extraction and phenotyping within an emulation framework.


Feuerriegel S, Frauen D, Melnychuk V, et al. Causal machine learning for predicting treatment outcomes. Nat Med 2024;30:958-968
Sets the boundary between predictive performance and causal validity that high-dimensional adjustment repeatedly crosses.

title: Learned embeddings from clinical text can carry post-treatment information into a baseline adjustment set
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Use temporally locked encoders trained only on pre-assignment text, and audit the resulting representations for treatment leakage by testing whether the embedding predicts the assigned treatment better than the structured pre-assignment covariates do. Prefer interpretable proxy sets, or an explicit proximal role in which the proxy’s function is stated, over indiscriminate adjustment for a high-dimensional representation. Report what the embedding was allowed to see, in dates rather than in prose, because that is the claim on which its validity rests.

title: Learned embeddings from clinical text can carry post-treatment information into a baseline adjustment set
text:
Verification

Verdict. Overstated. 3 independent auditors judged the claim as stated too strong. Embeddings whose input window is not demonstrably prior to treatment assignment and the underlying treatment decision can carry post-treatment or decision-related information into a nominal baseline adjustment set. Validity therefore requires auditable content provenance and causal timing. Treatment predictiveness alone neither establishes nor rules out leakage, and a proximal interpretation requires explicit proxy roles and additional identification conditions.
4 of the 4 independent auditors returned an opinion on this entry.

Literature and prior-art check

open / supported. A search for treatment leakage, temporal locking or auditing of learned representations used as adjustment sets returned nothing in the screened corpus. The claim is therefore unrefuted and weakly evidenced: the corpus is built from target trial and g-method phrases, and work on representation leakage would most likely appear in machine learning venues that none of the eight phrases reaches. The vote is open at the confidence ceiling this project sets for searched-and-found-nothing.

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / overstated. An embedding derived from content observed after treatment assignment or after the clinical treatment decision can encode descendants of treatment and make baseline adjustment invalid. The risk is conditional on the source content and causal timing, not on representation learning or opacity by itself. A deterministic embedding of genuinely baseline variables remains baseline, and site or protected characteristics are not automatically invalid adjustment variables. Individual embedding dimensions need not be causally interpretable if the provenance and causal roles of their inputs are defensible. The proposed treatment-prediction test is not a valid leakage diagnostic: stronger prediction of assigned treatment can arise from additional legitimate confounder information, instruments, or actual leakage, and the test cannot distinguish these explanations. Likewise, merely declaring an embedding a proximal proxy is insufficient without valid proxy roles and the associated identifying conditions. No package capability claim is present.

Grok 4.5, recency lens

partially-solved / overstated. The report frames embedding adjustment as an open risk without naming the literature that already defines and partially remediates it. Daoud, Jerzak, and Johansson (NAACL 2022) formalize treatment leakage when text is used as a confounder proxy, including leakage from pre-assignment documents that anticipate treatment. Daoud, Johansson, and Jerzak (arXiv:2601.02400, late 2025/2026) add formal definitions, four distillation methods (similarity passage removal, distant-supervision passage classification, salient-feature removal, iterative nullspace projection), and simulation plus empirical sensitivity analysis; they explicitly address the paradox that pre-timestamped text can still encode treatment. That is real prior art for detection and mitigation, not mere restatement. Residual openness remains for clinical TTE: methods are not standard in EHR phenotyping pipelines; Wang et al. (2026) still promote NLP for eligibility without a required leakage audit; temporal locking plus formal comparison of embedding-versus-structured treatment prediction is recommended in the agenda and only partially operationalized outside medicine. Sensitivity and distillation quantify or reduce leakage; they do not make an embedding’s causal role fully interpretable dimension-by-dimension. The problem is therefore partially solved in the text-as-confounder literature and still under-adopted in clinical emulation practice. Cites https://aclanthology.org/2022.naacl-main.413/: Defines treatment leakage when text used for confounding adjustment also carries treatment signal, including leakage from pre-assignment future-referencing language; establishes the identification and estimation problem the agenda restates.. Cites arXiv:2601.02400: Provides formal statistical definitions of treatment leakage plus automatic and semi-automatic distillers and leakage sensitivity analysis so that text representations can be purged or stress-tested for treatment-predictive content before adjustment..

GLM-5.2, third independent lens

open / overstated. The claim correctly identifies the risk of post-treatment leakage in learned embeddings. However, the assertion that ‘no test distinguishes’ a representation encoding prognosis from one encoding treatment is an overstatement of impossibility when it means that no standard or easily applicable test exists. It is a claim about current practice wearing the language of impossibility.

Decision path

R3:partially-solved(n=1/4) → R8:overstated-majority(n=3/4)

title: Flexible estimation is presented as a remedy for identification failure
text: LRN-01 Partially addressed High priority Promising Tractability 4/5

title: Flexible estimation is presented as a remedy for identification failure
text:
Statement
Identification is a property of the observed data together with the assumptions, not a property of the estimator. A neural network cannot learn a counterfactual contrast that the data and assumptions do not identify, and flexible modeling that reduces approximation error in a nuisance function can at the same time disguise unsupported extrapolation, because a smooth fit extends confidently into regions with no observations. The distinction is stated clearly in the methodological literature and is repeatedly elided in applied work, where a more flexible learner is offered as the answer to a confounding or positivity concern. There is no diagnostic in common use that separates a flexible model interpolating where data exist from the same model extrapolating where they do not.

title: Flexible estimation is presented as a remedy for identification failure
text:
Why it is open
Extrapolation is not visible in any conventional fit statistic: a model can have excellent cross-validated loss on the observed region and be entirely unconstrained off it. The regions that matter are conditional on a growing treatment and covariate history, so the question of whether a given prediction is supported is itself high-dimensional. The professional incentive also points one way, since the flexible estimate is the one with the tighter interval.

title: Flexible estimation is presented as a remedy for identification failure
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Feuerriegel S, Frauen D, Melnychuk V, et al. Causal machine learning for predicting treatment outcomes. Nat Med 2024;30:958-968
States that causal machine learning supports individualized effect estimation only under the same identification assumptions as conventional methods, which is the claim applied work elides.


Target trial emulation under nonmutually exclusive assignment. Am J Epidemiol 2026;195(4):1045
Demonstrates empirically that poor overlap defeats advanced adjustment, which is the concrete form the general point takes.

title: Flexible estimation is presented as a remedy for identification failure
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Require that any flexible nuisance model be paired with a support diagnostic reported for the same conditioning sets the model uses, so extrapolation is visible where it happens rather than aggregated away. Score estimators on failure awareness: whether their diagnostics correctly signal a severe positivity violation or a non-identifiable target, tested against deliberately non-identifiable simulation scenarios. Include at least one such scenario in every methods comparison, since an estimator that always returns a narrow interval is not robust if it never warns.

title: Flexible estimation is presented as a remedy for identification failure
text:
Our study






NoteA study is designed



Question. Within 236 estimand scenarios generated from 68 unique observed-data laws, does a cross-fitted flexible series AIPW workflow produce conventionally green intervals that fail to cover a prespecified compatible-truth set more often than fixed-cap longitudinal IPW or main-effects longitudinal AIPW, and how accurately does one prediction-level support map detect exact and practical support failures across linear, curved, disconnected, interaction-dependent, and longitudinally accumulated support boundaries?

title: Flexible estimation is presented as a remedy for identification failure
text:
Verification

Verdict. Partially addressed. Auditors found the problem open. At least one qualified how it is stated; the qualification and who made it are in the trail below. Moved by the full-text reading: 1 finding from 1 paper naming work that covers part of this problem survived both the reader and an independent second reviewer, so the verdict moves from confirmed-open to partially-addressed, on a single finding. A further 37 findings in the same reading restate the problem as open; the two are consistent, and the part that is covered is named above.
Dissent. literature dissented (supported): The corpus contains a growing body of flexible estimation inside emulations, including ensemble-learning marginal structural models and deep learning comparisons, and it contains no support diagnostic reported alongside a flexible nuisance model and no methods comparison that includes a deliberately non-identifiable scenario. […]
Revised by the full-text reading. Applied full-text reading of the consolidated library.

Verdict changed

confirmed-open -> partially-addressed 1 surviving finding from: Start with the Target Trial Protocol, Then Follow the Roadma. New citations: 10.1097/ede.0000000000001637


4 of the 4 independent auditors returned an opinion on this entry.

Literature and prior-art check

open / supported. The corpus contains a growing body of flexible estimation inside emulations, including ensemble-learning marginal structural models and deep learning comparisons, and it contains no support diagnostic reported alongside a flexible nuisance model and no methods comparison that includes a deliberately non-identifiable scenario. A 2026 Nature Communications paper evaluates bias across statistical and deep learning methods in a heart failure emulation, which is the comparison the entry wants and does not include a non-identifiable arm. Failure awareness as a scored property does not appear anywhere. Cites 10.1038/s41467-026-74999-6: Compares flexible against conventional estimation for bias inside an emulation, which is the nearest existing test and does not include a non-identifiable scenario.. Cites 10.1002/bimj.70133: Applies ensemble learning to the weight model in a longitudinal setting, which is where the extrapolation concern applies..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / overstated. The central identification claim is correct, although identification formally concerns the observed-data law, causal model, target estimand, and identifying assumptions rather than the realized finite dataset. Flexible estimation cannot repair failed exchangeability or positivity. The absolute diagnostic claim is too strong: propensity-score overlap, conditional treatment probabilities, density ratios, nearest-neighbor distances, leverage, and related support diagnostics can operationally flag extrapolation. They cannot certify identification, diagnose unmeasured confounding, or provide a model-free boundary between interpolation and extrapolation in high-dimensional longitudinal histories. Simulations can test warnings for deliberately detectable support failures, but no estimator can be required to detect every nonidentifiable target from the observed distribution alone. No package capability claim is present.

Grok 4.5, recency lens

open / supported-with-caveat. Inverted search did not find a standard that closes this gap. Feuerriegel et al. (Nat Med 2024) restate that causal ML requires the same identification assumptions as classical methods and does not identify contrasts the data cannot support; that is prior art for the claim, not a solution. Hill and Su (Ann Appl Stat 2013) and Nethery et al. (Ann Appl Stat 2019) give BART-centered common-support diagnostics and nonoverlap-aware estimation, and propensity-score density/trim diagnostics remain routine for low-dimensional scores. Those tools do not constitute a diagnostic in common use that flags, for a general flexible nuisance (including neural nets) and for the same high-dimensional conditioning sets the nuisance uses, which predictions are interpolation versus extrapolation. Package activity in TrialEmulation, gfoRmula, lmtp, WeightIt, and related tools still emphasizes IPW weight extremity and classical overlap plots rather than per-prediction support maps for flexible outcome models. Failure-awareness scoring against deliberately non-identifiable simulations is not an established methods-comparison standard. The problem remains open as stated for applied flexible nuisance work; the caveat is that specialized support diagnostics for some nonparametric models already exist and should be named rather than implied to be nonexistent.

GLM-5.2, third independent lens

open / supported. The claim correctly identifies that identification is a property of data and assumptions, not the estimator, and that flexible models can disguise extrapolation. The reason given for it being open (lack of common diagnostics for high-dimensional extrapolation) logically supports the claim. The claim is pitched at the right level of generality and correctly frames the issue as a current practice gap rather than a structural impossibility.

Decision path

R5:default-open → R9:substantiated-overstatement(n=1/4):codex → R17:reading-moved(confirmed-open->partially-addressed)

title: Large databases yield small effective samples after eligibility, comparator restriction and weighting
text:
Statement
A database of millions can carry very little information about a specific target trial once strict eligibility, active-comparator restriction and weighting have been applied, and extreme weights reduce the effective sample size much further than the nominal count suggests. Conventional asymptotic inference then becomes unreliable, most sharply for rare competing events and for subgroup effects, which are precisely the quantities decision-makers ask about. Papers continue to report the nominal number of patients, which for a weighted longitudinal analysis is not the quantity that governs the variance.

title: Large databases yield small effective samples after eligibility, comparator restriction and weighting
text:
Why it is open
The effective sample size is estimator-specific and time-varying in a longitudinal analysis, so there is no single number to report and no convention for which to choose. Small-sample corrections in this setting have to account for the estimated weights as well as the outcome model, and that theory is thin. There is also no incentive to report a number that shrinks a study’s apparent size by an order of magnitude.

Establish by simulation the point at which asymptotic intervals stop covering, as a function of the weight tail and the event rate, so the reporting threshold is empirical rather than conventional.

title: Large databases yield small effective samples after eligibility, comparator restriction and weighting
text:
Verification

Verdict. Confirmed open. Auditors found the problem open. At least one qualified how it is stated; the qualification and who made it are in the trail below.
Dissent. literature dissented (supported): Nothing in the corpus reports the effective sample size alongside the nominal one as a convention, nor establishes the point at which asymptotic intervals stop covering as a function of weight tail and event rate. […]
4 of the 4 independent auditors returned an opinion on this entry.

Literature and prior-art check

open / supported. Nothing in the corpus reports the effective sample size alongside the nominal one as a convention, nor establishes the point at which asymptotic intervals stop covering as a function of weight tail and event rate. Work on near-positivity violations in IPTW-estimated marginal structural survival models measures the consequence, which is the closest existing treatment, and it characterizes bias rather than supplying a reporting rule. The claim is a reporting and small-sample-inference gap rather than a missing estimator, which makes it harder to refute by finding a method paper and easier to confirm by observing practice. Cites 10.1002/bimj.70093: Quantifies the consequence of near-positivity for weighted survival estimation, which is the mechanism by which effective sample size collapses..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / supported-with-caveat. The central claim is correct. Eligibility and comparator restrictions reduce the number of relevant independent patients, while concentrated positive weights reduce the Kish effective sample size through (sum w)^2 divided by sum(w^2). Rare events and subgroup restrictions can leave little information despite a large source database. The important caveat is that a weight-only effective sample size is not the information governing every estimator. In longitudinal emulations it is time-specific and must account for risk sets, events, repeated or cloned records, within-patient dependence, estimated nuisance functions and the outcome variance. A small calculated effective sample size therefore does not automatically invalidate asymptotic inference; validity also depends on independent-cluster counts, event counts, weight-tail moments and nuisance-estimation behavior. Reporting time-specific weight concentration is useful but cannot replace at-risk counts, event counts, overlap plots and influence-function or cluster-level variance diagnostics. Exact or permutation inference is not generally available in observational data without a known assignment mechanism. Shrinkage and cross-site borrowing add assumptions and cannot repair structural positivity failure or absent outcome information. Simulation can characterize a specified design but cannot produce a universal coverage threshold. The lmtp software claim is unverified because no pinned lmtp source is vendored.

Grok 4.5, recency lens

open / supported-with-caveat. The core claim survives: after eligibility, active-comparator restriction, and inverse-probability weighting, information can collapse far below the nominal N, and papers still lead with headcount rather than information. What exists does not close the agenda item. Kish-style ESS, WeightIt::ESS, and cobalt balance tables already report weight-based effective sample size (including longitudinal MSM balance displays); Zhang, Bujkiewicz, and Jackson (BMC Medical Research Methodology 2024; 10.1186/s12874-024-02412-1) add three ESS estimators aimed at population-adjusted indirect comparison and general weighted analyses. Those are diagnostics for precision loss, not small-sample inference for estimated longitudinal weights plus outcome models, not time-varying ESS conventions for MSM/LTMLE follow-up, and not a simulation standard for when asymptotic intervals stop covering as a function of weight tails and event rates. lmtp’s modified treatment policies help keep positivity usable but do not solve ESS reporting or finite-sample theory. No 2024 to 2026 reporting guideline (TARGET 2025, HARPER, STaRT-RWE, ENCePP) was found that requires ESS alongside nominal N at each follow-up time. Searches: effective sample size inverse probability weights MSM longitudinal 2024 2025; Zhang Bujkiewicz Jackson ESS; WeightIt ESS cobalt; small sample inference IPW MSM sandwich correction; TARGET ESS reporting. Vote open because the agenda’s open parts (estimator-specific time-varying ESS convention, weight-aware small-sample theory, reporting incentive) remain; partial software and population-adjustment ESS papers are caveats, not solutions.

GLM-5.2, third independent lens

open / supported. The claim is well-constructed and proportionate. It describes a real statistical phenomenon (effective sample size collapse under weighting and restriction) and a real reporting gap (papers report nominal counts). The reason given for openness is practical and theoretical: effective sample size is estimator-specific and time-varying so there is no single number, small-sample correction theory for estimated weights is thin, and there is no incentive to report a smaller number. None of these are impossibility claims; they are claims about the absence of convention and theory. The scope is right—it does not claim all large databases are uninformative, only that they can be, and that the reporting does not reflect the information actually available.

Decision path

R5:default-open → R11:caveated(n=2)

title: Cross-validation for longitudinal nuisance models optimizes prediction, not causal performance
text: GMT-01 Partially addressed Very high priority Promising Tractability 4/5

title: Cross-validation for longitudinal nuisance models optimizes prediction, not causal performance
text:
Statement
Marginal structural models, the parametric g-formula, g-estimation and longitudinal targeted learning all identify sustained-regime effects under sequential exchangeability and positivity, and all of them require nuisance models for treatment, censoring and outcome. When those nuisance models are fitted by machine learning, the model that predicts treatment best is not the model that produces the best causal estimate: a highly adaptive learner can achieve excellent discrimination while returning near-zero treatment probabilities, poor longitudinal balance and invalid inference. Standard cross-validation selects on prediction loss and is blind to all three. No selection criterion in routine use combines treatment prediction with longitudinal balance, weight dispersion and an estimate of the influence-function remainder, and no default library is tuned for the causal objective rather than the predictive one.

title: Cross-validation for longitudinal nuisance models optimizes prediction, not causal performance
text:
Why it is open
The causal loss is not computable from the data the way a predictive loss is: the counterfactual contrast the estimator targets is never observed, so the quantity one would like to cross-validate against does not exist as a label. Balance and weight-dispersion criteria are computable but are not losses in the decision-theoretic sense and can be optimized by learners that fit poorly. Sequential double robustness is proved under conditions that do not obviously hold when the observation process in electronic health records is itself informative, so the theory that would justify a criterion is incomplete precisely where the data are hardest.

title: Cross-validation for longitudinal nuisance models optimizes prediction, not causal performance
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Robins JM, Hernán MA, Brumback B. Marginal structural models and causal inference in epidemiology. Epidemiology 2000;11(5):550-560
Introduces marginal structural models and inverse probability weighting for time-varying confounding affected by prior treatment. The nuisance models are parametric and their selection is not addressed.


Feuerriegel S, Frauen D, Melnychuk V, et al. Causal machine learning for predicting treatment outcomes. Nat Med 2024;30:958-968
Sets out what causal machine learning can and cannot do, and states that individualized effect estimation rests on the same identification assumptions as conventional methods.


ltmle: Longitudinal Targeted Maximum Likelihood Estimation. CRAN
Implements longitudinal TMLE, IPTW and g-computation, and accepts a SuperLearner library whose selection is left to the analyst.

title: Cross-validation for longitudinal nuisance models optimizes prediction, not causal performance
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Construct SuperLearner libraries whose loss combines treatment prediction with longitudinal standardized differences, weight dispersion and an estimate of the influence-function remainder, and evaluate whether that criterion selects models with lower causal bias than predictive cross-validation on the same data. Compare weighted marginal structural models, sequentially doubly robust estimators, longitudinal TMLE and Bayesian g-computation under deliberate misspecification of each nuisance component in turn. Cross-fit at the patient level rather than the record level, and report the empirical standard error ratio and convergence failures alongside bias, because an estimator that fails to converge on a fifth of replicates is not competitive at any bias.
