title: Convergence of treatment in the comparator arm attenuates the observational intention-to-treat analogue with follow-up length
text:
Verification

Verdict. Overstated. 2 independent auditors judged the claim as stated too strong. Methods for handling treatment switching exist and have been reviewed; emulations do not conventionally report initiation trajectories in both arms, so a reader cannot judge how far the contrasted strategies remained distinct over follow-up.
4 of the 4 independent auditors returned an opinion on this entry.

Literature and prior-art check

partially-solved / overstated. The entry treats comparator convergence as an unhandled feature of the observational intention-to-treat analogue. Treatment switching is a well-developed area with its own methods and its own scoping review. A 2025 Clinical Pharmacology and Therapeutics scoping review catalogs statistical methods to adjust for treatment switching in real-world studies and offers a decision framework for choosing among them. A 2026 American Journal of Epidemiology paper warns specifically about how switchers are handled in pharmacoepidemiologic effect estimation, and a 2024 BMC Medical Research Methodology paper applies g-methods to switching in the ALTA-1L trial. The entry’s implicit claim that the analyst has no options is wrong. What survives is narrower and still real: reporting the cumulative incidence of initiation in both arms is not conventional, so a reader cannot see how far the strategies stayed distinct, and no convention exists for choosing the horizon at which the contrast remains meaningful. Cites 10.1002/cpt.70013: Catalogs the available methods and supplies a framework for choosing among them, which contradicts the entry’s implication that convergence cannot be addressed.. Cites 10.1093/aje/kwaf044: Addresses the specific analytic hazard of switchers in effect estimation.. Cites 10.1186/s12874-024-02437-6: Applies g-methods to switching and examines the sensitivity of the result to specification..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

partially-solved / overstated. The valid core is that a baseline-assignment, treatment-policy analogue permits subsequent initiation, so increasing crossover can reduce exposure separation and may dilute the assignment effect. This is part of that estimand, not confounding bias to be adjusted away. However, crossover also occurs in randomized trials, so it is not uniquely observational. Convergence of current treatment status does not imply convergence of cumulative exposure histories, and attenuation toward the null with longer follow-up is not guaranteed: its direction and magnitude depend on treatment timing, effect dynamics, switching mechanisms, competing events, and the effect scale. A convergence rate alone therefore cannot determine an attenuation factor. Nor does a null estimate become categorically indistinguishable from biological inefficacy; treatment trajectories, alternative sustained or dynamic-strategy estimands, and assumption-based analyses can clarify interpretation, although they cannot identify a decomposition without additional assumptions. Existing target-trial and dynamic-strategy methods substantially address the design problem; context-specific horizon selection and adequate trajectory reporting remain unresolved practice issues. High severity is justified only when the reported estimand is mischaracterized or exposure separation is inadequate for the intended decision. Cites 10.1093/aje/kwv254: Provides the distinction between observational analogues of intention-to-treat and per-protocol effects and the corresponding design and adjustment requirements.. Cites 10.1093/ije/dyv295: Shows that later initiation and switching can be specified explicitly as dynamic strategies rather than treated as an unaddressable convergence problem..

Grok 4.5, recency lens

open / supported. Under an inverted prior, the open components of CNF-01 were treated as likely already closed by method, reporting guidance, or software; searches do not support that closure. The phenomenon itself is long recognized: observational assignment-to-initiate contrasts are confounded at baseline, and later initiation in the non-initiator arm dilutes the observational intention-to-treat (ITT) analogue as follow-up lengthens. Hernán and Hernández-Díaz (Clin Trials 2012; doi:10.1177/1740774511420743) document ITT dilution under nonadherence and argue for careful per-protocol (PP) work in comparative effectiveness. Hernán and Robins (Am J Epidemiol 2016; doi:10.1093/aje/kwv254), already cited, define observational ITT versus PP analogues and what each requires; they do not supply a reporting convention that forces cumulative initiation trajectories in both arms beside the effect estimate, nor a rule for a still-meaningful horizon. Cain et al. (Int J Epidemiol 2016; doi:10.1093/ije/dyv295), also already cited, is the main design response: name later initiation via dynamic strategies rather than an open-ended never-initiate arm. That changes the estimand; it does not identify or “debias” the attenuated ITT contrast under realistic crossover. Recent restatements keep the issue open rather than solved. Terman (Neurology 2025; doi:10.1212/WNL.0000000000214269) states that the ITT effect is typically attenuated to the degree patients switch after assignment, with a statin initiator versus noninitiator example where PP was stronger than ITT. Molero-Calafell et al. (J Clin Epidemiol 2024) restate that ITT can dilute effects when adherence differs. TARGET (Cashin et al., JAMA 2025; doi:10.1001/jama.2025.13350) is the strongest recent reporting push: it requires naming the causal contrast (assignment versus adherence), mapping strategies to data, and reporting sensitivity to design and analysis choices. From published summaries of the 21-item checklist, it does not mandate cumulative incidence of treatment initiation in both arms over follow-up as a standard diagnostic of strategy convergence, and it does not establish a horizon convention for when an initiate-now versus not-now contrast remains interpretable. STaRT-RWE, HARPER, NICE RWE framework, FDA RWE/data-source materials, ENCePP, and ICH E9(R1) improve estimand language and protocol structure generally; none close the specific CNF-01 gap that a long-horizon null observational ITT cannot be read against the convergence that produced it. Package checks (TrialEmulation, gfoRmula, lmtp, ltmle, WeightIt, MatchIt, cobalt, riskRegression, adjustedCurves, zEpid, causallib) show outcome cumulative-incidence tools and ITT/PP estimation, not a merged standard for dual-arm treatment-trajectory diagnostics or horizon-linked attenuation simulation. No 2024–2026 paper was found that (i) evaluates a field convention for publishing initiation trajectories beside the ITT estimate, (ii) defines a horizon rule for when the strategies remain distinct enough, or (iii) ships a validated simulation tool mapping observed convergence rates to expected attenuation at each horizon. Proposal and restatement are not resolution. Convergence remains a feature of the ITT strategy contrast under later initiation; PP or dynamic redesigns answer a different question. Status therefore remains open as stated. Queries run: observational ITT attenuation/dilution with later initiation and comparator crossover; target trial emulation treatment trajectories and cumulative initiation in both arms; TARGET/Cashin/Hansford reporting items on adherence and trajectories; Cain/Hernán prior art on dynamic strategies and ITT analogues; arXiv/medRxiv 2024–2026 TTE ITT crossover; CRAN/GitHub activity for TrialEmulation, gfoRmula, lmtp and related packages; FDA/EMA/NICE/ENCePP/STaRT-RWE/HARPER 2024–2026 guidance on adherence and ITT in observational emulations.

GLM-5.2, third independent lens

open / supported. The statement is internally consistent and correctly identifies a structural feature of the observational ITT analogue (convergence of strategies over time) rather than a removable bias. The reason given for the problem being open—that convergence is intrinsic to the strategy contrast, rarely reported, and lacks a convention for horizon selection—actually supports its open status. The scope is appropriate: it correctly limits the claim to the ITT analogue and acknowledges that dynamic strategies (per-protocol) are a design response, not a fix for the ITT contrast itself. The severity is proportionate because an unreported convergence can lead to a misinterpretation of a null result.

Decision path

R3:partially-solved(n=2/4) → R8:overstated-majority(n=2/4)

text: BEN-01 Overstated Very high priority Established Tractability 3/5

title: There is no theory for extrapolating successful replication of selected trials to new questions
text:
Statement
Agreement between an emulation and a randomized trial raises confidence, and disagreement can arise from emulation failure, random error, different adherence, different measurement, different populations, or a limitation of the trial itself. RCT-DUPLICATE and the 2026 concordance meta-analysis both show better agreement under closer emulation and neither shows equivalence: across 107 paired emulations and trials the effect correlation was 0.59 overall and 0.83 among the 63 pairs judged to emulate more closely. What no one has is a theory that licenses the inference from those results to a new question: how much confidence a successful replication of trial A in database D transfers to question B in database D, or to question A in database E. Publishing after the trial result is known also creates design-calibration and selective-reporting risks that the concordance statistic cannot see.

title: There is no theory for extrapolating successful replication of selected trials to new questions
text:
Why it is open
The benchmarking set is not a random sample of questions: trials get emulated when they are recent, large, and have an accessible active comparator, which are the conditions under which emulation works best. A concordance statistic is therefore an estimate of performance on a favorable subpopulation, with no design that would identify performance elsewhere. Attributing a discrepancy requires knowing which of six candidate causes produced it, and the data that would separate them, particularly the trial’s own adherence and measurement, are typically not available to the emulator.

title: There is no theory for extrapolating successful replication of selected trials to new questions
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Wang SV, Schneeweiss S, RCT-DUPLICATE Initiative. Emulation of randomized clinical trials with nonrandomized database analyses: results of 32 clinical trials. JAMA 2023;329(16):1376-1385
The largest prespecified benchmarking program: 32 trials emulated in claims data with agreement reported against the trial results.


Concordance between target trial emulation and randomised controlled trials: systematic review and meta-analysis. BMJ 2025
Pools 107 emulation-trial pairs, reporting correlation 0.59 overall and 0.83 among closer emulations, and links poorer concordance to baseline imbalance, hospital-initiated treatment and inferior outcome emulation.

title: There is no theory for extrapolating successful replication of selected trials to new questions
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Run prospective, blinded benchmarking suites in which the emulation protocol and code are frozen and registered before the trial result is revealed, which removes design calibration by construction rather than by assurance. Model concordance hierarchically by data source, clinical setting, outcome type and degree of protocol match, so the quantity estimated is a conditional expectation of agreement rather than a global rate. Treat benchmarking as calibration evidence about a data source and a design class, never as certification of a method.

title: There is no theory for extrapolating successful replication of selected trials to new questions
text:
Verification

Verdict. Overstated. 2 independent auditors judged the claim as stated too strong. A successful replication identifies calibration only for the evaluated trial, protocol, and database. Quantitative transfer to another question or database requires a prespecified target performance estimand, an explicit selection or transport model, conditional exchangeability, and overlap in relevant modifiers; outside that support, transfer is model-dependent rather than identified.
Dissent. literature dissented (supported-with-caveat): The entry proposes prospective, blinded benchmarking in which the protocol is frozen before the trial reports. That design now has at least one instance: a 2026 Circulation paper emulates a reference trial to predict the results of COBRRA before the trial’s result was available. So the proposal is not untried and the entry should say so. […]
4 of the 4 independent auditors returned an opinion on this entry.

Literature and prior-art check

partially-solved / supported-with-caveat. The entry proposes prospective, blinded benchmarking in which the protocol is frozen before the trial reports. That design now has at least one instance: a 2026 Circulation paper emulates a reference trial to predict the results of COBRRA before the trial’s result was available. So the proposal is not untried and the entry should say so. The theoretical claim survives intact: nothing licenses the inference from a successful replication in one database to a new question or a new database, and the concordance meta-analysis reports determinants of emulation success without supplying that extrapolation. One correction the entry must carry: the meta-analysis it cites has a published erratum, so any figure quoted from it needs checking against the corrected version. Supporting quotation retained here rather than as counter-evidence: [10.1136/bmj-2026-100303] Published Erratum to the concordance systematic review and meta-analysis. Any figure the entry quotes from that paper must be checked against the corrected version before publication. Cites 10.1161/circoutcomes.125.012892: A prospective emulation issued as a prediction of a trial’s result, which is the blinded benchmarking design the entry proposes as future work.. Cites 10.1136/bmj-2025-086810: Supplies the concordance estimates and their determinants across paired emulations and trials..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / overstated. The narrow identification concern is correct: performance on selected trial-database pairs does not nonparametrically identify performance for a new question or database without a defined target distribution, a sampling or selection model, conditional exchangeability of benchmark performance, and positivity over the relevant design and setting modifiers. The assertion that there is “no theory” or “no design” is too absolute. Transport and hierarchical prediction are possible under explicit assumptions, although a hierarchical model cannot identify extrapolation outside observed support merely by conditioning on study features. Correlation is also not an agreement measure: it can be high despite systematic bias and low because of restricted effect variation or sampling error. Freezing the protocol prospectively blocks outcome-informed design adaptation only if all analytic choices are locked; it does not by itself prevent selective reporting after unblinding. The problem remains open in its narrower form because the supplied agenda does not provide an identified and validated transfer procedure. Its very-high severity is warranted only when benchmarking is used to certify decisions beyond the benchmarked design class.

Grok 4.5, recency lens

partially-solved / overstated. Inverted prior favors solutions that license transfer of successful A-in-D replications to B-in-D or A-in-E. BenchExCal (Wang et al. 2025) is exactly that transfer procedure for indication expansion: benchmark an existing-indication trial in the database, then calibrate a subsequent database study for the expanded question using the observed RCT–database differences. Kirchgesner et al. (2024) state a related trial-calibration approach for questions RCTs never answered. Heyard et al. (2024) and the BMJ 2026 concordance meta-analysis already move from a global agreement rate toward design-conditional agreement (protocol match, baseline balance, outcome quality, claims vs other sources). Prospective prediction projects (GRADE, semaglutide phase IV, FDA prediction workstream) partially remove design-calibration by freezing protocols before trial readout. None of this is a completed, general statistical theory that quantifies how much confidence transfers to arbitrary new questions or databases, and BenchExCal’s empirical evaluation is still planned (simulation plus five examples), not finished. The six-cause attribution problem for single discrepancies remains open. Saying there is “no theory” is therefore too strong; the gap is the lack of a validated general theory and completed prospective hierarchical calibration, not a blank slate. Cites 10.1002/cpt.3621: Proposes an operational theory for transferring a successful existing-indication emulation (question A in database D) into a calibrated second-stage emulation for an expanded indication (question B in D), with simulation and five planned empirical evaluations. Directly addresses the report’s missing transfer step, though as proposal plus planned evaluation rather than finished validation.. Cites 10.1002/pds.70008: Articulates trial calibration as the route from benchmarked emulation of an answered question to RWE on a related unanswered question, the same transfer structure the problem says is missing.. Cites 10.1136/bmjmed-2023-000709: Models concordance variation as a function of design and population emulation differences rather than a single global rate, which is the hierarchical/conditional direction the report proposes.. Cites 10.1136/bmj-2025-086810: Estimates design-conditional concordance (closer emulation; baseline imbalance; hospital-initiated treatment; outcome emulation quality; claims data) across 107 pairs, so agreement is already treated as a conditional quantity, not only a global rate. Does not solve transfer to unselected questions..

GLM-5.2, third independent lens

open / supported. The claim is internally consistent and proportionate. It correctly identifies a structural gap: existing benchmarking provides empirical concordance on a favorable subpopulation but lacks a formal theory for extrapolating this to new questions or databases. The reasons given (non-random sampling of trials, multiple confounding causes for discrepancies) directly support why the problem remains open. The claim is appropriately scoped as a limitation of current methodological frameworks rather than an impossibility.

Decision path

R3:partially-solved(n=2/4) → R8:overstated-majority(n=2/4)

title: The method landscape
text: The catalog is organized by problem. This page is organized by method: which estimator answers which question, what each one assumes, and where each one fails. It exists so that an entry in the catalog can be read against the method it constrains.

title: The method landscape
text:
Choosing a method





flowchart TB
    A[Protocol: seven components stated] --> B{Assigned once, or sustained over time?}
    B -- Once --> C[Point-treatment estimator: IPTW, matching, standardization, AIPW, TMLE]
    B -- Sustained --> D{Is the strategy achievable at time zero?}
    D -- Yes, and eligibility is unambiguous --> E[Marginal structural model by IPTW]
    D -- Only within a window --> F[Clone, censor, weight]
    D -- The rule depends on evolving covariates --> G[Parametric g-formula, or ICE]
    D -- The rule shifts a continuous or natural value --> H[Modified treatment policy]
    E --> I{Does one person become eligible more than once?}
    F --> I
    G --> I
    H --> I
    I -- Yes --> J[Sequential nested trials, pooled with person-clustered inference]
    I -- No --> K[Single emulated trial]
    J --> L{Competing events present?}
    K --> L
    L -- Yes --> M[State the estimand first: total, controlled direct, or separable effect]
    L -- No --> N[Counterfactual risk at a stated horizon]






The branch worth noticing is the one at the bottom. A competing event is not a nuisance to be censored away; censoring at death is itself an identifying assumption, and applying it silently picks an estimand nobody stated. See OUT-01.

title: The method landscape
text:
Where the bias enters





flowchart TB
    L0[Baseline covariates] --> A0[Treatment at time 0]
    L0 --> Y[Outcome]
    A0 --> L1[Covariates at time 1]
    L1 --> A1[Treatment at time 1]
    L1 --> Y
    A0 --> Y
    A1 --> Y
    U[Unmeasured confounders] --> A0
    U --> A1
    U --> Y
    V[Visit process] --> L1
    V --> Y
    M[Phenotype algorithms] --> L0
    M --> Y
    P[Histories with no support] --> W[Weight instability and extrapolation]
    W --> Y






Read this for what it says about the three inputs no g-method touches.
L1 is the feedback loop the g-methods were built for, and they handle it. U is exchangeability, which nothing in the data can check, and which is why unmeasured confounding carries the largest evidence base in this catalog. V is the visit process: in routine records a covariate is measured when a patient attends care, so L1 is observed selectively, and the standard treatment of that is imputation rather than modeling. See MIS-01. M is that every variable in the diagram is an algorithm over billing codes and clinical text, and enters the analysis as though it were the thing it names. See MER-01.

title: The method landscape
text:
What each method identifies











Method
Setting it is stated for
Nominal estimand
Main identifying assumptions
Principal unresolved weakness




Propensity-score weighting or matching
Point treatment, new-user active comparator
Marginal contrast in the weighted or matched population
Baseline exchangeability; positivity; correct propensity model; consistency
The target population is whatever weighting produced, and is rarely stated; no protection against unmeasured confounding


Marginal structural model by IPTW
Sustained strategy with treatment-confounder feedback
Marginal contrast under each strategy
Sequential exchangeability; sequential positivity; correct treatment and censoring models; no interference
Weight instability over long follow-up; positivity failures surface as heavy weights rather than as a named unsupported region


Parametric g-formula
Sustained or dynamic strategy, discrete visits
Counterfactual risk under each strategy
Sequential exchangeability and positivity; correct models for every time-varying covariate
The null paradox: with a correctly specified but non-saturated model the sharp null can be rejected when it holds; misspecification compounds across time points


Iterated conditional expectation
The g-formula setting, long follow-up
Same
Same, except only the outcome regression at each step must be right
Fewer models than the g-formula, and no easier to check any of them


G-estimation of structural nested models
Sustained strategy, continuous or dose exposure
Effect of one additional unit or period of treatment
Sequential exchangeability; a correct model for the effect rather than for the covariates
Little software; unfamiliar output; rare in applied emulations


Clone, censor, weight
Strategies distinguishable only after time zero, grace periods
Per-protocol contrast under each strategy
Sequential exchangeability given the censoring covariates; positivity among those still uncensored
The grace period is a modeling choice that silently changes the estimand; variance after cloning has no scalable correct default


Sequential nested trials
Repeated eligibility, staggered entry
Pooled contrast across trials opened at successive times
Everything above, plus that pooling across calendar time is meaningful
One person appears in many trials; naive standard errors are wrong, and calendar-time confounding is usually unaddressed


Longitudinal targeted learning
Sustained strategy with machine-learned nuisances
The g-formula estimand
Sequential exchangeability and positivity; nuisance convergence rates; correct cross-fitting
Cross-validation optimizes prediction, not causal error; flexibility is routinely offered as a substitute for identification


Modified treatment policies
Continuous, dose or natural-value interventions
Contrast under a shift of the observed treatment
Sequential exchangeability; the shifted value stays inside the support
Support for the shifted value is exactly the positivity condition, and it is checked far less often than the shift is applied


Doubly robust AIPW and one-step estimators
Any of the above
The estimand of the estimator being augmented
Either the treatment model or the outcome model correct, plus the identification conditions
Double robustness protects against misspecification, never against unmeasured confounding or positivity failure


Negative controls, proxies, E-values
Any of the above, as a companion
A bound, a bias parameter, or a falsification test
An assumed structure relating the control to the exposure and the outcome
Each answers a different threat, none is integrated with the others, and a passing negative control is not evidence of exchangeability




This table is not a ladder. A doubly robust estimator does not cure positivity failure, a targeted estimator does not cure unmeasured confounding, cross-fitting does not cure a misspecified estimand, and a narrow confidence interval does not establish that the protocol described the trial anyone wanted. Each of those is an entry in this catalog rather than a rhetorical flourish; the summary is GMT-04, which records that no estimator is defensible as a default and that no study is required to show its choice mattered.

text:
Software
Every claim below is read from a version-pinned copy of the source under documentation/refs/packages/, not from documentation and not from memory. The versions are those pinned in documentation/audit/calibration.json, which is the standard the technical auditor is held to.




Package
Pinned
What its exports actually provide
Where it stops




TrialEmulation
CRAN 0.0.4.11
Sequential nested trials end to end: trial_sequence, expand_trials, set_switch_weight_model, set_censor_weight_model, calculate_weights, fit_msm, and case_control_sampling_trials for expansions too large to hold in memory
Robust and sandwich variance are both present, and the correct default after cloning and sequence expansion is still open (SFW-01)


gfoRmula
CRAN 1.1.1
The parametric g-formula for survival, binary and continuous end-of-follow-up outcomes, with static, threshold and simple_restriction interventions
No grace-period strategy among its exported interventions


gfoRmulaICE
CRAN 1.1.1
Iterated conditional expectation, and the one pinned package exporting grace_period directly, with "uniform" and "natural" types, alongside static, dynamic, pool and strat
Nothing in it selects the grace-period length (TZO-01)


lmtp
CRAN 1.5.4
Modified treatment policies through lmtp_tmle, lmtp_sdr, lmtp_ipw and lmtp_sub, with lmtp_survival, competing-risk indicators and incremental propensity shifts
The estimator is agnostic about whether the shifted treatment value has support


ltmle
CRAN 1.3-0, 2023
Longitudinal TMLE and ltmleMSM, with deterministic Q and g function templates
The oldest pin in the set by two years


concrete
CRAN 1.0.5
Continuous-time competing-risks TMLE
It makes the competing-event estimand estimable; it does not make the choice


CICI
CRAN 1.0
Continuous multiple-time-point interventions, and notably a feasible function alongside gformula and msm
One of the few places positivity is a first-class object rather than a diagnostic afterthought (OVL-01)


adjustedCurves
CRAN 0.11.4
Adjusted survival and cumulative incidence by AIPW, IPTW, direct standardization, matching and pseudo-values, with adjusted_rmst and formal curve comparison
Point-treatment adjustment; not a longitudinal platform


WeightIt, MatchIt, cobalt, ipw
CRAN 1.7.0, 4.7.2, 4.6.3, 1.3.0
The weighting, matching and balance-diagnostic layer everything above sits on
Balance is checked on measured covariates, which is not the assumption anyone is worried about


zEpid, causallib, lifelines, scikit-survival
PyPI 0.9.1, 0.10.0, 0.30.3, 0.28.0
The Python side: time-varying g-methods, an estimator API, and survival modeling
No Python package covers sequential nested trials the way TrialEmulation does




No package spans protocol specification, eligibility ascertainment, time-zero alignment, weight estimation, positivity accounting, competing events, measurement error and the reporting a regulator asks for. That gap is itself catalogued, under software, computation and reproducibility.

title: The method landscape
text:
How to evaluate a method
A simulation study reporting bias without naming the estimand the bias is relative to has reported nothing. In an emulation the estimand is a function of the protocol, so the protocol has to be part of the data-generating mechanism rather than of the analysis.








Metric family
Minimum metrics




Estimand recovery
Bias and relative bias against a stated counterfactual risk at a stated horizon, RMSE, sign error, and the same quantities under the sharp null


Uncertainty calibration
95% coverage, empirical to nominal standard-error ratio, type I error under the null, and coverage after cloning specifically


Positivity and support
Fraction of person-time with no support for the assigned strategy, the weight distribution, the maximum stabilized weight, and the estimate with and without truncation


Time-related bias
Sensitivity to the grace period, to the time grid, and to the alignment of eligibility, assignment and follow-up start


Structural robustness
Behavior under unmeasured confounding, under an informative visit process, and under phenotype misclassification, varied jointly rather than one at a time


Computation and reproducibility
Runtime at national-registry scale, failure rate, seed sensitivity, and whether the analysis reruns from a container




The two rows most often omitted are positivity and structural robustness, and they are the two that decide whether the estimate means anything. Varying one violated assumption at a time is its own catalogued problem (UCF-02): biases can cancel, and a one-at-a-time analysis makes that accident look like robustness.





flowchart LR
    A[State the seven protocol components] --> B[Data-generating mechanism includes the protocol]
    B --> C[Manipulate: feedback, positivity, visit process, misclassification]
    C --> D[Fit competing estimators]
    D --> E[Evaluate against the declared counterfactual risk]
    E --> F[Publish code, seeds, phenotype logic, rejected protocol versions]






The last box is the one nobody does. See SFW-03.

title: The chronology of the evidence
text:
Every finding in this catalog carries the publication year of the paper that made it, so a problem’s evidence can be read as a sequence rather than a pile. That answers three questions a pooled count cannot: has later work answered what an earlier paper left open, is a problem being closed in pieces by different groups, and is a problem simply being restated across the years with nothing happening in between.
39 problems carry at least one dated finding, drawn from a full-text reading of 564 papers published between 2006 and 2026.

The same gap, named again and again
Papers name the gaps they leave behind, in their own words. Across the corpus the same gap gets named repeatedly by authors who never cite each other, and that repetition is invisible while the gaps sit as free text under the paper that wrote them. Clustering the text does not find it, because a recurrence is a paraphrase rather than a near duplicate. So all 798 future-research gaps were read and attached to a theme instead, and the chronology falls out.
27 themes were named by three or more papers across eight or more years; 4 of those have no paper in the corpus reporting any progress at all.

title: The chronology of the evidence
A prioritized agenda
text:
The catalog lists problems. This page ranks them, in three tiers plus a list of work the field does not need. Tier 1 requires no new methodology: every item is something an analyst could do differently in the next study. Tiers 2 and 3 are research programs.
The priority field carried on each entry is weak evidence and is treated as such: 10 of the 43 entries are graded Very high and 27 High, which is under half a bit of information. The ranking below rests on three observable things instead. Whether the problem changes what the estimate means rather than how precisely it is measured. Whether any method addresses it at all, which is what the verdict records. And whether anything runnable implements it, which is checked against the version-pinned source in the method landscape.

title: A prioritized agenda
text:
Tier 1: change current practice now
These need no new theory. Every one is a convention the field could adopt in its next protocol.

Report the estimand you estimated, not the one you set out to estimate. A hazard ratio published where the design targeted a weighted per-protocol effect among the grace-period compliers is a different quantity with the same name. See EST-03.
State the grace period and the time grid before looking at the outcome, and report the estimate under at least one other choice. Both are modeling decisions that move the estimand, and neither has an outcome-blind selection procedure. See TZO-01.
Name which patient histories are unsupported, not how heavy the weights got. A weight distribution is a symptom. The decision-relevant quantity is the fraction of person-time for which the assigned strategy was never observed, and the estimate with and without it. See OVL-01.
Treat censoring at a competing event as an identifying assumption and say which estimand it selects. Censoring at death is currently applied as data cleaning, which chooses a counterfactual quantity by default rather than by argument. See OUT-01.
Separate the assumptions that can be diagnosed from those that cannot, and report them separately. An analysis that lists positivity diagnostics beside an assertion of exchangeability invites a reader to treat both as checked. See REG-02.
Do not treat the phrase target trial emulation as evidence about the analysis. The label describes a design discipline, not a discharged assumption burden, and it is currently cited as though it were the second thing. See REG-03.
Publish the phenotype logic, the weight diagnostics and the rejected protocol versions, not only the final protocol. A registration recording only what survived hides the researcher degrees of freedom it exists to constrain. See SFW-03 and PRO-03.
Report benchmarking as a calibrated comparison of estimates, not as agreed or not agreed. A binary replication label mixes estimand mismatch with random error, and it is the label that gets cited. See BEN-02.
Vary violated assumptions jointly. Confounding, measurement error and informative visits occur together; a one-at-a-time sensitivity analysis can make a cancellation accident look like robustness. See UCF-02.
Show that the estimator choice did not decide the answer. No estimator is defensible as a default, and nothing currently requires a study to demonstrate that a different one would have agreed. See GMT-04.







NoteThe one-page test



A committee-facing summary should answer nine questions. If an analysis cannot, the problem is not the statistics.
What is being estimated, on what scale, at what horizon? For whom? When is time zero, and do eligibility, assignment and the start of follow-up coincide there? What is the treatment strategy, and what grace period makes it achievable? Which variables are assumed to make treatment as good as randomized at each time point? What fraction of person-time had no support for the assigned strategy? Which variables are algorithms rather than measurements? Which assumptions were diagnosed and which were asserted? How much assumption violation changes the recommendation?

title: A prioritized agenda
text:
Tier 2: develop and validate next
Tractable programs where a first publishable contribution is within reach. Everything here is graded 4 or 5 out of 5 for tractability in the catalog.

An outcome-blind procedure for selecting the grace period and the time grid, and a reporting convention that shows the estimand moving with them
A positivity account that names unsupported histories and reports the estimate restricted to the supported region, in place of weight diagnostics
Cross-validation criteria for longitudinal nuisance models that target causal error rather than predictive error (GMT-01)
A scalable and correct default for variance after cloning and sequence expansion (SFW-01)
End-to-end propagation of phenotype misclassification through a longitudinal estimator, rather than a validation study reported beside an analysis that assumes error-free variables (MER-01)
Thresholds for data fitness that can stop a study, and a route to publishing a negative fitness assessment (DTA-01)
Semantic conformance checking for common data models, so harmonized structure is not mistaken for harmonized meaning (DTA-03)
Federated diagnostics that surface between-site estimand heterogeneity instead of averaging over it (DTA-02)
Person-clustered and calendar-time-aware inference for sequential nested trials, validated in finite samples rather than asymptotically (SEQ-01)
Bias bounds for comparator sampling schemes computable before cohort construction (ELG-03)
Verification that automated protocol translation preserves the estimand, not only that it produces running code (LRN-02)
Subgroup estimation that reports overlap per subgroup, since the groups with the worst overlap are the ones the analysis exists to serve (LRN-04)
Evaluation of generative models on causal quantities rather than on distributional fidelity (SFW-02)
A discrepancy prior for entering an emulation into a synthesis with randomized trials, calibrated on the existing benchmarking literature (EST-05)

title: A prioritized agenda
text:
Tier 3: high risk, high reward
Where the payoff is large and a clean result is not likely. These are the entries the catalog grades 2 or 3 for tractability, and the ones where the obstacle is identification rather than engineering.

Identification of dynamic regimes in continuous time under a treatment-dependent observation process, which is the ordinary situation in electronic health records and the one the discrete g-formula assumes away (GMT-02)
Interference and the joint strategies cloning can construct that no policy could implement (EST-01)
The visit process as part of the causal structure rather than as missingness to impute (MIS-01)
Negative controls, proxies and validation data integrated into one bias account instead of three separate reassurances (UCF-01)
A mediated estimand defined for a sustained strategy realized by cloning and artificial censoring, with a protocol slot that fixes the mediator before the analysis (EST-04)
Clinically defensible equivalence classes of treatment versions, which is what consistency quietly assumes (STR-01)
Inference that accounts for the target trial having been selected after seeing the data (PRO-02)
Counterfactual prediction validated outside the assumptions that produced it, with operating characteristics under exchangeability failure (LRN-05)
Regulatory thresholds for adequate emulation, acceptable residual confounding and sufficient data fitness, which is a governance problem carrying a methodological core (REG-01)
Emulation of non-pharmaceutical and policy interventions whose treatment versions are not enumerable, the one entry in the catalog the auditors could not settle (PRO-05)

title: A prioritized agenda
section: What the field does not need
text:
What the field does not need
Stated plainly, because an agenda that only adds is not an agenda. Each of these is refused for a reason recorded in the catalog or in the rejected candidates.

Another emulation demonstrating that immortal time bias exists. It is the most-restated finding in the entire reading and has been settled since 2008.
Another package reimplementing inverse probability weighting under a new function name. The gap named in the catalog is a missing default for variance after cloning, not a missing weighting routine.
Simulation studies run where every method works. Correct specification, good overlap, measured confounders and complete follow-up describe conditions under which the estimator choice cannot matter, which is the question the study was meant to answer.
Adopting a more flexible estimator in place of an identification argument. This is a catalogued error, not a research direction (LRN-01).
Papers observing that applied subfields have not adopted existing methods. Named independently by four gap labellers and rejected on assessment: the sources themselves say the methods are available in standard software and simply not used, which is a fact about diffusion rather than a gap in the field.
Requests for someone to write a package. Named independently by three labellers, rejected twice on the same ground. It closes with engineering and funding, not with research, and the methodological residue is already carried by GMT-04 and SFW-03.
Reporting checklists that stop where the disputes start. A guideline covering what to report about eligibility and time zero, and nothing about grace periods, cloning or time-varying confounding, standardizes the easy half.

title: A prioritized agenda
text:
The organizing discipline

No effect estimate without a stated estimand at a stated horizon. No time zero without eligibility, assignment and follow-up aligned at it. No sustained strategy without the grace period that makes it achievable and the positivity account that makes it estimable. No exchangeability claim without a bias analysis that says how much violation the conclusion survives.

title: Open Problems in Target Trial Emulation
text:
Target trial emulation gave observational comparative effectiveness research a discipline it lacked: state the protocol of the randomized trial you would have run, then say exactly how each component is emulated in the data you have. That discipline removed a class of self-inflicted errors. It did not remove the rest.
This site catalogs the open problems, one entry at a time. Each says what the problem is, why it stays open, what has already been tried, and the most probable route to a solution.

title: Open Problems in Target Trial Emulation
text:
Start here


Browse the catalog
Every problem in one filterable table. Sort by priority, filter by category or verdict, or search across all fields.


The prioritized agenda
What should change in practice now, what should be built next, and what is high-risk and high-reward.


The method landscape
What each approach identifies, where it breaks, and a decision path from an emulation problem to a defensible method.


How this was verified
The provenance of this material, the audit protocol, and an honest account of what the verdicts do and do not establish.

title: Open Problems in Target Trial Emulation
text:
The organizing distinction
The decisive division is between problems a complete protocol specification solves and problems that survive a perfect protocol.
Writing the protocol down is what defeats misalignment of eligibility, assignment and the start of follow-up, and with it immortal time bias. Those problems are, in principle, bookkeeping: they are caused by the analyst and fixed by the analyst. The catalog records them because applied practice still gets them wrong, not because the theory is missing.
Everything else survives. A protocol states which confounders you intend to adjust for; it cannot make them measured. It states a sustained strategy; it cannot make that strategy achievable in people whose covariate history never receives it. It names an outcome; it cannot make the phenotype algorithm that ascertains the outcome correct. Most of the hardest entries here sit on that side of the line.
Three consequences run through the whole collection.
Emulation prevents self-inflicted bias; it does not create randomization. An immaculately aligned time zero and an active-comparator new-user design remove specific, nameable errors. They leave exchangeability exactly where it was: an assumption, untestable from the data being analyzed. Covariate balance after weighting is evidence about the variables you measured and silent about the ones you did not.
Choices made before any model is fitted cannot be priced by the model. The grace period, the time grid, the lookback window, the code list defining the outcome: each is fixed before estimation, and each changes the estimand rather than merely the precision. No amount of flexibility in the nuisance models recovers a choice made upstream of them.
Agreement with a randomized trial is calibration evidence, not certification. When an emulation and its index trial disagree, the candidates are residual confounding, a different population, differently measured exposure or outcome, a different estimand, and chance. Nothing in the current toolkit separates them for the single study in front of a decision maker.

title: Open Problems in Target Trial Emulation
text:
Reading a verdict
Every entry carries a verdict recording what happened when its claims were checked against the literature and against independent external auditors. A verdict of Overstated does not mean the problem is not real; it usually means the underlying issue is real and a claim about its severity was pitched too strongly. Entries marked Resolved since report are kept rather than deleted, because knowing that something was recently closed is as useful as knowing it is open.
The source material for this catalog was produced by a large language model and then audited. How this was verified explains what that means in practice, including where the audit’s own limits are.

title: How this was verified
text:
This catalog is derived from a deep-research document produced by a large language model (ChatGPT deep research) in July 2026, covering open methodological, theoretical, practical, data-related and interpretive problems in target trial emulation.
That origin is the reason this page exists. A machine-generated research agenda is a plausible-sounding artifact whether or not it is correct, and publishing one as settled fact would be a disservice. Nothing from the source document appears on this site without a verification verdict attached, and the evidence behind each verdict is shown on the entry itself.
The source document is kept as working material and is not published here.


The source was supplied in three formats. The markdown export had lost every citation. ChatGPT’s markdown export replaces each link with private-use-area characters and an opaque handle, so the exported file contained 125 citation tokens, zero DOIs, zero URLs, and zero PubMed identifiers. The .docx of the same document retained the real hyperlinks.
Extraction therefore runs from the .docx, not the export. That distinction is not cosmetic: had the markdown been used, every entry in this catalog would have been unsourced, and the audit would have had nothing to check a citation against.

text:
What was checked mechanically
Before any of the substantive audit, every resolvable identifier in the source was checked against its registry.
The source carries 48 numbered references pointing at 35 distinct works.

title: How this was verified
text:
The audit
Every problem was assessed as a whole statement rather than decomposed into atomic claims, because the statements are written to be falsifiable in one piece: each names a specific thing that does not exist. Four auditors assessed each entry independently, and each returned two votes, one on whether the problem is still open and one on whether the claim as written is faithful and proportionate, together with the weakest version of the claim they would still defend. Those weakest restatements are what the published statement was rewritten to.

Literature verification
For each problem, every cited work was checked to confirm it supports the claim attributed to it, and the screened corpus on this site was searched for later work that would resolve or narrow the problem. The search ran against the 1,376 records held locally rather than against recall, so every locator in a verification opinion is a record that exists in the collection and can be opened. Where the search found nothing, the opinion says so and its confidence is capped, because absence from one corpus of PubMed and PMC records is weak evidence of absence in the field.


Citation resolution
Every citation in the catalog is resolved mechanically. Of 117 cited works, 96 carry a DOI: each is resolved against CrossRef and the cited surname and year are compared with the record it returns, because the failure that matters here is misattribution rather than fabrication. A real DOI under a plausible name reads as sound to everything downstream. 0 disagree on an author or a year, 0 fail to resolve, and 0 works are cited with two different years in different entries.
The remaining 21 cite regulatory guidance, a package page or a preprint, none of which carries a DOI. Those are checked by asking for them: 9 of 9 distinct locators answer. A cited preprint is also checked for a journal version, since citing one is correct until it is published and then stops being correct without any link breaking; 0 of 2 currently need moving.
The fault being looked for is misattribution, not fabrication. An entry can credit a real paper to the wrong group, and nothing downstream notices: the DOI resolves, the paper exists, and the work described is real. Only the names and the year are wrong. The check runs from build/lit/check_citations.py and its full output is in the repository.


Adversarial refutation
The adversarial lens is one of the independent auditors rather than a separate pass. It is given an inverted prior: assume the problem has already been solved, and go find who solved it. Asking a model to confirm a claim and asking it to break the claim produce different results, and only the second is informative.
The sibling project this pipeline was ported from declares a separate refuting auditor in its adjudication rule that casts no opinions, which leaves one guard in that rule permanently inert. Rather than reproduce a lens that is named and does not run, the roster here names only auditors that vote, and the rule counts only those.


Independent external auditors
Frontier models outside this system were given the same claims, blind to each other and to the literature pass, each with a different lens:

a technical and source-code lens, which checks identification arguments, weight algebra, cloning and censoring bookkeeping, and immortal-time accounting, and which verifies any claim about a software package against that package’s pinned source rather than against the report;
a recency and prior-art lens, which adopts an inverted prior. It assumes each problem has already been solved and goes looking for who solved it, because an agenda that lists a solved problem as open is the most damaging error this site can make: the people most likely to read it are the people who solved it;
a third independent lens on the same claims, so that a majority is a majority of more than two.

Each entry’s page lists the auditors that voted on it. Coverage is not uniform. External models run out of quota mid-run, and one of them intermittently returns a well-formed but empty verdict for a batch, answering in about a hundred tokens where a real assessment takes several thousand. Those batches are detected and re-run rather than counted as complete, and the ones that stay empty after a re-run leave the entry adjudicated by fewer auditors. Where that happened the page says so, rather than presenting a thinner audit as an equal one, and every majority rule is taken over the auditors that actually voted on that entry.


Adjudication
Opinions become a published verdict by a fixed rule, not by judgment. The rule records its own decision path on every entry, so the route from votes to verdict is visible.
Two principles govern it:
A “solved” vote without a locator is not evidence. It is downgraded rather than counted. An auditor asserting that something has been solved must name the work that solved it.
Evidence beats votes. A lone dissenter holding an unrebutted verbatim quote is not silently outvoted by auditors holding opinions.
Majority rules carry a denominator. A verdict such as Overstated requires at least two independent auditors and at least half of the auditors that actually returned an opinion on that entry. Using the roster size as the denominator would let an entry reached by two auditors be decided on the same evidence as one reached by four.

title: How this was verified
section: Which fields are audited, and which are editorial
text:
Which fields are audited, and which are editorial
This distinction matters and is easy to lose.
Audited. The statement, why it is open, the prior work, and the extracted claims. These went through literature verification, adversarial refutation and the independent auditors, and they carry the verdict.
Editorial. Maturity, tractability, severity, the proposed research direction, and the protocol-component and data-setting tags. These are one reader’s judgment applied to make the catalog browsable. They were not audited and should not be cited as findings. The proposed direction in particular reads with the same visual authority as the audited statement above it, and it is a research suggestion rather than a verified claim.
Deliberately rebuilt. Priority is not carried over from the source. It reflects three observable things: whether the problem blocks a decision-grade estimand, whether any method addresses it at all, and whether any software implements it.

title: How this was verified
section: What the verdicts do not mean
text:
What the verdicts do not mean
A verdict is a judgment about a claim, not about a problem’s importance.
Overstated almost never means the problem is fictional. It usually means the underlying difficulty is real and the source pitched its severity, or the claim that no method exists, more strongly than the evidence supports. The entry records the strongest version of the claim that survived.
Confirmed open is a verdict about status and only about status: the auditors that returned an opinion found the problem unsolved, and no substantiated resolving work was produced. It does not mean they were unanimous about the wording. Almost every entry carrying this badge also carries a qualification from at least one auditor, because the rule that leaves a claim intact and the rule that flags it as too strong feed the same status. The qualification is on the entry, in the verification trail, and the decision path names the rule that produced the verdict. It also does not mean nobody is working on the problem, and it is a statement about the literature that was reachable, not about the literature that exists.
Unverifiable means the auditors disagreed with evidence on both sides, or that no accessible source could settle it. The disagreement is shown on the entry rather than resolved silently.

title: How this was verified
text:
Limits of this exercise
This is not a systematic review. There was no protocol registration, no duplicate independent screening with a reported agreement statistic, and no formal risk-of-bias assessment.
The literature harvest covers PubMed and PubMed Central only. Conference abstracts and journals indexed in Embase but not PubMed are missing. Embase has no API available without a subscription.
The auditors are language models. They are better at finding a paper that closes a gap than at proving no such paper exists, so Confirmed open carries less weight than Resolved since report. A confirmed absence of evidence is the weakest thing on this site.

title: How this was verified
text:
Reproducing this
Everything is in the repository. build/render_site.mjs turns the registry into these pages, build/make_audit_batches.mjs produces the auditor prompts, and build/adjudicate.mjs applies the rule. documentation/audit/calibration.json holds known-answer cases verified by hand; any audit configuration that fails to reproduce them is miscalibrated, and they are asserted before the site is built.

title: Studies
text:
The catalog records what is open. This is the attempt to close some of it: one study a week, each aimed at a single entry, taken in priority order.
Scope is target trial emulation only: the specification of an emulated protocol, the g-methods used to estimate the effects of sustained treatment strategies, and the benchmarking of emulations against the trials they emulate. A problem that would be the same problem in any observational analysis is out of scope, because it is not what this catalog is about.

title: Studies
text:
Completed

BEN-02: A binary replication label changes with precision alone, and one operator carries almost all of it
Question. BEN-02 says replication is reported as a binary label that mixes estimand mismatch with random error. Holding the true trial-emulation discrepancy fixed, how much of the label is decided by precision rather than by the discrepancy, and which of the operators in use carries that sensitivity?
Answer. For the operators tested, yes, and it is concentrated in one of them. The sensitivity S is the larger of the two operator-specific values at 0.4915, against a threshold of 0.10 declared before the run, with a 95 percent Monte Carlo interval of 0.4903 to 0.4931; the lower endpoint clears the threshold by roughly 538 Monte Carlo standard errors. Confidence-interval overlap supplies that value; direction agreement moves by 0.1244 over the same range. Two benchmark pairs carrying the same true discrepancy can therefore be labeled agreeing and disagreeing on the strength of how precisely each was estimated, and the operator most used to produce the label is the most exposed.
What it does not answer. S is the maximum over the operators tested, so the result is an at-least-one-operator claim: it establishes that interval overlap is materially precision-sensitive and that direction agreement is less so, not that every binary replication label is. It holds for these two illustrative operators, these 16 fixed scenarios and these three nested precision levels. This is the pair-level component of BEN-02 and not the entry as a whole: it says nothing about between-pair heterogeneity across a benchmarking program, about calibration of a graded metric against a decision, or about the graded alternatives the entry’s own audit established already exist, all three of which the design review named as out of scope and which are declared limitations rather than results. Outcomes are binary at a single horizon, so the behavior of these operators on a time-to-event scale is untouched.
Read it: PDF · Markdown · OpenDocument


CNF-01: A single cumulative-initiation number at the horizon does not determine the attenuation it is asked to explain
Question. CNF-01 asks authors to publish the cumulative incidence of initiation in both arms so a reader can see how far the contrasted strategies stayed distinct, and to quantify by simulation how much attenuation a given convergence rate produces. Does that diagnostic actually recover the attenuation?
Answer. No. Within the simulated grid, comparator-arm cumulative initiation at 120 months does not uniquely determine attenuation: matched early and late initiation scenarios, whose reported diagnostic agrees to within 0.0005, differ in attenuation by 0.0528 to 0.2027. Nine of the twelve matched pairs exceed the 0.05 threshold declared before the run by at least three Monte Carlo standard errors, at 5 to 46 of them; the other three sit within 3 and are individually inconclusive, and all three are at the lowest convergence rate, where there is least attenuation to misattribute. A single cumulative-incidence value at the horizon is therefore insufficient for recovering attenuation in these scenarios. What the reported number cannot see is when the comparator arm initiated and who initiated.
What it does not answer. The comparison holds the diagnostic fixed only at 120 months. At earlier horizons the early and late scenarios differ in observed cumulative initiation by as much as 0.269, so those contrasts are not comparisons at equal C(h) and cannot independently establish insufficiency there. The study establishes that C(120) alone is insufficient within this grid. It does not establish that reporting C is necessary, that the full initiation curve would be sufficient, or that a universal conversion from convergence to attenuation exists. The comparator arm converges upward and the treated arm never discontinues, so this is one direction of convergence only. There is no loss to follow-up and no competing event, both excluded so the attenuation is not confounded with a second mechanism. The scale is the risk difference throughout; a hazard ratio would mix this mechanism with non-collapsibility.
Read it: PDF · Markdown · OpenDocument


PRO-02: A recorded, effect-blind search over highly correlated protocols leaves naive intervals close to nominal on average, and undercovering when the candidates disagree
Question. PRO-02 says inference conditions on a fixed target trial that was in fact selected after seeing the data. When the search is recorded and the selector is blind to the treatment effect, choosing among 4 or 16 candidate protocols by outcome counts or covariate-outcome associations, how much coverage do naive 95% intervals for the selected protocol lose, and what do Bonferroni correction and sample splitting cost?
Answer. Not materially, within this design. The global deficit D_all was 0.0015 (simultaneous 95% Monte Carlo interval -0.0001 to 0.0030) and D_nonboundary 0.0023 (0.0004 to 0.0042), both upper limits far below the registered 0.02 threshold; all 360 fixed-candidate evaluations passed the calibration gate. The nonboundary deficit is detectably above zero, but it is about a fifth of a percentage point. Averaged over replicates, a recorded, effect-blind choice among these protocols costs naive intervals almost nothing.
What it does not answer. The conclusion covers deterministic recorded searches over nested age thresholds and outcome horizons, libraries of 4 or 16 highly correlated candidates, treatment-effect-blind selectors, and correctly specified inverse probability weighting. It does not cover undocumented or sequential protocol development by an analyst who has seen results, other protocol components such as grace periods or treatment definitions, libraries of weakly correlated protocols, or misspecified weights. The replication’s calibration gate controls false failure across 360 comparisons and in exchange would pass a candidate miscalibrated by less than about two percentage points.
Read it: PDF · Markdown · OpenDocument

title: Studies
section: What each study has to do
text:
What each study has to do
Simulation studies follow ADEMP: aims, data-generating mechanisms, estimands, methods, performance measures (Morris, White and Crowther 2019). Two rules follow from it and are enforced rather than encouraged.

Every performance measure carries a Monte Carlo standard error.

A bias of 0.02 is uninterpretable without knowing whether the Monte Carlo error is 0.001 or 0.03. The replicate count is derived in the protocol from a target Monte Carlo standard error, not chosen because it is a round number.

Failed replicates are results.

A method that converges on 60% of replicates and is unbiased on those is not an unbiased method. Convergence is reported for every method in every scenario.

The protocol is committed before the run.

It fixes the design and states in advance what result would count as showing the problem is real and what would count as showing it is not. The commit that adds it is the timestamp.


Code, protocols and results are at github.com/choxos/TTE-open-problems/tree/main/studies.

title: Replication is reported as a binary label rather than as a calibrated comparison of estimands
text: BEN-02 Overstated High priority Established Tractability 5/5

title: Replication is reported as a binary label rather than as a calibrated comparison of estimands
text:
Statement
Agreement between an emulation and a trial is informative only when the estimands, populations and measurements are close enough to be comparable, and better design alignment is empirically associated with stronger concordance. Benchmarking nonetheless reports success or failure as a binary label, usually derived from whether the confidence intervals overlap or whether the direction agrees. That label mixes estimand mismatch with random error: two studies estimating the same quantity with wide intervals will agree by that criterion, and two estimating different quantities precisely will disagree. The reported statistic therefore does not measure what its users take it to measure.

title: Replication is reported as a binary label rather than as a calibrated comparison of estimands
text:
Why it is open
Constructing a graded measure requires deciding how much estimand difference is tolerable, which is a judgment the binary label exists to avoid. Prediction-interval coverage would be the natural criterion and requires a distributional claim about the trial’s own error that the trial does not publish. The label is also convenient for the audiences who cite benchmarking results, so there is little pressure to replace it.

title: Replication is reported as a binary label rather than as a calibrated comparison of estimands
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Wang SV, Schneeweiss S, RCT-DUPLICATE Initiative. Emulation of randomized clinical trials with nonrandomized database analyses: results of 32 clinical trials. JAMA 2023;329(16):1376-1385
Reports agreement across 32 prespecified emulations using several agreement metrics, which is the most careful existing treatment of the labeling question.


Concordance between target trial emulation and randomised controlled trials: systematic review and meta-analysis. BMJ 2025
Reports effect correlation and standardized-difference agreement across 107 pairs and relates concordance to specific design features rather than to a pass or fail label.

title: Replication is reported as a binary label rather than as a calibrated comparison of estimands
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Report the ratio of effects, the absolute effect difference, standardized agreement and prediction-interval coverage together, so that estimand mismatch and random error are separately visible. Use positive and negative controls alongside the trial comparison, and prefer prospective forecasts of a trial’s result to retrospective comparisons, since only the former is uncontaminated by knowing the answer. Replicate across databases as well as across questions, because a data source’s calibration is what a decision-maker actually needs to know.

The sensitivity S is the larger of the two operator-specific values at 0.4915, against a threshold of 0.10 declared before the run, with a 95 percent Monte Carlo interval of 0.4903 to 0.4931; the lower endpoint clears the threshold by roughly 538 Monte Carlo standard errors. Confidence-interval overlap supplies that value; direction agreement moves by 0.1244 over the same range. Two benchmark pairs carrying the same true discrepancy can therefore be labeled agreeing and disagreeing on the strength of how precisely each was estimated, and the operator most used to produce the label is the most exposed.
Results.

The label moves with precision at fixed truth. Holding the true risk-difference discrepancy constant and varying only trial and emulation precision moves the probability of an agreement verdict by 0.49 on the interval-overlap operator, against a threshold of 0.10 set in the protocol before any result existed.
The exposure is not shared evenly. Direction agreement moves by 0.1244 over the same range, a quarter of the interval-overlap figure. An operator choice that is usually made for convenience decides most of the conflation.
It is not an estimation artifact. Coverage runs 0.944 to 0.956 against a nominal 0.95, maximum absolute bias is 0.00086, convergence is complete in every scenario, and the exact finite-cell summation used for truth agrees with itself to 2.2e-16. Nothing here is an estimator failing.
The bootstrap interval is narrow enough to matter. The Monte Carlo interval on S spans 0.0028, so the distance from the 0.10 threshold is not a Monte Carlo question.

Design.

Estimand

The probability that a pair-level agreement operator returns agreement, as a function of precision at a fixed true discrepancy, and the sensitivity S of that probability to precision alone

Methods compared

direction agreement, confidence-interval overlap, forced plug-in tolerance classifier, three-way joint-uncertainty tolerance procedure, graded normal-compatibility score, sceptical p-value

Data-generating mechanism

16 structural scenarios crossing the true risk-difference discrepancy with trial and emulation precision, 10,000 replicates each, 480,000 benchmark pairs. Each replicate is one trial cohort and one emulation cohort with a binary outcome, scored by four agreement operators in current use. Truth is enumerated by exact summation over the covariate strata rather than by simulation, so the discrepancy each scenario carries is known to machine precision.

Replicates

10,000 per scenario, 480,000 pairs, 0 replicate errors


What this does not answer. S is the maximum over the operators tested, so the result is an at-least-one-operator claim: it establishes that interval overlap is materially precision-sensitive and that direction agreement is less so, not that every binary replication label is. It holds for these two illustrative operators, these 16 fixed scenarios and these three nested precision levels. This is the pair-level component of BEN-02 and not the entry as a whole: it says nothing about between-pair heterogeneity across a benchmarking program, about calibration of a graded metric against a decision, or about the graded alternatives the entry’s own audit established already exist, all three of which the design review named as out of scope and which are declared limitations rather than results. Outcomes are binary at a single horizon, so the behavior of these operators on a time-to-event scale is untouched.

title: Replication is reported as a binary label rather than as a calibrated comparison of estimands
text:
Verification

Verdict. Overstated. 2 independent auditors judged the claim as stated too strong. Binary replication labels based on interval overlap or effect direction discard magnitude and uncertainty and cannot diagnose why estimates differ. Decision-grade benchmarking should first align estimands, then report paired contrasts with joint uncertainty, heterogeneity, and prespecified tolerances whenever a categorical judgment is required.
Dissent. literature dissented (open): The entry criticizes binary replication labels. The concordance meta-analysis it draws on does not use one: it reports correlation and standardized-difference agreement and relates them to design features, which is the graded reporting the entry asks for. RCT-DUPLICATE similarly reports several agreement metrics. […]
4 of the 4 independent auditors returned an opinion on this entry.

Literature and prior-art check

open / supported-with-caveat. The entry criticizes binary replication labels. The concordance meta-analysis it draws on does not use one: it reports correlation and standardized-difference agreement and relates them to design features, which is the graded reporting the entry asks for. RCT-DUPLICATE similarly reports several agreement metrics. So the criticism lands on the citing practice rather than on the benchmarking literature, and the entry should say that. The part that survives is that a graded criterion still does not separate estimand mismatch from random error, since prediction-interval coverage requires a distributional claim about the trial’s own error that trials do not publish. Cites 10.1001/jama.2023.4221: Reports multiple agreement metrics rather than a single binary label.. Cites 10.1136/bmj-2025-086810: Reports correlation and standardized agreement and relates both to design features, which is graded rather than binary..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

partially-solved / overstated. The criticism of confidence-interval overlap and sign agreement is technically sound, but the problem is framed too broadly. The agenda’s own descriptions say that the cited benchmarks already report several graded metrics, including effect correlation and standardized differences, so benchmarking is not uniformly binary. Continuous effect differences, ratios, and standardized contrasts still cannot separate estimand mismatch from random error. That separation first requires commensurate estimands and then a joint sampling model incorporating uncertainty from both estimates, their covariance when applicable, and between-pair heterogeneity. Prediction-interval coverage does not require a trial to publish a full error distribution when an estimate and standard error or confidence interval are available, and coverage is itself calibrated across a suite rather than diagnosed from one pair. Ratios are additionally unstable when the reference effect is near zero. This is therefore partly an implementation and reporting problem with existing tools, not wholly an unresolved statistical-method problem; high severity is disproportionate unless the binary label is the sole basis for a decision. Cites 10.1001/jama.2023.4221: As characterized in the batch, this program reports several agreement metrics rather than only a binary replication label, partially resolving the reporting problem while not separating all sources of discrepancy.. Cites 10.1136/bmj-2025-086810: As characterized in the batch, this analysis reports effect correlation and standardized-difference agreement across pairs and evaluates design-related variation, partially addressing graded comparison..

Grok 4.5, recency lens

partially-solved / overstated. The claim that benchmarking “nonetheless reports success or failure as a binary label” is not faithful to the field’s primary programs or to the report’s own cited works. RCT-DUPLICATE and Franklin-line methods report regulatory/significance agreement, estimate agreement, and standardized-difference agreement together; the BMJ 2026 meta-analysis leads with Pearson correlation, ICC, ratio of ratios, standardized-difference agreement, and Bland–Altman, and only secondarily with binary metrics. Köppe, Micheloud, Erdmann, Heyard, and Held (2025) go further: they replace the two-trials (regulatory agreement) rule with the graded sceptical p-value, which uses both p-values, effect sizes, and relative precision, and invert it to combined confidence intervals; they apply it to 29 RCT-DUPLICATE pairs. ISPOR Europe 2024 also floated enhanced multi-metric RCT–RWE agreement assessments for HTA. What remains open is universal adoption, explicit estimand alignment (how much estimand difference is tolerable), and routine prediction-interval coverage that treats trial sampling error as a distribution. Binary labels are still convenient for secondary citation and still appear beside continuous metrics, but they are not the sole or best existing practice. The report’s proposed direction (ratio of effects, absolute difference, standardized agreement, prediction-interval coverage, prospective forecasts) is largely what the better literature already does or is building. Cites 10.1001/jama.2023.4221: Already reports multiple agreement metrics (not a single pass/fail label) across 32 prespecified emulations; this is the report’s own cited “most careful existing treatment of the labeling question.”. Cites 10.1136/bmj-2025-086810: Primary reporting is continuous and multi-metric (correlation 0.59/0.83, ratio of ratios, standardized-difference rates, design-feature regressions), not a binary success label. Directly undercuts the claim that benchmarking only reports binary agreement.. Cites arxiv:2412.09334: Supplies a graded, calibrated alternative to binary two-trials/regulatory agreement (the sceptical p-value), depending on both p-values, effect sizes, and relative precision; extends to non-inferiority and inverted CIs; applied to RCT-DUPLICATE. Partially delivers the report’s call for calibrated comparison rather than a binary label.. Cites 10.1186/s12874-025-02589-z: Peer-reviewed publication of the sceptical p-value application to RWE emulations (same work as arXiv 2412.09334), confirming the graded metric is in the methods literature, not only a preprint..

GLM-5.2, third independent lens

open / supported. The claim is internally consistent and proportionate. It accurately characterizes a limitation in current practice: benchmarking often relies on binary labels (e.g., CI overlap) that conflate estimand mismatch with random error. The stated reasons for it being open (the difficulty of defining tolerable estimand differences and the convenience of binary labels) logically support the persistence of this practice. The claim is appropriately scoped as a critique of current reporting standards rather than an impossibility claim.

Decision path

R3:partially-solved(n=2/4) → R8:overstated-majority(n=2/4)
