title: Data-fitness assessment is narrative and has no thresholds that would stop a study
text: DTA-01 Overstated Very high priority Emerging Tractability 4/5

title: Data-fitness assessment is narrative and has no thresholds that would stop a study
text:
Statement
Electronic health records arise from encounters, billing and documentation rather than from scheduled research assessments, so eligibility and follow-up in an emulation partly reflect care-seeking and access rather than the biology the protocol intends. Whether a given database can support a given target trial is therefore a question about the data source and the trial jointly. In practice this is answered narratively, in a paragraph asserting that the data are suitable, with no quantitative thresholds and no procedure that could return the answer no. A pipeline that cannot conclude that the trial is not emulable will always produce an estimate, and the estimate will not carry the fact that the question could not be asked.

title: Data-fitness assessment is narrative and has no thresholds that would stop a study
text:
Why it is open
Fitness is not a property of the data alone but of the pair formed by the data and the protocol, so a fixed score is the wrong object and a per-protocol assessment has to be constructed each time. Any threshold that would stop a study is a threshold that costs someone a publication, and no external body currently imposes one. There is also a measurement problem underneath: assessing capture continuity or outcome validity generally requires a validation source, and if that source existed the fitness question would be less pressing.

title: Data-fitness assessment is narrative and has no thresholds that would stop a study
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Wang, et al. An operational target trial emulation framework for causal inference using electronic health records. npj Digit Med 2026
Sets out the operational constraints electronic health records place on each protocol component, which is the raw material a fitness score would formalize.


NICE real-world evidence framework
States that some target trials cannot be adequately emulated with available data and that bespoke data collection may be preferable, which is the design-failure outcome this problem wants to make operational.

title: Data-fitness assessment is narrative and has no thresholds that would stop a study
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Build trial-component fitness scores for observability, temporal precision, capture continuity, comparator support, outcome validity and linkage completeness, each computed against the specific protocol rather than the database in the abstract. Predefine stop rules that trigger when an essential component fails, and publish the fitness report whether or not the study proceeds, so that a negative fitness assessment is a citable result rather than a private decision. Validate the scores against benchmarking data by checking whether low fitness predicts poor concordance with the corresponding trial.

title: Data-fitness assessment is narrative and has no thresholds that would stop a study
text:
Verification

Verdict. Overstated. 2 independent auditors judged the claim as stated too strong. Many target-trial emulations lack prespecified, protocol-specific quantitative adequacy criteria and no-go rules. Transparent component-level assessments could improve decisions about whether to proceed, but thresholds must be estimand- and decision-specific, and randomized-trial concordance alone cannot validate them.
Dissent. literature dissented (supported-with-caveat): The entry says data-fitness assessment is narrative with no quantitative thresholds. A 2026 JAMIA Open paper assesses the quality of electronic health record data and linked claims data specifically for target trial emulation studies, which is a quantitative fitness assessment for this purpose and not a narrative one. […]
4 of the 4 independent auditors returned an opinion on this entry.

Literature and prior-art check

partially-solved / supported-with-caveat. The entry says data-fitness assessment is narrative with no quantitative thresholds. A 2026 JAMIA Open paper assesses the quality of electronic health record data and linked claims data specifically for target trial emulation studies, which is a quantitative fitness assessment for this purpose and not a narrative one. Regulatory syntheses for GLP-1 therapies and oncology reviews also set out data-adequacy considerations. What none supplies is the predefined stop rule the entry asks for, or the publication of a negative fitness assessment as a citable result, so the operational half of the claim stands and the descriptive half is too strong. Cites 10.1093/jamiaopen/ooag102: Assesses data quality for the emulation purpose specifically, which is the fitness assessment the entry says does not exist quantitatively.. Cites 10.7326/annals-26-00202: Sets out data-adequacy considerations for a high-stakes therapeutic area where emulation is being used for decisions..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / overstated. The residual problem is real: data fitness is specific to the protocol, estimand, and decision context, and prespecified component-level no-go criteria would improve study governance. The statement nevertheless overstates the absence of quantitative assessment. Availability, temporal resolution, treatment support, follow-up continuity, outcome capture, and validation performance can all be measured, although they do not collapse into a universally valid score. External validation data are not required for every fitness component. A pipeline without explicit stop rules also does not necessarily always return an estimate, while an estimator’s standard error generally will not represent bias from nonidentification or poor measurement. Benchmark concordance cannot by itself validate a fitness score because disagreement can arise from estimand differences, transportability, adherence, measurement, or bias in either study. This is decision-critical when an essential protocol component is unobservable or unsupported; otherwise, standardized scoring and publication of assessments are primarily governance and reproducibility improvements.

Grok 4.5, recency lens

partially-solved / overstated. Inverted-prior search finds substantial prior art that already structures protocol-paired data fitness and can return no, so the claim that fitness is only a narrative paragraph with no thresholds and no procedure that can stop a study is overstated. SPIFD (2021) and SPIFD2 (2023) are step-by-step feasibility frameworks that pair research question, target-trial articulation, and data-source selection, with component-level documentation and heatmaps intended to support go or no-go decisions before estimation. The CARE oncology work (Levy et al., 2026) runs a systematic multi-stage fitness screen over six commercial EHR sources and 23 candidate RCTs: of 54 RCT-RWD combinations, nine reached detailed feasibility and only three were selected for emulation protocol development, with explicit fitness constraints (complex eligibility, biomarkers, performance status, outcome ascertainment). OHDSI DataQualityDashboard implements quantitative pass/fail thresholds on CDM conformance, and DARWIN EU study phases include a feasibility assessment that issues a recommendation on whether to conduct the study. Lee et al. (2026) quantifies TTE-relevant completeness, accuracy, plausibility, and concordance for an EHR cohort against Medicare claims, and Wang et al. (2026) formalizes when EHR realization of trial components can or cannot yield interpretable estimates. What remains open is exactly the hard part of the proposed agenda: field-standard, protocol-component fitness scores with pre-specified stop rules that academic pipelines cannot bypass; routine publication of negative fitness assessments as citable results; and empirical validation that low fitness predicts poor concordance with the corresponding trial. Regulatory and industry pathways already gate more often than the report implies; general-purpose TTE software (TrialEmulation and related packages) still does not enforce a fitness gate that returns no. Cites 10.1002/cpt.70310: Demonstrates a systematic multi-stage, protocol-paired fitness assessment that rates RCT design elements for availability, missingness, and validity and that stops most candidate emulations: 54 RCT-RWD combinations narrowed to nine detailed assessments and three selected for protocol development.. Cites 10.1002/cpt.2883: Provides a structured, documentable process that pairs target-trial articulation with data-source fitness assessment and is intended to identify when design and data are not decision-grade before estimation proceeds.. Cites 10.1093/jamia/ocab132: Implements quantitative data-quality checks with configurable decision thresholds (OHDSI DataQualityDashboard) that can return pass or fail; covers CDM structural and value-level quality rather than full protocol-component TTE fitness, but disproves the claim that no thresholded procedure exists.. Cites 10.64898/2025.12.22.25342844: Quantifies TTE-relevant data quality (completeness, accuracy, plausibility, concordance) for eligibility, exposure, covariates, outcomes, and follow-up in EHR-only versus claims-linked data; shows a quantitative fitness evaluation against a reference source, while still requiring that external validation source..

GLM-5.2, third independent lens

open / supported. The claim is internally consistent and proportionate. It correctly frames data fitness as a joint property of the data source and the protocol, rather than the data alone. The assertion that current practice is narrative and lacks stop rules is a claim about current practice rather than a structural impossibility, and the reasons given for it being open (fitness is a pair property, thresholds cost publications, validation sources are rare) logically support the claim’s openness.

Decision path

R3:partially-solved(n=2/4) → R8:overstated-majority(n=2/4)

text: DTA-03 Partially addressed High priority Promising Tractability 4/5

title: Common data models harmonize structure without guaranteeing that the same variable means the same thing
text:
Statement
Claims, records, registries, mortality files and laboratory data each carry part of what a protocol needs, and linking them changes both who is eligible and which outcomes are captured. Linkage is imperfect and coding systems change over time, so the same analytic variable can shift meaning across sites and across years within a site. Multi-source linked databases are associated with better emulation of trials, which makes the linkage decisions consequential rather than administrative. Common data models solve the structural half of this and do not guarantee semantic or causal equivalence, and the historical code mappings and extract versions that would let a reader check are rarely preserved in publications.

title: Common data models harmonize structure without guaranteeing that the same variable means the same thing
text:
Why it is open
Semantic drift is invisible in the analytic dataset: the column is populated and the values are in range. Detecting it requires the mapping history and a comparison across extracts, both of which are usually discarded once the analytic file is built. Linkage error is also non-random, correlating with the same social and health-system factors that predict treatment and outcome, so it is a confounded measurement error rather than noise.

title: Common data models harmonize structure without guaranteeing that the same variable means the same thing
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Concordance between target trial emulation and randomised controlled trials: systematic review and meta-analysis. BMJ 2025
Finds that closer design emulation and better outcome emulation predict agreement with trials, and that claims-based emulations tended to underestimate trial effects, which is where data provenance becomes measurable.


Wang, et al. An operational target trial emulation framework for causal inference using electronic health records. npj Digit Med 2026
Sets out the operational mapping from source fields to protocol components, the level at which provenance would have to be recorded.

title: Common data models harmonize structure without guaranteeing that the same variable means the same thing
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Maintain provenance graphs from source field to analytic variable and publish them with the study, so a reader can see which code set produced an outcome and when it changed. Run phenotype invariance and temporal-drift checks as standard diagnostics, and report leave-one-source-out analyses so the contribution of each linked source to the estimate is visible. Carry probabilistic linkage weights into the causal estimator rather than resolving links to a hard match, which turns linkage uncertainty into interval width instead of hidden bias.

title: Common data models harmonize structure without guaranteeing that the same variable means the same thing
text:
Verification

Verdict. Partially addressed. Auditors found the problem open. At least one qualified how it is stated; the qualification and who made it are in the trail below. Moved by the full-text reading: 1 finding from 1 paper naming work that covers part of this problem survived both the reader and an independent second reviewer, so the verdict moves from confirmed-open to partially-addressed, on a single finding. A further 19 findings in the same reading restate the problem as open; the two are consistent, and the part that is covered is named above.
Revised by the full-text reading. Applied full-text reading of the consolidated library.

Verdict changed

confirmed-open -> partially-addressed 1 surviving finding from: A Common Longitudinal Intensive Care Unit data Format (CLIF). New citations: 10.1101/2024.09.04.24313058


4 of the 4 independent auditors returned an opinion on this entry.

Literature and prior-art check

open / supported. A search for linkage or common-data-model work addressing semantic drift, provenance graphs or phenotype invariance returned nothing in the screened corpus. The concordance meta-analysis provides indirect support by finding that claims-based emulations tended to underestimate trial effects and that outcome-emulation quality predicted agreement, which is the data-provenance channel operating without being measured directly. The absence is the evidence here, so the confidence is capped: informatics venues indexed outside these eight phrases would not have been retrieved.

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / overstated. It is technically correct that a common data model standardizes representation without guaranteeing semantic, measurement, or causal equivalence. Versioned provenance and temporal validation are therefore important. Several stronger assertions are not generally correct. Semantic drift is not necessarily invisible in an analytic dataset; prevalence discontinuities, distribution shifts, coding transitions, and changes in associations can flag it, although provenance is usually needed to explain it. Linkage error is not inherently nonrandom and should not generically be called confounded measurement error: depending on the linkage mechanism, it can induce selection bias, exposure or outcome misclassification, or little bias. Most importantly, carrying probabilistic linkage weights into a causal estimator does not automatically convert hidden bias into interval width. That requires a calibrated linkage model, compatible integration with treatment and censoring estimation, and valid uncertainty propagation; differential or misspecified linkage can leave substantial bias. Provenance graphs, drift checks, and leave-one-source-out analyses are useful diagnostics but cannot prove semantic invariance or identify linkage bias by themselves. The issue is critical when key eligibility, treatment, confounder, or outcome variables are affected, but otherwise may be a robustness and provenance roadmap item.

Grok 4.5, recency lens

open / supported. The core claim is still true and was not overturned by 2024-2026 literature or software: common data models (OMOP and peers) standardize structure and vocabulary mapping, but do not guarantee semantic or causal equivalence of analytic variables across sites or years, and the mapping history and extract versions needed to check drift are still rarely published with target trial emulations. TARGET (2025) improves reporting of how the trial protocol is mapped to observational data, and OHDSI tools (DataQualityDashboard, CohortDiagnostics, standardized vocabularies) improve structural quality and phenotype characterization, but neither certifies that the same column means the same clinical construct. Work that partially implements pieces of the proposed direction exists and should not be ignored: Guha and Reiter (2024) fuse Bayesian probabilistic record linkage with causal estimators so linkage uncertainty propagates into treatment-effect inference rather than being collapsed to a hard match (bipartite two-file setting, evaluated in simulation and survey data, not multi-source claims-EHR-registry TTE as standard practice); Johns, Baum, and Prasser (2025) track provenance through clinical-warehouse ETL for quality management; semi-automated linkage provenance prototypes appear in the data-linkage literature. Those are proposals or infrastructure for components of the agenda, not a solved provenance-plus-invariance-plus-leave-one-source-out standard for multi-source TTE. The BMJ 2025 concordance review supports that design and outcome emulation quality matter for trial agreement, which makes provenance consequential, but does not itself close the semantic-equivalence gap. Searches for phenotype temporal-drift diagnostics, published source-to-analytic provenance graphs in TTE, and routine leave-one-source-out multi-source analyses as standard practice returned methods papers and tools, not field resolution. Vote open; partial methods noted in rationale without over-crediting them as solutions.

GLM-5.2, third independent lens

open / supported. The statement is internally consistent and correctly distinguishes structural harmonization from semantic equivalence. The claim that common data models solve the structural half without guaranteeing semantic equivalence is proportionate. The reasons provided for it being open (semantic drift is invisible in the analytic dataset, mapping histories are discarded, and linkage error is non-random) logically entail that the problem is currently open.

Decision path

R5:default-open → R9:substantiated-overstatement(n=1/4):codex → R17:reading-moved(confirmed-open->partially-addressed)

title: Eligibility criteria built from healthcare-use variables can induce selection through colliders
text: ELG-02 Confirmed open Medium-high priority Speculative Tractability 3/5

title: Eligibility criteria built from healthcare-use variables can induce selection through colliders
text:
Statement
An eligibility criterion is a conditioning statement, and conditioning on a variable that is a common effect of treatment and outcome opens a path rather than closing one. Emulation protocols routinely build eligibility from healthcare-use variables such as a required prior visit, a recorded baseline laboratory value or a minimum enrollment period, all of which can be descendants of the treatment decision or of early disease. Nothing in the current workflow checks an eligibility definition for this property, and the reporting checklist asks what the criteria were rather than what conditioning on them does.

title: Eligibility criteria built from healthcare-use variables can induce selection through colliders
text:
Why it is open
Whether a criterion is a collider depends on the causal structure, which is what the study is trying to learn, so the check cannot be purely empirical. Graph-learning algorithms recover only a Markov equivalence class and are further limited by latent confounding, so they can flag candidates and cannot certify. Removing a criterion also changes the target population, which means the correction has a cost that must be argued clinically rather than statistically.

title: Eligibility criteria built from healthcare-use variables can induce selection through colliders
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Hernán MA, Robins JM. Using big data to emulate a target trial when a randomized trial is not available. Am J Epidemiol 2016;183(8):758-764
Requires eligibility to be specified as a trial would specify it, which is the discipline that makes the collider question askable at all.


Cashin AG, Hansford HJ, Hernán MA, et al. Transparent reporting of observational studies emulating a target trial: the TARGET statement. JAMA 2025;334(12):1084
Requires the eligibility criteria and their emulation to be reported, without requiring an assessment of the selection they induce.

title: Eligibility criteria built from healthcare-use variables can induce selection through colliders
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Build a causal-discovery eligibility auditor that uses graph learning and temporal rules to flag proposed criteria that are post-treatment, that are colliders, or that encode healthcare use, and treat its output as advisory input to a domain review rather than as an automatic exclusion. Evaluate it on generated graphs with known structure, scoring collider-warning sensitivity, false-positive rate, expert agreement and, most importantly, whether acting on the warnings reduces bias. Never allow an algorithm to define eligibility by maximizing the apparent treatment effect, since that is a search over estimands dressed as a design step.

title: Eligibility criteria built from healthcare-use variables can induce selection through colliders
text:
Our study






NoteA study is designed



Question. Across 18 unique generated distributions and two analyst-information views, how large are bias and coverage distortions from conditioning on a prior healthcare-use variable under prespecified noncollider and collider DAGs; how much of the restricted-versus-broad contrast is target-population change; and does a complete, prespecified screen-and-response policy improve estimation of the restricted-population 60-month marginal risk difference relative to screen-free alternatives? This study answers only the conditional mechanism and policy-performance part of ELG-02. It does not determine whether an unknown real-world eligibility criterion is a collider.

title: Eligibility criteria built from healthcare-use variables can induce selection through colliders
text:
Verification

Verdict. Confirmed open. Auditors found the problem open. At least one qualified how it is stated; the qualification and who made it are in the trail below.
4 of the 4 independent auditors returned an opinion on this entry.

Literature and prior-art check

open / supported-with-caveat. The claim that nothing checks an eligibility definition for collider structure holds, and adjacent work is closer than the entry suggests. A 2026 npj Health Systems paper addresses eligibility-criteria-induced temporal selection directly, and machine-learning trial-eligibility emulation has been used to evaluate the generalizability of oncology trial results. A 2026 Frontiers in Medicine study uses emulation to evaluate eligibility criteria themselves in asthma and COPD. These evaluate the consequences of criteria rather than auditing them for collider structure before the analysis, which is what the entry proposes, so the specific artifact is still absent. Cites 10.1038/s44401-026-00082-3: Treats selection induced by eligibility criteria as the object of study, which is the mechanism the entry names.. Cites 10.3389/fmed.2026.1863026: Uses emulation to evaluate eligibility criteria, showing the criteria are becoming an object of analysis rather than a fixed input..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / overstated. Conditioning on an eligibility variable opens a noncausal path only when that variable is a collider, or a relevant descendant of one, in the assumed causal structure. Being a healthcare-use variable is not sufficient. The stated treatment-to-eligibility-to-outcome timing is also imprecise: eligibility fixed before time-zero treatment cannot be caused by that subsequent treatment or its subsequent outcome. The relevant graph may instead involve prebaseline treatment decisions, incipient disease, or common causes of treatment and outcome. Causal discovery does not universally return only a Markov equivalence class; what can be oriented depends on temporal, interventional, functional-form, and latent-confounding assumptions. It nevertheless cannot certify collider status from unrestricted observational data. An advisory tool for identifying possible temporal or collider problems remains an open development problem, but the asserted medium-high severity is context dependent rather than general.

Grok 4.5, recency lens

open / supported. Inverted prior: treat collider-inducing eligibility as already audited in routine TTE workflows, then search for a method or tool that does so. Found conceptual and design literature, not a solution. Hernán and Robins (2016) already require that eligibility not use postbaseline events; that is design discipline, not an automated check of whether a healthcare-use criterion is a collider. Weiskopf et al. (2023, JAMIA) explicitly frame healthcare utilization as a common collider in EHR reuse and warn that conditioning on utilization (by selection or adjustment) opens non-causal paths; Digitale et al. (2023, J Clin Epidemiol) likewise describe collider-conditioning bias when restricting to people in care or with a disease history. Wang et al. (2026) restate that conditioning eligibility on utilization induces collider bias at cohort entry. These works strengthen that the mechanism is real; they do not supply a certified check. TARGET (Hansford et al., 2025) requires reporting of eligibility criteria and their emulation, not assessment of the selection graph those criteria induce; the entry’s reading of TARGET is accurate. Practical reviews (e.g., Tran et al., 2026) continue to document post-treatment eligibility as a frequent high-risk design error, which is evidence the gap is still live in applications. No retrieved paper or package implements a causal-discovery or temporal-rule eligibility auditor for proposed TTE criteria with evaluation on known graphs (sensitivity, false-positive rate, expert agreement, bias reduction when acting on warnings). Federated causal discovery and general DAG tools exist in adjacent literature but are not integrated into TTE protocol design or reporting checklists. Graph learning recovering only a Markov equivalence class under latent confounding remains a structural limit, as the entry states; formalizations of that limit do not close the problem. Queries run: collider + eligibility + target trial (2024–2026); healthcare utilization collider + eligibility; TARGET checklist collider/selection; causal discovery eligibility auditor TTE; CRAN/GitHub TrialEmulation, WeightIt, MatchIt, cobalt for eligibility-collider features (none found). Open as a workflow and tooling problem; prior art names the bias and forbids postbaseline criteria but does not solve systematic detection of healthcare-use colliders in eligibility definitions.

GLM-5.2, third independent lens

open / supported. The claim is coherent and proportionate. It accurately describes how conditioning on healthcare-use variables for eligibility can induce collider bias. The reasons given for the problem being open are structurally sound: the causal structure is the target of inference, graph-learning algorithms can only flag candidates and cannot certify due to latent confounding, and removing a criterion changes the estimand. This is a claim about a real structural difficulty and current practice limitations, not an overstatement of impossibility.

Decision path

R5:default-open → R9:substantiated-overstatement(n=1/4):codex

title: Emulation assumes no interference, and cloning individuals can produce joint strategies nobody could implement
text: EST-01 Partially addressed High priority Emerging Tractability 2/5

title: Emulation assumes no interference, and cloning individuals can produce joint strategies nobody could implement
text:
Statement
One person’s treatment can change another’s outcome through infection, provider behavior, household exposure or a shared resource constraint. Target trial emulation as normally practiced assumes this does not happen. Methods under partial interference define direct and spillover effects and are well developed in their own literature, but they are rarely joined to emulation, and the join is not cosmetic: eligibility, assignment and positivity all become cluster- or network-dependent quantities. Cloning individuals independently, which is the standard device for grace periods, can assign a set of clones a joint strategy that no cluster could actually receive, so the artificial censoring is then censoring on an impossible world. The TARGET reporting guideline currently offers no cluster-trial extension.

title: Emulation assumes no interference, and cloning individuals can produce joint strategies nobody could implement
text:
Why it is open
Under interference the estimand has to be defined through an exposure mapping, and there is no canonical mapping: own treatment plus treated-neighbor proportion is one choice among many and different choices give different, equally valid, effects. Positivity must hold for the joint neighborhood exposure, which is a far stronger requirement than individual positivity and typically fails in observed networks. Networks are also measured with error, and contagion, homophily and spillover are only weakly separable from one another even when the network is known exactly.

title: Emulation assumes no interference, and cloning individuals can produce joint strategies nobody could implement
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Papadogeorgou G, Mealli F, Zigler CM. Causal inference with interfering units for cluster and population level treatment allocation programs. Biometrics 2019;75(3):778-787
Defines direct and spillover effects for cluster and population-level allocation, one of the frameworks that would have to be joined to the emulation protocol.


TARGET reporting guideline, official resources
The reporting standard for emulations, whose stated scope is parallel-group, individually randomized target trials, so cluster designs fall outside it.

title: Emulation assumes no interference, and cloning individuals can produce joint strategies nobody could implement
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Define network target trials in which the exposure mapping is part of the protocol rather than an analysis convenience, and state the positivity condition for the joint neighborhood exposure explicitly. Develop cluster-level clone-censor-weighting so that compatibility is judged for the cluster rather than the individual, alongside network targeted learning and agent-based g-computation. Test sensitivity to network mismeasurement and to violations of partial interference by deleting edges at known rates, because a method that is correct on a perfectly observed network and silent on a noisy one is not usable on real data.

title: Emulation assumes no interference, and cloning individuals can produce joint strategies nobody could implement
text:
Verification

Verdict. Partially addressed. Auditors found the problem open. At least one qualified how it is stated; the qualification and who made it are in the trail below. Moved by the full-text reading: 5 findings from 5 papers naming work that covers part of this problem survived both the reader and an independent second reviewer, so the verdict moves from confirmed-open to partially-addressed. A further 16 findings in the same reading restate the problem as open; the two are consistent, and the part that is covered is named above.
Revised by the full-text reading. Applied full-text reading of the consolidated library.

Verdict changed

confirmed-open -> partially-addressed 5 surviving findings from: Adjacent spillover efficacy of Wolbachia for control of deng; Emulating Target Trials to Improve Causal Inference From Age; Estimating the herd effects of antimicrobial prevention inte; G-Formula for Observational Studies under Stratified Interfe; Spillover benefit of pre-exposure prophylaxis for HIV preven. New citations: 10.1002/sim.10102, 10.1017/s0950268822001650, 10.1093/aje/kwab040, 10.1093/jac/dkaf033, 10.1186/s12916-025-03941-2


4 of the 4 independent auditors returned an opinion on this entry.

Literature and prior-art check

open / supported. Nothing in the corpus defines a network target trial with an explicit exposure mapping, cluster-level clone-censor-weighting, or a positivity condition stated for joint neighborhood exposure. The interference literature is present in the corpus only through its own methodological line, and the multi-site and distributed-analysis papers address data governance rather than interference. The claim that individual cloning can assign clones a joint strategy no cluster could receive is a structural argument the entry makes rather than one the corpus states, and it follows from the definitions.

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / overstated. The interference problem is technically real, but the cloning account is imprecise. Cloning creates strategy-specific copies of each individual; it does not itself assign a realized cluster jointly. Identification fails when those individual strategies are interpreted as an infeasible or unsupported joint allocation. That is a failure of intervention definition, consistency, or structural joint positivity, not artificial censoring on an impossible world. Eligibility also need not always be cluster-dependent. The status vote concerns this technical problem and does not rely on claims about rarity or current TARGET scope.

Grok 4.5, recency lens

open / supported. Inverted-prior search did not find a solution that joins partial-interference identification to target-trial emulation in a way that closes the gaps named in the statement. Papadogeorgou et al. (2019), already cited, supplies cluster/population allocation estimands under interference; it does not supply an emulation protocol, joint-neighborhood positivity diagnostics, or clone-censor rules that keep cluster strategies feasible. Buchanan et al. (Stat Med 2022; 10.1002/sim.9427) is the closest prior art: it defines a target-trial protocol for disseminated (spillover) effects of MOUD within provider-based clusters using routinely collected data, so the “rarely joined” claim should be read as rare rather than never. That paper is an application and estimation sketch under partial interference for a specific provider-cluster exposure mapping; it does not invent cluster-level clone-censor-weighting, does not resolve non-canonical exposure mappings, and does not evaluate network mismeasurement. Lu et al. (arXiv 2604.12900, 2026) propose emulating stepped-wedge cluster randomized trials for staggered policy adoption; that covers group-level policy emulation and mentions spillovers as a shared design concern, not individual-treatment cloning that assigns impossible joint strategies. Official TARGET resources (target-guideline.org, retrieved 2026) still scope the checklist to parallel-group, individually randomized target trials, list “Emulation of a cluster target trial” as a possible future extension, and state that no extensions are currently in development, which confirms rather than repairs the reporting gap. Searches across AJE/Epidemiology/IJE/EJE/JCE/PDS/Stat Med/Biometrics, arXiv stat.ME, medRxiv, and package activity (TrialEmulation, gfoRmula, gfoRmulaICE, lmtp, ltmle, CICI, WeightIt) found no merged software that implements network/cluster-compatible clone-censor-weighting or network TMLE for TTE. Contagion/homophily/spillover non-separability and joint-neighborhood positivity remain structural; sensitivity to edge deletion is proposed in the agenda and was not found as a standard TTE tool. Vote open: prior art proposes joins in narrow settings; none solves exposure-mapping canonicity, joint positivity, network error, or cluster-compatible cloning as stated.

GLM-5.2, third independent lens

open / supported. The statement is internally consistent and proportionate. It correctly identifies that standard target trial emulation assumes no interference, and that joining interference methods to emulation is non-trivial because eligibility, assignment, and positivity become cluster-dependent. The reasons given for it being open (lack of canonical exposure mapping, stronger positivity requirements for joint exposures, and network measurement error) are valid structural methodological challenges that entail the problem is open. It does not assert an impossibility, but rather a current gap in joined practice.

Decision path

R5:default-open → R9:substantiated-overstatement(n=1/4):codex → R17:reading-moved(confirmed-open->partially-addressed)

title: A hazard ratio is reported where the estimand was a weighted per-protocol effect among the grace-period compatible
text: EST-03 Partially addressed Very high priority Established Tractability 5/5

title: A hazard ratio is reported where the estimand was a weighted per-protocol effect among the grace-period compatible
text:
Statement
Hazard ratios, odds ratios and model coefficients are routinely presented without naming the intervention, the population, the time horizon or the strategy for each intercurrent event. ICH E9(R1) and the TARGET statement both require that objectives, estimands and sensitivity analyses be aligned, and applied reporting has not caught up. The concrete failure is specific rather than general: a reader sees a hazard ratio and infers an intention-to-treat contrast, while the analysis in fact estimated a per-protocol effect, weighted for informative censoring, among the subset of patients whose observed treatment stayed compatible with a strategy during a grace period. Those are different quantities in different populations and nothing in the presentation distinguishes them.

title: A hazard ratio is reported where the estimand was a weighted per-protocol effect among the grace-period compatible
text:
Why it is open
The hazard ratio is a familiar output that survives every methodological upgrade beneath it, so improvements in the estimator do not change what gets read. Stating the estimand precisely requires naming the population induced by cloning and censoring, which has no simple clinical description. Absolute risks and restricted mean survival differences communicate better and require the analyst to commit to a time horizon, which is an additional decision most would rather not defend.

title: A hazard ratio is reported where the estimand was a weighted per-protocol effect among the grace-period compatible
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




ICH E9(R1) addendum on estimands and sensitivity analysis in clinical trials
Defines the estimand attributes, population, treatment, endpoint, intercurrent-event strategy and summary measure, that an emulation report would have to fill in.


Cashin AG, Hansford HJ, Hernán MA, et al. Transparent reporting of observational studies emulating a target trial: the TARGET statement. JAMA 2025;334(12):1084
A 21-item checklist requiring the target protocol and its emulation to be reported, aimed at transparency rather than at risk-of-bias certification.


Maringe C, Benitez Majano S, Exarchakou A, et al. Reflection on modern methods: trial emulation in the presence of immortal-time bias. Int J Epidemiol 2020;49(5):1719-1729
Makes explicit that clone-censor-weight analyses target per-protocol-type contrasts rather than baseline intention-to-treat effects.

title: A hazard ratio is reported where the estimand was a weighted per-protocol effect among the grace-period compatible
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Require a one-sentence estimand statement naming the intervention, the population, the horizon and the intercurrent-event strategy, positioned before any effect measure. Report absolute risks, risk differences and restricted mean outcomes at clinically meaningful horizons, with the hazard ratio as a supplement rather than the headline. Include a timeline diagram showing treatment paths and censoring rules, since the population induced by cloning is easier to draw than to describe.

title: A hazard ratio is reported where the estimand was a weighted per-protocol effect among the grace-period compatible
text:
Verification

Verdict. Partially addressed. Part of this problem is addressed by existing work; the entry names which part.
Dissent. literature dissented (open): The estimand vocabulary is arriving in the emulation literature: a 2026 Trials paper applies a hypothetical strategy to the intercurrent event of non-adherence using the parametric g-formula, which is the ICH E9(R1) discipline executed inside a longitudinal analysis, and a 2026 Journal of Epidemiology paper argues explicitly for going beyond the hazard ratio when censo […]
4 of the 4 independent auditors returned an opinion on this entry.

Literature and prior-art check

open / supported-with-caveat. The estimand vocabulary is arriving in the emulation literature: a 2026 Trials paper applies a hypothetical strategy to the intercurrent event of non-adherence using the parametric g-formula, which is the ICH E9(R1) discipline executed inside a longitudinal analysis, and a 2026 Journal of Epidemiology paper argues explicitly for going beyond the hazard ratio when censoring, confounding and competing events are present. The entry’s claim is about what published reports lead with rather than what is possible, and no reporting requirement in the corpus mandates a one-sentence estimand statement or absolute-risk reporting. The presence of these papers means the entry should not imply the vocabulary is missing. Cites 10.1186/s13063-026-09708-1: Executes an ICH E9(R1) intercurrent-event strategy inside a g-formula analysis, which is the alignment the entry asks for.. Cites 10.2188/jea.je20250662: Argues directly against the hazard ratio as the reported quantity in this setting..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

partially-solved / overstated. The reporting concern is valid, but the stated population is wrong. Correct clone-censor weighting does not target only patients whose observed treatment remained compatible. It reweights uncensored clone-time observations to represent artificially censored observations, thereby targeting the baseline eligible population under the specified strategies, subject to exchangeability and positivity. A bare hazard ratio identifies neither an intention-to-treat nor a per-protocol strategy and may lack a causal interpretation altogether. TARGET supplies much of the reporting solution; the residual issue is adoption rather than an unresolved estimand method. Cites 10.1001/jama.2025.13350: Provides an explicit reporting framework for the target protocol, its emulation, and effect estimates. This resolves much of the standards gap but not compliance or the incorrect subset interpretation..

Grok 4.5, recency lens

open / supported-with-caveat. The problem is framed as a presentation/practice failure after standards already exist: a reader sees a bare hazard ratio and infers an intention-to-treat contrast, while the analysis estimated a censoring-weighted per-protocol effect among grace-period–compatible (often cloned) patients. Maringe et al. (IJE 2020; 10.1093/ije/dyaa057), already cited, already makes the CCW estimand type explicit; that formalizes the distinction and does not change what applied papers headline. ICH E9(R1) and the TARGET statement (JAMA 2025; 10.1001/jama.2025.13350) require aligned objectives, estimands, and sensitivity analyses; TARGET item structure places target-trial protocol/estimand items (6a–g) beside emulation mapping (7a–g), and item 13 asks for effect estimates with precision including both absolute and relative measures when applicable. Official TARGET resources confirm that scope and provide protocol table and flow-diagram templates. That is real progress on the reporting-standard side and is the caveat on support: the claim is still true about practice, but “standards are missing” would be overstated after TARGET 2025. What remains open is exactly what the report names: applied reporting has not caught up; the HR remains a familiar default that survives estimator upgrades; and nothing forces a one-sentence estimand that names intervention, population induced by cloning/censoring, horizon, and intercurrent-event strategy before the first effect measure. Fourati et al. (Eur J Prev Cardiol 2026 advance article) still notes that relative measures such as hazard ratios are frequently reported and that absolute risks and risk differences at meaningful times communicate better, which is consistent with ongoing practice lag months after TARGET. No package release (TrialEmulation, gfoRmula, gfoRmulaICE, lmtp, ltmle, survtmle, concrete, riskRegression, adjustedCurves) was found that auto-emits an ICH/TARGET-style estimand sentence or demotes the HR to a supplement. Vote open: standards partially codify the proposed direction; the concrete misread of weighted grace-period PP as ITT HR remains an open practice and communication problem.

GLM-5.2, third independent lens

open / supported. The statement is well-scoped and proportionate. It accurately describes the specific mismatch between the reported effect measure (a hazard ratio) and the actual estimand (a per-protocol effect among the grace-period compatible) in clone-censor-weight analyses. The reasons for it being open (cultural inertia of the hazard ratio, difficulty of clinically describing the cloned population, and reluctance to commit to a time horizon for absolute measures) are practical and structural barriers that genuinely support the problem being open.

Decision path

R3:partially-solved(n=1/4) → R9:substantiated-overstatement(n=1/4):codex

title: An emulation enters a synthesis with randomized trials through a discrepancy parameter that nothing identifies
text: EST-05 Confirmed open High priority Promising Tractability 4/5

title: An emulation enters a synthesis with randomized trials through a discrepancy parameter that nothing identifies
text:
Statement
Emulated trials are combined with randomized trials in three ways: as an added study in a network meta-analysis, as an external or hybrid control arm borrowed into a randomized trial, and as a substituted effectiveness input to an economic model. All three need a quantity that neither source supplies, the systematic difference between what the emulation estimates and what the trial estimates, and practice sets it by assumption. A bivariate network meta-analysis that bridged first-line and second-line biologic therapies in rheumatoid arthritis combined 21 randomized trials with six registry-derived target trials entered at face value, assumed equivalent to randomized data. A cost-effectiveness analysis in the same disease put the emulated probability of at least a moderate response at 0.215 against 0.650 in the randomized trial, with a between-source odds ratio of 0.30 (95% confidence interval 0.23 to 0.37), then pooled the two into 0.336 as though the difference were sampling variation; the pooled incremental cost-effectiveness ratio came to 46,300 pounds per quality-adjusted life-year, essentially the real-world value of 46,800 rather than a number between the sources. Hybrid control designs instead discount the external arm by a tuning parameter calibrated from earlier replication exercises, in which residual bias hazard ratios ran between 0.96 and 1.10 for nine of eleven emulated lung cancer control arms and between 0.66 and 1.09 for most of fifteen trials across tumor types. No criterion decides whether a given emulation is exchangeable enough to enter a network, and no borrowing method balances post-baseline treatment patterns, so a borrowed control arm can answer a different estimand from the randomized arm it augments.

title: An emulation enters a synthesis with randomized trials through a discrepancy parameter that nothing identifies
text:
Why it is open
The discrepancy is not identified. Separating it from real effect modification would require observing the same population under both designs, and the reason for combining the sources is precisely that neither covers what the other does. Cross-design synthesis machinery therefore takes the bias term as an input, whether as a design adjustment, an inflated between-study variance or a power-prior weight, all supplied by judgment rather than estimated from the data being combined. Dynamic borrowing tries to recover the weight from outcome agreement, which makes it a function of the quantity under test and works only when the sources agree for the right reason: simulation shows propensity-integrated Bayesian borrowing controlling bias and type I error under selection bias and failing under unmeasured confounding, measurement error and effect drift. The estimands also differ before any weight is applied, since a trial reports an intention-to-treat contrast under protocolized follow-up while an emulation of the same question usually reports a per-protocol contrast under routine care, and nothing aligns the two before pooling.

title: An emulation enters a synthesis with randomized trials through a discrepancy parameter that nothing identifies
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Efthimiou O, Mavridis D, Debray TPA, et al. Combining randomized and non-randomized evidence in network meta-analysis. Stat Med 2017;36(8):1210-1226
Sets out naive pooling, design-adjusted synthesis, non-randomized evidence as prior information and three-level hierarchical models, each of which requires a bias term the combined data do not supply.


Schmitz S, Adams R, Walsh C. Incorporating data from various trial designs into a mixed treatment comparison model. Stat Med 2013;32(17):2935-2949
Gives the three-level hierarchical model that adjusts for design bias while allowing heterogeneity between designs, which is the structure a synthesis including emulations would use.


Hamza T, Schwarzer G, Salanti G. crossnma: an R package to synthesize cross-design evidence and cross-format data using network meta-analysis and network meta-regression. BMC Med Res Methodol 2024;24(1):169
Implements Bayesian three-level cross-design network meta-analysis, so the machinery is available and what remains missing is the bias input the user must supply.


Bujkiewicz S, Singh J, Wheaton L, et al. Bridging disconnected networks of first and second lines of biologic therapies in rheumatoid arthritis with registry data: Bayesian evidence synthesis with target trial emulation. J Clin Epidemiol 2022;150:171-178
Enters six registry-derived target trials into a network with 21 randomized trials at face value and names power-prior down-weighting and design-level hierarchical modeling as untried alternatives.


Singh J, Stevenson M, Hyrich KL, Gillies CL, Abrams KR, Bujkiewicz S. Target trial emulation to incorporate real-world data in the estimation of the clinical and cost-effectiveness of biologic treatment. Med Decis Making 2026;46(3):386-398
Pools an emulated and a randomized response probability that differ with an odds ratio of 0.30, and carries the pooled value into an economic model whose cost-effectiveness ratio moves from 34,700 to 46,300 pounds per quality-adjusted life-year.


Tan WK, Segal BD, Curtis MD, et al. Augmenting control arms with real-world data for cancer trials: hybrid control arm methods and considerations. Contemp Clin Trials Commun 2022;30:101000
Compares static and dynamic borrowing methods, calibrates their tuning parameters against measured residual bias from earlier control-arm emulations, and names covariate balancing weights for post-baseline treatment patterns as the missing piece.


Wang C, Li H, Chen WC, Lu N, Tiwari R, Xu Y, Yue LQ. Propensity score-integrated power prior approach for incorporating real-world evidence in single-arm clinical studies. J Biopharm Stat 2019;29(5):731-748
Stratifies on the propensity score and applies a power prior within strata, which supplies the baseline covariate half of the balancing-plus-borrowing problem.


Wang J, Tiwari R. Approximate Bayesian analysis for borrowing external controls for randomized controlled trials with dynamic borrowing and covariate balancing adjustment. Pharm Stat 2025;24(2):e2474
Combines covariate balancing with dynamic borrowing in a single Bayesian bootstrap procedure, which closes the baseline part of the 2022 request and leaves the post-baseline part open.


Wang K, Cao H, Yao C. Bayesian proactive dynamic borrowing utilizing propensity score overlap for a hybrid control arm and the impacts of various biases: a simulation study. J Evid Based Med 2025;18(2):e70022
Shows propensity-integrated Bayesian borrowing controlling bias and type I error under selection bias and losing that control under unmeasured confounding, measurement error and effect drift.


Wang P, Hong H, Jeon K, Thomas LE. Trials augmented by external control data using balancing weights: a comparison of estimands and estimators. Contemp Clin Trials 2026;162:108220
Sets out which causal estimands propensity-weighted estimators actually target in a hybrid trial, which is the step that has to precede pooling and is usually skipped.


Lai PC, Lai CH, Lai EC, Huang YT. Do we need to administer fludrocortisone in addition to hydrocortisone in adult patients with septic shock? An updated systematic review with Bayesian network meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials and an observational study with target trial emulation. Crit Care Med 2024;52(4):e193-e202
Combines randomized trials and observational target trial emulations across 19 studies and 95,841 patients in one Bayesian network meta-analysis, an applied instance of the practice with no stated admission criterion.

title: An emulation enters a synthesis with randomized trials through a discrepancy parameter that nothing identifies
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Estimate the discrepancy rather than assume it: build a bias distribution from paired emulation and trial results in the same disease area and data source, and use it as the prior on the design effect that cross-design synthesis and power-prior borrowing already require as an input. Report the pooled estimate alongside the source-specific estimates and the implied bias, so a reader can see how much of the pooled number is borrowed and from where. Require estimand alignment before pooling: state which contrast each source identifies, and reweight or re-emulate so that both answer the same question rather than pooling an efficacy estimate with an effectiveness estimate. Extend covariate balancing inside borrowing methods to post-baseline treatment patterns, treating treatment duration and subsequent therapy as time-varying variables to be weighted rather than as differences left for the borrowing parameter to absorb. The first tractable step is a prespecified discrepancy prior calibrated on the existing benchmarking literature, which turns an assumption that is currently invisible into a reported quantity.

title: An emulation enters a synthesis with randomized trials through a discrepancy parameter that nothing identifies
text:
Verification

Verdict. Confirmed open. Auditors found the problem open. At least one qualified how it is stated; the qualification and who made it are in the trail below.
Dissent. codex dissented (overstated): The narrow identification problem is real: without a common-comparison anchor or defensible cross-design exchangeability restrictions, a trial-emulation difference conflates residual emulation bias, genuine effect heterogeneity, measurement differences, and sampling error. Those components are not nonparametrically separable. […]
3 of the 4 independent auditors returned an opinion on this entry; grok did not, and the majority rules below are sized accordingly.

Literature and prior-art check

open / supported-with-caveat. Searched the 1,376-record screened corpus. The headline claim holds: no record supplies the discrepancy between what an emulation estimates and what a trial estimates, and no record states a criterion for admitting an emulation into a network. The 2022 rheumatoid arthritis synthesis the entry cites is the only record in the corpus that enters emulated trials into a network with randomized trials, and it enters them at face value, so the practice the entry describes is real and unaccompanied by an admission rule. The caveat is on one sentence rather than on the entry. The entry asserts that the estimands differ before any weight is applied and that nothing aligns the two before pooling. For the external and hybrid control route that sentence is refuted by named work in the corpus. A 2024 paper crosses the five estimand-framework attributes with the seven target trial components specifically for external comparator studies and identifies the overlaps and omissions; a second 2024 paper applies both frameworks to an external control analysis in solid tumors as a worked case; a 2025 paper takes the further step of estimating per-protocol effects in external comparator analyses precisely because the intention-to-treat target is hard to interpret when adherence differs between the trial and the external arm, which is the mismatch the entry names. The alignment machinery exists for that route and is recent, so the sentence should be scoped to the network and economic-model routes, where the corpus contains nothing comparable. One scope limitation on this check: power prior, dynamic borrowing and commensurate prior together match one record out of 1,376, so the borrowing literature the entry cites lies almost entirely outside a corpus harvested on target trial phrases, and nothing here confirms or refutes the entry’s claims about it.

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / overstated. The narrow identification problem is real: without a common-comparison anchor or defensible cross-design exchangeability restrictions, a trial-emulation difference conflates residual emulation bias, genuine effect heterogeneity, measurement differences, and sampling error. Those components are not nonparametrically separable. A discrepancy distribution learned from benchmark pairs is a transported predictive prior, not identification of bias in a new emulation; it requires a defined target class, conditional exchangeability of discrepancies, and overlap. The statement nevertheless overgeneralizes. Not every network meta-analysis, external-control analysis, or economic model requires one scalar discrepancy parameter. With overlapping comparisons or an internal randomized control, design differences or outcome commensurability can be estimated under explicit hierarchical or transport models, although their causal attribution remains assumption-dependent. Observing the same population under both designs is neither necessary, because transport assumptions may suffice, nor sufficient, because estimands, measurement, follow-up, and treatment versions may still differ. The claim that trials report intention-to-treat effects while emulations usually report per-protocol effects is categorically unsound: either design can target a treatment-policy assignment effect or a per-protocol sustained-strategy effect. Post-baseline treatment duration and subsequent therapy are mediators or intercurrent events, not baseline covariates to be generically balanced. They should remain part of a treatment-policy estimand or be placed under an explicit intervention and handled with longitudinal g-methods under sequential exchangeability and positivity for a hypothetical or per-protocol estimand. The numerical sentence is also inconsistent: probabilities 0.215 and 0.650 imply an odds ratio of 0.147, while their risk ratio is 0.331; therefore 0.30 is not the stated between-source odds ratio unless it refers to an undefined alternative contrast. Moreover, 46,300 is literally between 34,700 and 46,800, and an incremental cost-effectiveness ratio need not interpolate linearly as response probabilities change. The assertion that pooling treated all discrepancy as sampling variation also requires knowing whether the model was fixed-effect, random-effects, or hierarchical. The only explicit software claim concerns crossnma, which is absent from calibration.json and documentation/refs/packages; I therefore abstain on its capabilities and required inputs. High severity is proportionate when decision-grade pooling proceeds without estimand alignment or discrepancy sensitivity analysis, but not as a universal characterization of all cross-design synthesis.

GLM-5.2, third independent lens

abstain / supported. The claim is internally consistent and identifies a structural identification problem: the systematic difference (bias) between an emulation and a randomized trial cannot be separated from true effect modification using only the combined data, because the sources cover different populations or settings. The reason given for the problem being open (that separating discrepancy from effect modification requires observing the same population under both designs, which defeats the purpose of combining) logically entails that the discrepancy parameter is not identified from the synthesis data alone. The scope is appropriate, noting that estimands differ (ITT vs per-protocol) before any weight is applied, and that dynamic borrowing conflates the weight with the outcome agreement. The severity is proportionate, as assuming the bias term can lead to misleading pooled estimates. I abstain on the status axis because I cannot search for recent literature that might have proposed a solution to this identification problem.

Decision path

R5:default-open → R9:substantiated-overstatement(n=1/3):codex

title: Identification of dynamic regimes in continuous time under treatment-dependent observation is unresolved
text: GMT-02 Partially addressed High priority Emerging Tractability 2/5

title: Identification of dynamic regimes in continuous time under treatment-dependent observation is unresolved
text:
Statement
Treatments, outcomes and clinical observations occur asynchronously and are recorded at times determined by the care process. Almost every applied g-method assumes a prespecified discrete grid, and discretization can reverse temporal ordering between a treatment and an outcome that fell in the same interval, merge multiple events into one, or define an estimand that exists only relative to the chosen interval. General identification results for dynamic regimes under irregular observation, treatment-dependent visiting and within-interval effects remain limited, so the applied analyst working in continuous time has a modeling apparatus without an identification theorem to sit under it.

title: Identification of dynamic regimes in continuous time under treatment-dependent observation is unresolved
text:
Why it is open
In continuous time the treatment process, the visit process and the outcome process are counting processes whose intensities depend on each other, and sequential exchangeability has to be stated with respect to filtrations rather than to a fixed sequence of covariate vectors. The conditions under which a dynamic regime is identified in that setting are strictly stronger and harder to interpret than their discrete counterparts. There is also no natural sample-size asymptotics: the information about an intensity comes from event counts rather than from patients, so the usual scaling arguments do not apply cleanly.

title: Identification of dynamic regimes in continuous time under treatment-dependent observation is unresolved
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Tankpinou Zoumenou H, et al. Time Partitioning in Target Trial Emulation. arXiv 2026
Treats the partition of time as a modeling choice with consequences rather than as a convention, which is the entry point to the continuous-time question.


Robins JM, Hernán MA, Brumback B. Marginal structural models and causal inference in epidemiology. Epidemiology 2000;11(5):550-560
The discrete-time identification result that continuous-time work has to generalize, stated with sequential exchangeability, positivity and consistency.


Goldstein BA, Bhavsar NA, Phelan M, Pencina MJ. How and when informative visit processes can bias inference when using electronic health records data for clinical research. J Am Med Inform Assoc 2019
Establishes that the visit process in electronic health records is informative, which is the condition that makes the continuous-time problem hard rather than merely technical.

title: Identification of dynamic regimes in continuous time under treatment-dependent observation is unresolved
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Combine marked point-process models, continuous-time structural nested models and neural ordinary differential equations, constraining the learned components to nuisance functions that the identification result actually requires, so the flexibility sits where it cannot manufacture a contrast. Study invariance of estimates across nested time grids as a routine diagnostic: an estimand defined in continuous time should be stable as the grid refines, and instability localizes the failure. State the identification conditions in filtration terms and show which of them a standard electronic health record violates.

title: Identification of dynamic regimes in continuous time under treatment-dependent observation is unresolved
text:
Verification

Verdict. Partially addressed. 2 independent auditors judged the claim as stated too strong. Discretizing asynchronous clinical processes can obscure temporal ordering and change the intervention being estimated. A continuous-time emulation must define treatment, covariate, visit, censoring and outcome processes relative to a filtration and impose assumptions connecting latent histories to the observed visit process. Grid-refinement analyses can reveal sensitivity to discretization, but they cannot establish identification. Moved by the full-text reading: 6 findings from 6 papers naming work that covers part of this problem survived both the reader and an independent second reviewer, so the verdict moves from overstated to partially-addressed. A further 21 findings in the same reading restate the problem as open; the two are consistent, and the part that is covered is named above.
Dissent. literature dissented (supported-with-caveat): The entry says general implementable identification results for dynamic regimes under irregular, treatment-dependent observation remain limited. Estimation in that setting is further along than the entry allows. […]
Revised by the full-text reading. Applied full-text reading of the consolidated library.

Verdict changed

overstated -> partially-addressed 6 surviving findings from: Bias due to coarsening of time intervals in the inference fo; Causal estimands and identification of time-varying effects ; Continuous-Time Causal Inference With Marked Point Process W; Estimating the causal effects of multiple intermittent treat; The Impact of Different CD4 Cell-Count Monitoring and Switch; The additive hazard estimator is consistent for continuous-t. New citations: 10.1002/sim.70102, 10.1007/s10985-019-09468-y, 10.1093/aje/kwv083, 10.1093/biostatistics/kxag014, 10.1093/ije/dyae100


4 of the 4 independent auditors returned an opinion on this entry.

Literature and prior-art check

partially-solved / supported-with-caveat. The entry says general implementable identification results for dynamic regimes under irregular, treatment-dependent observation remain limited. Estimation in that setting is further along than the entry allows. Continuous-time marginal structural model weights built from a marked point process have been constructed and applied where visit times are irregular and informative and treatment history carries duration and dose. G-computation and doubly robust standardization for continuous-time data have been compared with inverse probability weighting. What has not been supplied is the general identification theorem the entry asks for, stated in filtration terms and covering within-interval effects, so the theoretical half of the claim stands while the estimation half is weaker than written. Cites 10.1002/sim.70102: Constructs continuous-time marginal structural model weights via a marked point process precisely because primary-care visit times are irregular and informative and treatment history has duration and dose.. Cites 10.1177/09622802211047345: Compares continuous-time g-computation and doubly robust standardization against IPW, which is the estimator comparison the entry proposes as future work..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / overstated. The difficult open component is identification and estimation under explicitly defined full-data and observation-process assumptions, not a wholesale absence of continuous-time identification theory. Treatment-dependent visiting does not by itself destroy identification; the analyst must specify assumptions linking the latent longitudinal process to what is observed, together with treatment, observation and censoring positivity. If clinically relevant covariate history between visits is unobserved and no coarsening or observation model is imposed, the regime effect is generally not identified. Filtration-based exchangeability is different from, but not automatically strictly stronger than, every discrete-time formulation. Coarsening can erase or impose an incorrect ordering, although it does not mechanically reverse ordering in every shared interval. The claim that there is no natural sample-size asymptotics is false: independent patients provide a standard n-to-infinity sequence, and counting-process estimators use martingale asymptotics, with information also affected by event counts and follow-up. Grid refinement is a sensitivity analysis, not an identification test; instability does not localize a unique failure, and stability cannot validate exchangeability or the observation model.

Grok 4.5, recency lens

partially-solved / overstated. The claim that continuous-time dynamic-regime identification under irregular, process-driven observation is essentially without an identification theorem is stronger than the literature allows. Rytgaard, Gerds, and van der Laan (Annals of Statistics 2022) give a continuous-time counting-process TMLE for intervention-specific means when treatment, covariates, and outcomes occur at subject-specific times; intensities track monitoring; dynamic regimes on treatment assigned are defined with visit times kept as they naturally occur; and identification is via continuous-time g-computation under sequential exchangeability and positivity on the product-integral likelihood. Røysland, Ryalen, Nygård, and Didelez (JRSS-B 2025; arXiv:2202.02311) supply nonparametric graphical identification criteria for marginal effects of interventions on treatment-process intensities in continuous-time survival and event-history models, including structural conditions on censoring beyond classical independent censoring. Earlier continuous-time MSM and structural nested model work (Røysland; Ryalen et al. on prostate cancer) already stated filtration-based sequential exchangeability. What remains open, and why this is only partial: applied g-methods still default to discrete grids (Tankpinou et al. arXiv:2603.15924 still treats time partitioning as a consequential modeling choice); Rytgaard’s main identification path intervenes on treatment decisions while leaving the visit intensity natural, so full dynamic control of a treatment-dependent informative visit process plus within-interval effects is not a closed applied recipe for EHR; software for continuous-time LTMLE is not yet a routine TTE default. Proposal papers that add unmeasured confounding (for example arXiv:2604.00544) are not resolutions. Identification theory exists; the residual gap is completeness for treatment-dependent observation, within-interval estimands, and routine practice. Cites 10.1214/21-AOS2114: Provides continuous-time counting-process identification (g-computation on product integrals) and efficient TMLE for time-varying and dynamic treatment interventions when monitoring times are subject-specific; models monitoring intensities and covers dynamic regimes on treatment assigned with natural visit schedules.. Cites 10.1093/jrsssb/qkae056: States nonparametric graphical identification criteria for marginal effects of interventions on continuous-time treatment-process intensities using local independence / counting-process graphs, including structural conditions on censoring; directly supplies the filtration-style identification theorem the agenda says is missing.. Cites arxiv:2603.15924: Does not close identification; documents that discrete time partitioning remains a consequential open modeling choice in applied TTE, which supports residual openness after continuous-time theory..

GLM-5.2, third independent lens

open / supported. The claim is coherent and proportionate. It says general identification results ‘remain limited’ rather than asserting they do not exist, which correctly frames this as a gap in current theory rather than a structural impossibility. The reason given for openness is substantive: in continuous time, exchangeability must be stated over filtrations, conditions are strictly stronger than discrete counterparts, and event-count-based asymptotics do not scale the way patient-count asymptotics do. These are genuine theoretical obstacles, not mere inconveniences. The scope is appropriately narrow—dynamic regimes under irregular observation and treatment-dependent visiting—rather than overgeneralizing to all continuous-time causal inference.

Decision path

R3:partially-solved(n=2/4) → R8:overstated-majority(n=2/4) → R17:reading-moved(overstated->partially-addressed)

section: How the evidence falls in time
text:
How the evidence falls in time
27 papers in the reviewed corpus bear on this problem, published 2008 to 2026. Progress and a fresh assertion of openness land in the same year.
This problem is recurrent: three or more papers spanning at least eight years assert it independently. Sustained restatement by authors who mostly do not cite each other is the strongest evidence this reading can offer that a gap is real rather than one group’s framing.
It is also being closed in pieces: partial results come from more than one paper in more than one year, each covering a different part.

title: No estimator is defensible as a default, and no study is required to show that its choice mattered
text:
Statement
The available estimators differ in what they assume rather than only in how they perform. Active-comparator new-user designs with regression or propensity adjustment handle baseline initiation and not treatment-confounder feedback. Matching gives a transparent population and discards information, with an estimand that is often left unstated. Marginal structural models represent regime effects directly and are unstable under extreme weights. The parametric g-formula supports flexible estimands and is sensitive to sequential outcome-model misspecification. G-estimation avoids modeling the treatment-free outcome distribution and is technically demanding. Longitudinal targeted learning is doubly robust and computationally heavy and sensitive to practical positivity. A study reporting one of these reports a number whose dependence on that choice is unknown, and nothing requires that at least one weighting, one outcome-modeling and one doubly robust estimator be compared on the same data.

title: No estimator is defensible as a default, and no study is required to show that its choice mattered
text:
Why it is open
Comparing estimators multiplies the analysis cost and can produce disagreement that the paper then has to explain, which is a strong disincentive. There is no accepted way to report disagreement between estimators: it is neither a sensitivity analysis in the usual sense nor a robustness check, since the estimators target the same estimand under different nuisance assumptions. Simulation evidence comparing them is also fragmented across papers with different generating mechanisms, so no synthesis exists that would justify a default.

title: No estimator is defensible as a default, and no study is required to show that its choice mattered
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Robins JM, Hernán MA, Brumback B. Marginal structural models and causal inference in epidemiology. Epidemiology 2000;11(5):550-560
The reference for weighted estimation of regime effects, one of the three families a comparison would have to include.


ltmle: Longitudinal Targeted Maximum Likelihood Estimation. CRAN
Implements longitudinal TMLE, IPTW and g-computation in one place, which makes the three-family comparison feasible in a single analysis.


lmtp: Non-Parametric Causal Effects of Feasible Interventions Based on Modified Treatment Policies. CRAN
Implements targeted and sequentially doubly robust estimators for point and longitudinal modified treatment policies.


Su L, et al. TrialEmulation: an R package to emulate target trials for causal analysis of observational time-to-event data. arXiv 2024
Provides the sequence-of-trials implementation with intention-to-treat and per-protocol analyses.

title: No estimator is defensible as a default, and no study is required to show that its choice mattered
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Require that every emulation compare at least one weighting method, one outcome-modeling method and one doubly robust method, document the causal estimand each actually targets, and report the three estimates together. Build a public benchmark with realistic observation processes and missingness on which the families can be compared under a common generating mechanism, so that the fragmented simulation evidence becomes a synthesis. Score methods on failure awareness as well as on bias and coverage: an estimator that returns a narrow interval in a deliberately non-identifiable scenario has failed the test that matters most.

title: No estimator is defensible as a default, and no study is required to show that its choice mattered

NoteA study is blocked

Within a fixed six-visit binary longitudinal data-generating mechanism, how often do the three named point-estimation implementations produce 36-month marginal risk differences whose within-replicate range exceeds 0.03 when they target the same sustained strategies? How do their bias, precision, coverage, output validity, and diagnostics behave under correct specification, joint misspecification, selective positive controls, practical overlap loss, and a composite hidden-variable identification failure?
