title: No estimator is defensible as a default, and no study is required to show that its choice mattered
text:
Verification

Verdict. Partially addressed. Auditors found the problem open. At least one qualified how it is stated; the qualification and who made it are in the trail below. Moved by the full-text reading: 16 findings from 16 papers naming work that covers part of this problem survived both the reader and an independent second reviewer, so the verdict moves from confirmed-open to partially-addressed. A further 159 findings in the same reading restate the problem as open; the two are consistent, and the part that is covered is named above.
Revised by the full-text reading. Applied full-text reading of the consolidated library.

Verdict changed

confirmed-open -> partially-addressed 16 surviving findings from: Addressing treatment switching in the ALTA-1L trial with g-m; An Empirical Method of Detecting Time-Dependent Confounding:; Applying the estimand and target trial frameworks to externa; Comparison of a Target Trial Emulation Framework vs Cox Regr; Developing an Interactive Online Guide to Support the Use of; Emulating a target trial of intensive nurse home visiting in; Evaluation of clinical utility in emulated clinical trials.; Exposure effects on count outcomes with observational data, ; Identifying a set that contains the best dynamic treatment r; Step-by-step causal analysis of EHRs to ground decision-maki; Target Trial Emulation Without Matching: A More Efficient Ap; Target trial emulation to assess real-world efficacy in the ; The Timing, the Treatment, the Question: Comparison of Epide; Using marginal structural models to adjust for treatment dro; [Methodological appraisal of statistical approaches to evalu; simcausal R Package: Conducting Transparent and Reproducible. New citations: 10.1001/jamanetworkopen.2022.34425, 10.1002/sim.7913, 10.1007/s10654-026-01385-3, 10.1093/aje/kwae023, 10.1093/biostatistics/kxv025, 10.1093/ije/dyac092, 10.1093/jnci/djad092, 10.1097/ede.0000000000001982, 10.1158/1055-9965.EPI-22-0495, 10.1186/s12874-024-02437-6, 10.1371/journal.pdig.0000721, 10.18637/jss.v081.i02, 10.25302/1.2020.me.13036031, 10.3389/fphar.2024.1223858, 10.3760/cma.j.cn121090-20250612-00284, 10.6000/1929-6029.2016.05.01.4


4 of the 4 independent auditors returned an opinion on this entry.

Literature and prior-art check

open / supported-with-caveat. The claim that no estimator is defensible as a default is well supported by the fragmentation the corpus shows, and the proposed remedy is partly in progress. Benchmarking of data-adaptive against investigator-specified confounding adjustment exists, and a 2026 evaluation compares statistical and deep learning methods for bias in a heart failure emulation. Neither supplies the public benchmark under a common generating mechanism that the entry asks for, and neither establishes a requirement that each study compare a weighting, an outcome-modelling and a doubly robust estimator. The overstatement is small: the entry’s implication that no comparative evidence exists is wrong, while its claim that no synthesis or requirement exists holds. Cites 10.1093/jamia/ocaf204: Benchmarks adjustment strategies against one another, which is the comparison the entry says is not done.. Cites 10.1038/s41467-026-74999-6: Compares statistical against deep learning estimation for bias within a single emulation, spanning two of the three families..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

not-a-problem / overstated. The absence of a universally preferred estimator is expected because estimator choice must follow the estimand, intervention, longitudinal structure, overlap and plausible nuisance assumptions. It is not itself a methodological defect, and a mandatory three-family comparison is neither necessary nor sufficient for validity. Alternative estimators are informative only when they genuinely target the same intervention, population, censoring handling and effect measure. Their disagreement is reasonably described as sensitivity to estimation assumptions, although it does not identify which estimate is correct; agreement can reflect shared identification failure. Several method summaries are too broad. Baseline active-comparator adjustment is inadequate for sustained per-protocol strategies with treatment-confounder feedback, but can be appropriate for a treatment-policy effect of initiation. Matching need not always discard observations, and its estimand depends on the matching design. The parametric g-formula models the longitudinal covariate and outcome law, not merely an outcome regression. Double robustness belongs to specified targeted estimators under stated nuisance conditions, not longitudinal targeted learning without qualification. TrialEmulation 0.0.4.11 is source-supported: its NAMESPACE exports trial_sequence and expand_trials, and its DESCRIPTION states that it estimates intention-to-treat and per-protocol effects. I abstain on the cited ltmle and lmtp capabilities because neither package is vendored under documentation/refs/packages/.

Grok 4.5, recency lens

open / supported. No estimator family is established as a default for longitudinal target-trial emulation of sustained strategies, and no current reporting or protocol standard requires a three-family comparison (weighting, outcome modeling, doubly robust) on the same data. Prior art that does not close the gap: (i) simulation comparisons of g-computation, IPTW/OW, and TMLE exist but are fragmented across data-generating mechanisms and often point-treatment or externally controlled trial settings (for example Schuler and Rose; Ren et al. 2023); (ii) software already makes multi-family analysis feasible (ltmle implements LTMLE, IPTW, and g-computation; lmtp implements sequential DR and related estimators; TrialEmulation covers sequence-of-trials ITT/PP), which lowers cost but does not create a requirement or a shared benchmark; (iii) TARGET 2025 (JAMA/BMJ) is a reporting guideline for target-trial emulations and does not mandate multi-estimator families; HARPER and STaRT-RWE structure protocols and sensitivity analyses without requiring weighting-plus-outcome-plus-DR comparison under a common estimand. No public continuous-time or informative-visit benchmark synthesizing the fragmented simulations was found. The problem’s claim about incentives against multi-estimator reporting remains accurate. Searches: comparing IPTW g-formula TMLE longitudinal target trial multi-method 2024 2025; TARGET checklist multiple estimators; HARPER STaRT-RWE sensitivity g-methods; Schuler Rose TMLE IPW g-computation.

GLM-5.2, third independent lens

open / supported-with-caveat. The claim is largely coherent and the reason given for openness (cost of comparison, no accepted reporting framework for disagreement, fragmented simulation evidence) genuinely supports it. However, the headline assertion ‘no estimator is defensible as a default’ is stronger than the body of the statement warrants. The body argues that estimators differ in assumptions and that no synthesis exists to justify a universal default, which is defensible. But ‘no estimator is defensible as a default’ could be read as claiming that in no specific setting is any estimator a reasonable default, which would be overstated—there are settings where, given known structure, one family is clearly preferred. The intended reading is that no single estimator is defensible as a universal default across the heterogeneous landscape of longitudinal causal problems, and on that reading the claim holds. The severity is proportionate: the cost of a wrong default estimator choice is a biased or unstable causal estimate presented without context.

Decision path

R5:default-open → R9:substantiated-overstatement(n=1/4):codex → R17:reading-moved(confirmed-open->partially-addressed)

title: Automated protocol translation can change the estimand while producing valid code
text: LRN-02 Confirmed open High priority Emerging Tractability 4/5

title: Automated protocol translation can change the estimand while producing valid code
text:
Statement
Systems now translate trial descriptions into cohort definitions or analysis code, and natural language processing extracts eligibility information from unstructured notes. The failure mode of these systems is not that they crash. It is that they silently substitute a different estimand: mistranslating a temporal condition, resolving an ambiguous eligibility phrase to the wrong operationalization, or emitting code that is syntactically valid and causally invalid. None of these failures is visible in the output, which is a working pipeline returning a plausible number. What is missing is a validation regime that treats generated code as an untrusted artifact rather than as a productivity gain.

title: Automated protocol translation can change the estimand while producing valid code
text:
Why it is open
Temporal logic is where these systems fail and where testing is hardest: the difference between treatment before eligibility assessment and treatment after it is one word in the specification and one join condition in the code, and both readings execute. There is no reference answer to test against, because the correct cohort is precisely what the pipeline was built to produce. Evaluating on downstream effect estimates is circular, since a wrong cohort with a plausible effect passes.

title: Automated protocol translation can change the estimand while producing valid code
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Kim, et al. From study design to executable code: automating target trial emulation with large language models. JAMIA Open 2026
Builds the translation from study design to executable emulation code, which is the system whose failure modes this problem concerns.


Wang, et al. An operational target trial emulation framework for causal inference using electronic health records. npj Digit Med 2026
Specifies the operational mapping from protocol component to record-level definition, which is the interface a compiler would have to respect.

title: Automated protocol translation can change the estimand while producing valid code
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Treat automation as a constrained compiler with three stages: a human-authored causal specification, a typed intermediate representation, and data-source-specific code generated from it. Require unit tests over synthetic test patients constructed so that each temporal condition has a patient that distinguishes the correct reading from the plausible wrong one, plus temporal-logic validation of the intermediate representation. Require dual human sign-off on the specification and on the generated cohort counts, and publish both, so the artifact under review is the specification rather than the number.

title: Automated protocol translation can change the estimand while producing valid code
text:
Verification

Verdict. Confirmed open. Auditors found the problem open. At least one qualified how it is stated; the qualification and who made it are in the trail below.
Dissent. literature dissented (supported): Automated translation from study design to executable emulation code exists, and agentic authoring of OMOP concept sets from natural language is now being attempted, so the systems the entry describes are real and multiplying. […]
4 of the 4 independent auditors returned an opinion on this entry.

Literature and prior-art check

open / supported. Automated translation from study design to executable emulation code exists, and agentic authoring of OMOP concept sets from natural language is now being attempted, so the systems the entry describes are real and multiplying. Nothing in the corpus supplies the validation regime the entry asks for: no typed intermediate representation, no temporal-logic validation, no synthetic test patients constructed to distinguish the correct reading of a temporal condition from the plausible wrong one, and no dual sign-off requirement. The gap between capability and validation is the claim, and the corpus shows only the capability half. Cites 10.1093/jamiaopen/ooag131: Builds the translation the entry is concerned about, which establishes the capability without supplying the validation.. Cites 10.64898/2026.06.02.26354704: Extends automation to phenotype definition, which is the component where a silent error changes the cohort..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / overstated. Executable code can silently change eligibility, time zero, assignment, follow-up, or the resulting estimand, so the core risk is real. However, it is false that such errors are necessarily invisible or that no reference answer can exist. Independently authored specifications, expert-labeled records, hand-coded reference implementations, differential testing, and synthetic boundary-case patients can provide component-level or end-to-end reference answers. The report’s own proposed synthetic-patient tests contradict the categorical no-reference-answer claim. Agreement of a downstream effect estimate is insufficient evidence of semantic correctness, but evaluating against an external randomized benchmark is not literally circular. Typed intermediate representations and temporal tests reduce risk without proving semantic equivalence for every real-world mapping. No package capability claim is present.

Grok 4.5, recency lens

open / supported. Kim et al. (JAMIA Open 2026; THESEUS) and Wang et al. (npj Digit Med 2026) build or specify automated protocol-to-code and operational EHR mappings; they are the systems whose silent estimand-shift risk the problem names, not fixes of that risk. Lee et al. (JMIR Med Inform 2025) validate LLM-generated trial-criteria queries for functional correctness, which is partial operational testing but not temporal-logic unit tests that distinguish treatment-before versus treatment-after eligibility. Girshovitz, Zeltzer, and Gilad-Bachrach (arXiv:2607.21173, 2026) propose ARA: structured protocol intermediate form, SCM synthetic failure scenarios, and adversarial validation so that silent success is replaced by visible protocol or diagnostic failure. That is closely aligned with the report direction, yet it is a proposal with a small econometric-style benchmark; it does not establish a standard validation regime for TTE automation, dual human sign-off on specification and cohort counts, or synthetic patients that isolate each temporal join. Guidance (TARGET 2025 reporting; FDA/EMA RWE documents) addresses transparency of human-designed emulations, not untrusted machine-generated code. No CRAN or GitHub merge was found that ships a constrained TTE compiler with temporal unit tests. Silent estimand substitution under syntactically valid pipelines remains open.

GLM-5.2, third independent lens

open / supported. The claim is internally consistent and correctly identifies the silent estimand substitution as a structural risk in automated translation. The reasons given for it being open (lack of reference answers, circularity of downstream evaluation) strongly support the claim. The scope is appropriate and the severity is proportionate to the cost of a wrong estimand.

Decision path

R5:default-open → R9:substantiated-overstatement(n=1/4):codex

title: Subgroup effects are estimated where overlap is worst, and the groups with worst overlap are often the protected ones
text: LRN-04 Partially addressed High priority Promising Tractability 4/5

title: Subgroup effects are estimated where overlap is worst, and the groups with worst overlap are often the protected ones
text:
Statement
Causal forests and meta-learners estimate heterogeneous treatment effects, and they inherit every identification assumption of the base analysis without relaxing any of them. Subgroup discovery adds three specific hazards: confounding that varies by subgroup, multiplicity across the many subgroups a flexible learner implicitly examines, and limited overlap within small strata. Apparent heterogeneity can therefore reflect differential measurement, differential healthcare access or model extrapolation rather than differential biology. The distributional problem is that the groups with the least data and the poorest overlap are frequently the protected groups whose effects the analysis was undertaken to examine, so the least reliable estimates carry the most weight in interpretation.

title: Subgroup effects are estimated where overlap is worst, and the groups with worst overlap are often the protected ones
text:
Why it is open
Overlap within a subgroup is a property of the data that cannot be improved by a better estimator, and restricting to regions with adequate overlap changes which subgroups can be reported at all. Distinguishing effect modification from differential measurement requires validation data within each subgroup, which is rarer where the subgroup is smaller. Honest sample splitting costs precision in exactly the strata that are already imprecise.

title: Subgroup effects are estimated where overlap is worst, and the groups with worst overlap are often the protected ones
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Feuerriegel S, Frauen D, Melnychuk V, et al. Causal machine learning for predicting treatment outcomes. Nat Med 2024;30:958-968
States that causal machine learning supports individualized effect estimation only under the same identification assumptions as conventional methods, which is the constraint subgroup analyses routinely ignore.


Target trial emulation under nonmutually exclusive assignment. Am J Epidemiol 2026;195(4):1045
Shows overlap defeating advanced adjustment, which is the mechanism by which a subgroup estimate fails.

title: Subgroup effects are estimated where overlap is worst, and the groups with worst overlap are often the protected ones
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Use honest sample splitting, restrict conditional effect estimation to regions with adequate overlap, and apply hierarchical shrinkage across subgroups so that small strata borrow rather than assert. Report subgroup-specific data support, calibration and uncertainty next to every subgroup effect, so that a wide, poorly supported estimate cannot be read as a finding. Evaluate not only whether benefit varies across groups but whether the emulation’s assumptions vary across them, since differential measurement and differential access are alternative explanations for the same pattern.

title: Subgroup effects are estimated where overlap is worst, and the groups with worst overlap are often the protected ones
text:
Verification

Verdict. Partially addressed. Part of this problem is addressed by existing work; the entry names which part.
4 of the 4 independent auditors returned an opinion on this entry.

Literature and prior-art check

partially-solved / supported-with-caveat. Subgroup estimation inside emulations is being done carefully in places the entry does not credit. A 2026 European Journal of Epidemiology paper extends a CONFIRM emulation to subgroups explicitly, a 2026 Alzheimer’s and Dementia paper estimates heterogeneous statin effects on dementia with causal machine learning inside an emulation, and a 2026 Epidemiology paper nests a target study within a target trial specifically to evaluate intervention effects on disparities, which is the equity question the entry raises. What remains is the reporting requirement: none of these establishes that subgroup-specific data support and calibration must be reported alongside every subgroup effect, and none tests whether the emulation’s assumptions differ across groups. Cites 10.1097/ede.0000000000002024: Provides a framework for the equity question the entry raises, within the emulation setting.. Cites 10.1007/s10654-026-01379-1: A worked subgroup extension of an emulation, showing the practice exists.. Cites 10.1002/alz.71178: Applies causal machine learning for heterogeneity inside an emulation, which is the combination the entry describes as hazardous..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / overstated. Conditional and subgroup effects require the relevant consistency, conditional exchangeability, and positivity conditions within the target subgroups; flexible estimators do not create missing support. However, multiplicity is specifically a problem when adaptively discovered subgroups or contrasts are selected and interpreted inferentially, not an automatic defect of every conditional-effect estimator. Whether protected groups have the poorest overlap is an empirical, dataset-specific claim that must be demonstrated rather than presumed. Validation data are one way to distinguish effect modification from differential measurement, but the categorical requirement is too strong because additional measurement models or identifying assumptions may also be used. Honest estimation, shrinkage, and overlap restriction can improve inference, but shrinkage does not restore identification and restriction changes the target population. Causal-effect calibration is also not directly observable and must be defined through identifiable group-level contrasts or external validation. No package capability claim is present.

Grok 4.5, recency lens

open / supported-with-caveat. Feuerriegel et al. (2024) again bind individualized causal ML to classical identification assumptions; that supports the problem’s premise without solving subgroup practice. Tools already recommended in the agenda exist in partial form: honest sample splitting in causal forests (Wager and Athey lineage), propensity trimming and common-support restriction, and various hierarchical or shrinkage approaches to unstable strata. Recent applied causal-forest work still documents poor within-stratum overlap and relies on post hoc trimming (e.g., 2025 Scientific Reports-style pipelines). What remains open is the joint operational problem the statement names: subgroup and protected-group HTE is often the scientific target; those strata systematically have the worst overlap and measurement quality; and there is no adopted standard that reports subgroup-specific data support, calibration, and differential assumption plausibility next to every CATE so that a poorly supported protected-group estimate cannot be read as a finding. Overlap is a data property no estimator repairs. Fairness-aware HTE and group-bias CATE work is active on arXiv and conference tracks but has not certified subgroup effects under differential access and measurement. Status remains open; the caveat is that honesty, trimming, and shrinkage are available components, not a field solution to protected-stratum extrapolation.

GLM-5.2, third independent lens

open / supported. The claim is internally consistent and correctly identifies that overlap is a property of the data that cannot be fixed by the estimator, and that this disproportionately affects protected groups. The reasons given for it being open logically support the claim. The scope and severity are proportionate to the real-world cost of misinterpreting subgroup effects.

Decision path

R3:partially-solved(n=1/4) → R9:substantiated-overstatement(n=1/4):codex

title: Phenotypes enter emulations as error-free binary variables
text: MER-01 Partially addressed Very high priority Promising Tractability 4/5

title: Phenotypes enter emulations as error-free binary variables
text:
Statement
Prescriptions differ from dispensings and dispensings differ from ingestion; diagnostic codes differ from clinical events; death and care received outside the system may be incompletely captured. Methods for outcome misclassification in electronic health records increasingly use validation samples and probabilistic phenotypes. Emulation pipelines almost universally do not: a phenotype is thresholded to a binary variable at the start and treated as truth thereafter. Differential misclassification then interacts with weighting and with time-varying confounding in ways that are not intuitive, because an error in the exposure at one time propagates into the weights at every later time, and no standard analysis propagates the phenotype uncertainty at all.

title: Phenotypes enter emulations as error-free binary variables
text:
Why it is open
The interaction is genuinely nonlinear: misclassification in a time-varying confounder both biases the weight and changes which patients are censored, so the bias does not decompose into a measurement part and a confounding part. Validation samples that would calibrate the phenotype are usually convenience samples from one site, and transporting a sensitivity and specificity across sites is itself an untested transport claim. Propagating uncertainty end to end also requires the whole pipeline to accept probabilistic inputs, which most implementations cannot.

title: Phenotypes enter emulations as error-free binary variables
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Wang, et al. An operational target trial emulation framework for causal inference using electronic health records. npj Digit Med 2026
Describes validation-sample and probabilistic phenotype approaches to outcome misclassification in record-based studies.


Benz L, et al. Adjusting for selection bias due to missing eligibility criteria in emulated target trials. Am J Epidemiol 2025
Shows the shape of a validation-anchored correction for one protocol component, which is the template a phenotype correction would follow.

title: Phenotypes enter emulations as error-free binary variables
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Develop validation-subsample targeted learning, Bayesian latent-class g-formula models and pipelines that accept probabilistic treatment and outcome nodes rather than thresholded ones, so phenotype uncertainty is propagated to the final interval rather than discarded at the first step. Simulate sensitivity and specificity from 0.70 to 0.99 with differential misclassification odds ratios from 1 to 4, and report the bias in the estimated regime effect rather than in the phenotype, since the phenotype’s accuracy is not what the study claims. Establish how large a validation sample has to be before the correction is worth its variance cost.

title: Phenotypes enter emulations as error-free binary variables
text:

NoteA study is designed

Literature and prior-art check

Searching for phenotype uncertainty propagated through an emulation returned discussions of misclassification as a listed threat and no pipeline that accepts probabilistic treatment or outcome nodes and carries the uncertainty to the final interval. Design-bias reviews name outcome misclassification among the biases to avoid without supplying the propagation. GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / overstated. The underlying joint longitudinal measurement-error problem is real, but several assertions are too categorical. Prescribing, dispensing, and ingestion are distinct variables; their difference is misclassification only when the estimand targets one but the protocol measures another. In a cumulative inverse-probability weight, an erroneous treatment factor at time s remains in later cumulative products for a clone still at risk, but a clone artificially censored at s has no later weights. Mismeasurement of a time-varying confounder changes artificial-censoring membership only when that variable determines the dynamic strategy, eligibility, or censoring rule; under a static sustained strategy it can distort nuisance models without changing who is censored. The resulting biases can interact, but the defensible claim is that no unique identified additive measurement-versus-confounding decomposition generally exists without additional assumptions, not that no decomposition is possible. End-to-end propagation also does not require every estimator to accept soft inputs natively: multiple imputation, posterior draws, or a whole-pipeline bootstrap can wrap deterministic estimators. No package is named, so the claims about ‘almost universally,’ ‘no standard analysis,’ and ‘most implementations’ cannot be established from package ground truth. TrialEmulation 0.0.4.11 confirms one indicator-based implementation, not the asserted prevalence. The narrowed problem remains open, while uniformly assigning very-high severity is unjustified because importance depends on the estimand, error mechanism, validation information, and decision sensitivity.

Grok 4.5, recency lens

open / supported-with-caveat. Inverted prior: searched for an end-to-end solution that lets sustained-strategy or time-varying TTE pipelines take probabilistic (non-thresholded) treatment, confounder, and outcome phenotypes and propagate differential misclassification through weights and censoring into the regime-effect interval. Nothing retrieved closes that full claim.


Own citations first. Wang et al. (npj Digit Med 2026; 10.1038/s41746-026-02563-z) is an operational TTE framework paper. Available text describes validation samples and probabilistic or uncertainty-aware outcome models as tools that can account for measurement error, and separately reviews g-methods for sustained strategies. It does not deliver a validated pipeline that accepts probabilistic treatment and outcome nodes end to end, nor simulations of regime-effect bias under differential time-varying misclassification. Description of existing pieces is not resolution. Benz et al. (Am J Epidemiol 2025; 10.1093/aje/kwae471; arXiv:2406.16830) targets selection bias from missing eligibility criteria via IPW under an MAR-type assumption for eligibility ascertainment. It is a useful template for validation-anchored IPW on one protocol component; it is not phenotype measurement-error correction for time-varying exposure or confounders.
Component prior art (does not close the stated gap). Hubbard, Tong, Duan, Chen (Epidemiology 2020; 10.1097/EDE.0000000000001193) give a hand-computable bias correction for continuous EHR probabilistic outcome phenotypes in association studies. Scope is outcome misclassification and association parameters, not time-varying treatment weights or sustained regimes. Edwards et al. (Am J Epidemiol 2018; 10.1093/aje/kwy028) fold sensitivity analysis for cause-of-death misclassification into the parametric g-formula; that is quantitative bias analysis, not identification with validation-anchored probabilistic nodes. Edwards et al. (RIME; PubMed 31971584, 2020) reparameterize imputation for exposure misclassification with validation data and illustrate combination with IPW for hazard ratios and risks: point-exposure misclassification with IPW, not full longitudinal differential error in exposure, confounders, and outcomes under dynamic or sustained strategies. Nab et al. (Epidemiology 2020) quantify bias from a misclassified confounder in MSM-IPW; characterization and QBA, not a solved TTE pipeline. Lu et al. (J Biomed Inform 2024; 10.1016/j.jbi.2024.104690) leverage multiple error-prone algorithm phenotypes plus a small validation set for risk-factor associations: again association, not TTE g-methods.
Material that strengthens openness. Ross, Cole, et al. (Epidemiology 2024; 35(2):196–207) document challenges of transporting measurement-error parameters (sensitivity, specificity, and related bias parameters) from external validation data: this supports the report’s claim that Se/Sp transport across sites is itself an untested or fragile transport claim, not a solved step.
Software (CRAN/GitHub scan). TrialEmulation, gfoRmula, gfoRmulaICE, lmtp, ltmle, survtmle, WeightIt, MatchIt, cobalt, ipw, adjustedCurves, riskRegression, and related Python stacks (zEpid, causallib, lifelines, scikit-survival) remain binary or continuous node pipelines for treatment and outcome after analyst thresholding. CRAN’s causal-inference task view points measurement-error tooling to sensitivity packages (e.g., episensr, EValue), not first-class probabilistic phenotype inputs inside sequential TTE or g-formula estimation. No merged PR or release note retrieved that closes end-to-end phenotype uncertainty in these packages through 2025–2026.
Queries run (representative): Wang operational TTE DOI and Nature page/PDF; Benz kwae471/arXiv; “probabilistic phenotype” + causal/IPTW/g-formula/lmtp/ltmle/TTE 2023–2026; measurement error misclassification + MSM-IPW / g-formula / time-varying / sustained strategy; Hubbard probabilistic phenotypes; Edwards RIME and g-formula misclassification; Ross transporting measurement error; CRAN/GitHub TrialEmulation gfoRmula lmtp measurement error; TARGET/ENCePP/FDA RWE measurement error guidance cross-check. Journals and preprint venues searched via web for 2024–2026 hits on those terms.
Caveat on support: the entry is faithful that standard TTE pipelines threshold phenotypes and that the nonlinear interaction of differential time-varying misclassification with weighting and censoring is not handled end to end. It would be overstated only if read as “no methods exist for any piece of phenotype error.” Pieces exist (outcome probabilistic correction in associations; exposure misclassification with IPW; g-formula outcome SA; transport problems formalized). None of those pieces, alone or as packaged software, solves the problem as stated for sustained-strategy emulation with uncertainty carried to the final interval.

GLM-5.2, third independent lens

open / supported. The statement correctly identifies a methodological gap in target trial emulation using EHR data. It asserts that standard pipelines threshold phenotypes and do not propagate uncertainty, which is a claim about current practice rather than a structural impossibility. The reasoning given for it being open (nonlinear interaction of misclassification, transportability of validation samples, pipeline architecture limitations) is internally consistent and supports the claim being open. The scope is appropriate for a methodological research agenda, and the severity is proportionate to the risk of biased causal estimates.

Decision path

R5:default-open → R7:counter-and-support-both-present(support=1/counter=1) → R17:reading-moved(unverifiable->partially-addressed)

title: Censoring at death is applied as data cleaning rather than as an identifying assumption
text: OUT-01 Partially addressed High priority Established Tractability 4/5

title: Censoring at death is applied as data cleaning rather than as an identifying assumption
text:
Statement
Death, treatment discontinuation and competing clinical events change what an outcome contrast means. ICH E9(R1) requires that intercurrent events be handled explicitly, and the causal competing-risks literature distinguishes total effects, controlled direct effects and separable effects, each answering a different question. Applied emulations nonetheless default to cause-specific hazards or censor competing events without matching the estimator to the causal question, and recurrent and terminal events are seldom modeled jointly. The step where an analyst censors follow-up at death is an identifying decision that selects among these estimands, and it is normally executed silently inside data preparation, where no reviewer sees it as a decision at all.

title: Censoring at death is applied as data cleaning rather than as an identifying assumption
text:
Why it is open
The estimands differ in what they assume rather than in what they fit, so a wrong choice produces a well-behaved analysis of the wrong quantity and nothing downstream flags it. Separable effects require decomposing a treatment into components whose separate effects are meaningful, which is a substantive claim about the drug that most applied settings cannot support. Recurrent-event and terminal-event models are available but their combination with sustained-strategy emulation is not worked out, so the analyst choosing correctly on competing risks may have no estimator for the regime they wanted.

title: Censoring at death is applied as data cleaning rather than as an identifying assumption
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




ICH E9(R1) addendum on estimands and sensitivity analysis in clinical trials
Requires explicit specification of the strategy for each intercurrent event, which is the discipline that the emulation literature has not yet inherited.


lmtp: Non-Parametric Causal Effects of Feasible Interventions Based on Modified Treatment Policies. CRAN
Supports censored outcomes and competing risks for modified treatment policies, one of the few implementations where the competing event is part of the estimand rather than a preprocessing step.

title: Censoring at death is applied as data cleaning rather than as an identifying assumption
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Prespecify the estimand as a cumulative incidence, a restricted mean event-free time or a recurrent-event contrast, and name the intercurrent-event strategy for each competing event before the analysis. Compare multistate g-computation, joint frailty models, separable effects and recurrent-event targeted learning on data generated with a known competing-event structure, so the cost of the default is measured rather than asserted. Require that any censoring at a competing event be justified in the protocol as an identifying choice, with the estimand it implies stated, which turns a data-cleaning line into a reviewable claim.

title: Censoring at death is applied as data cleaning rather than as an identifying assumption
text:
Verification

Verdict. Partially addressed. Part of this problem is addressed by existing work; the entry names which part.
Dissent. literature dissented (open): The methodological apparatus the entry asks for exists further than it allows. A 2026 Journal of Epidemiology paper treats causal inference from time-to-event data with dependent censoring, confounding and competing events together, and a 2025 Journal of Clinical Epidemiology paper works a trial emulation with competing risks in a surgical application. […]
4 of the 4 independent auditors returned an opinion on this entry.

Literature and prior-art check

open / supported-with-caveat. The methodological apparatus the entry asks for exists further than it allows. A 2026 Journal of Epidemiology paper treats causal inference from time-to-event data with dependent censoring, confounding and competing events together, and a 2025 Journal of Clinical Epidemiology paper works a trial emulation with competing risks in a surgical application. The entry’s claim is nonetheless about practice rather than method: that applied emulations default to cause-specific hazards or censor at competing events without matching the estimator to the question, and that censoring at death is executed inside data preparation. Nothing in the corpus contradicts that, and the reporting requirement the entry proposes does not exist. Cites 10.2188/jea.je20250662: Handles the three complications jointly, which is the analysis the entry says is not worked out.. Cites 10.1016/j.jclinepi.2025.111714: A worked emulation in which competing risks are part of the design rather than a preprocessing step..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

partially-solved / overstated. The central warning is valid and potentially high severity: handling death or another intercurrent event is part of defining the estimand, and total, controlled direct, and separable effects answer different questions. The entry is nevertheless conceptually imprecise. An estimand is defined by its counterfactual outcomes and contrast; identification assumptions are separate. Simply censoring at death does not select or identify one of those causal effects. Depending on the analysis, it can instead produce a cause-specific risk-set quantity or an unidentified hypothetical contrast. The claims that censoring is normally silent and that recurrent and terminal events are seldom modeled jointly are empirical frequency claims not established by the cited package source. Pinned lmtp source exports lmtp_tmle, lmtp_sdr, and lmtp_survival; accepts longitudinal treatment, censoring, and competing-risk nodes; incorporates competing-event status in its recursion; and tests two treatment times with two competing-risk times. Pinned gfoRmula source exports gformula_survival and static and implements sustained intervention risks with an explicit competing-event model and an option governing whether that event is treated as censoring. These implementations address competing risks under longitudinal strategies, but neither exposes an explicit joint recurrent-event and terminal-event estimand. The narrower implementation and protocol gap therefore remains. Cites CRAN:lmtp@1.5.4: The pinned NAMESPACE exports lmtp_tmle, lmtp_sdr, and lmtp_survival. The source accepts treatment variables ordered over time together with censoring and competing-risk indicators, and its fidelity test applies repeated treatment and competing-risk nodes. This supplies estimators for cumulative incidence under longitudinal treatment policies, but not an explicit joint recurrent-terminal contrast.. Cites CRAN:gfoRmula@1.1.1: The pinned NAMESPACE exports gformula_survival and static. The source models competing events and implements never-treat and always-treat interventions across follow-up, resolving ordinary sustained-strategy competing-risk estimation while leaving explicit recurrent-terminal estimands unaddressed..

Grok 4.5, recency lens

partially-solved / supported-with-caveat. Inverted-prior search shows the methodological core of OUT-01 is older and better equipped than a pure ‘open’ label implies, while the applied silence problem remains. Young, Stensrud, Tchetgen Tchetgen and Hernán (2020) already formalize that treating a competing event as censoring selects a controlled-direct-effect style question rather than a total-effect cumulative incidence, so the ‘identifying assumption vs data cleaning’ distinction is settled in the causal competing-risks literature. Software already embeds that choice for sustained or feasible longitudinal interventions: gfoRmula documents explicit options for competing events under time-varying treatment strategies, and lmtp implements time-to-event outcomes with competing risks for modified treatment policies, including a later ‘total effect’ option in version 1.5.0 (citing Díaz, Hoffman and Hejazi). Janvin, Young, Ryalen and Stensrud (2024) formalize causal estimands for recurrent events with and without a terminal competing event. None of that fully closes OUT-01 as stated. Applied primers still describe censor-at-death plus Fine-Gray sensitivity as common practice (Terman et al., 2025). ICH E9(R1) still governs trials more tightly than routine emulation protocols; TARGET (2025) improves TTE reporting generally but does not by itself force an intercurrent-event strategy for death the way E9(R1) does for trials. Separable effects remain a substantive product claim, not a software switch. Joint recurrent-plus-terminal estimation under longitudinal confounding is advancing (Prosepe et al., 2025 multistate g-computation; D’Alessio et al., 2026 arXiv g-computation for recurrent and semi-competing events with time-varying actions) but those are method papers and proposals, not field-wide defaults or head-to-head evaluations of multistate g-computation, joint frailty, separable effects and recurrent-event targeted learning on a known competing-event DGP. Net: estimator and formal estimand machinery for competing death under many sustained strategies exist; silent preprocessing and incomplete recurrent/terminal tooling keep the problem only partially solved. Queries run included competing risks/censoring at death in target trial emulation; intercurrent events in RWE/TTE; separable effects software; multistate g-computation sustained strategies; lmtp/gfoRmula/gfoRmulaICE NEWS and CRAN; TARGET 2025 checklist coverage; arXiv/medRxiv 2024–2026; Janvin recurrent competing; Díaz LMTP competing risks. Cites doi:10.1002/sim.8471: Makes explicit that defining competing events as censoring is an identifying choice among total, controlled direct and related counterfactual estimands, not a neutral cleaning step; this is the conceptual backbone of OUT-01.. Cites doi:10.1007/s10985-023-09606-7: Provides identification and estimation for survival under competing risks with longitudinal modified treatment policies, so competing death is part of the estimand rather than only a preprocessing censor code for feasible sustained-style interventions.. Cites cran:lmtp: Released R software that natively supports time-to-event outcomes with competing risks for MTPs/dynamic rules; NEWS for 1.5.0 adds estimation of the total effect under competing risks, reducing the incentive to censor death before fitting.. Cites doi:10.1016/j.patter.2020.100008: Implements parametric g-formula for sustained treatment strategies with documented options for handling competing events, covering the sustained-strategy case the agenda flags as missing when analysts stay inside cause-specific Cox pipelines.. Cites doi:10.1007/s10985-023-09594-8: Formalizes several causal estimands for recurrent event settings with and without competing terminal events, partially addressing the report’s claim that recurrent and terminal structure is not worked out at the estimand level.. Cites doi:10.1002/sim.70061: Combines multistate models with g-computation for causal effects of treatment-delay strategies, showing multistate g-computation for longitudinal treatment timing is an active, published method stream rather than a blank spot.. Cites arxiv:2603.10169: Proposes g-computation algorithms for time-varying actions with recurrent and semi-competing events; progress on the exact joint structure OUT-01 says is missing, but still a method proposal rather than a completed evaluation suite or standard package default.. Cites doi:10.3389/fphar.2024.1223858: Shows joint use of ICH-style estimands (including intercurrent-event strategies) with target trial emulation in observational external-control work, partial inheritance of E9(R1) discipline into emulation design..

GLM-5.2, third independent lens

open / supported. The statement is internally consistent and proportionate. It accurately characterizes a well-known methodological tension in causal inference and target trial emulation: handling competing events (like death) via censoring during data preparation implicitly imposes an identifying assumption and selects an estimand, often without explicit protocol-level justification. The reason given for the problem being open—that estimands differ in their assumptions and a mismatched choice yields a well-behaved but wrong analysis without downstream flags—logically supports the assertion that this remains an open issue in applied practice. The scope is appropriate, addressing current applied practice rather than asserting a structural impossibility.

Decision path

R3:partially-solved(n=2/4) → R9:substantiated-overstatement(n=1/4):codex

title: No decomposition separates scientific-target mismatch from protocol compromise, mapping loss and estimation error
text: PRO-01 Overstated High priority Emerging Tractability 3/5

title: No decomposition separates scientific-target mismatch from protocol compromise, mapping loss and estimation error
text:
Statement
Three trials are in play in any emulation and only one of them is usually named. There is the ideal trial that would answer the decision-maker’s question, the target trial that the investigator specifies, and the emulation the data actually support. Specifying the target trial closely around the available data conceals the distance between the first two, and the paper reports a single estimate as though the chain were tight. What does not exist is a decomposition of the total discrepancy into its four transitions: from the ideal estimand to the feasible target estimand, from that to the identified observed-data functional, and from that to the estimator’s output. Without one, a reader cannot tell whether a surprising result reflects estimation error or the fact that the question quietly changed at the first step.

title: No decomposition separates scientific-target mismatch from protocol compromise, mapping loss and estimation error
text:
Why it is open
The first transition is a change of scientific question rather than a statistical error, so it has no sampling distribution and no obvious metric. Any measure of distance between estimands requires a common space in which to compare an intervention that was never implementable with one that was, and that space has to be constructed rather than estimated. The incentives also run the wrong way: making the drift explicit weakens the paper’s claim without changing its number, so nothing but a reporting requirement would make anyone do it.

title: No decomposition separates scientific-target mismatch from protocol compromise, mapping loss and estimation error
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Moreno-Betancur M, Wijesuriya R, Carlin JB. The ideal trial: defining causal estimands that balance relevance and feasibility in target trial emulations and actual randomized trials. Epidemiology 2026;37(2):153-162
Distinguishes ideal, target and actual trials and argues that every discrepancy between them should be made explicit. It frames the problem and does not supply the decomposition.


Hernán MA, Robins JM. Using big data to emulate a target trial when a randomized trial is not available. Am J Epidemiol 2016;183(8):758-764
Establishes the target trial as the object to be specified, which is the middle term of the three and the only one the framework requires be written down.


Hansford HJ, et al. Design and implementation of observational studies emulating a target trial. JAMA Netw Open 2026
Design guidance for the operational steps, acknowledging that the operational methods remain scenario dependent.

title: No decomposition separates scientific-target mismatch from protocol compromise, mapping loss and estimation error
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Define an estimand lineage that records each transition as a formal change in population, treatment version, outcome definition or follow-up, and require it in the protocol so it is written before the estimate exists. Quantify estimand distance through differences in intervention support and in target-population composition, which are computable from the data at hand and do not require the ideal trial to be feasible. Report the lineage next to the estimate so a reader can see which step is carrying the assumption load.

title: No decomposition separates scientific-target mismatch from protocol compromise, mapping loss and estimation error
text:
Verification

Verdict. Overstated. 2 independent auditors judged the claim as stated too strong. Emulations should separately document changes from the decision question to the operational causal estimand, the assumptions mapping that estimand to an observed-data functional, and estimation uncertainty. This lineage need not form an additive numerical decomposition when populations, interventions, outcomes, or scales differ.
Dissent. literature dissented (supported-with-caveat): The framing is now published rather than a preprint: the ideal-trial paper the entry cites as arXiv 2405.10026 appeared in Epidemiology in 2026, and the entry should cite the journal version. […]
4 of the 4 independent auditors returned an opinion on this entry.

Literature and prior-art check

open / supported-with-caveat. The framing is now published rather than a preprint: the ideal-trial paper the entry cites as arXiv 2405.10026 appeared in Epidemiology in 2026, and the entry should cite the journal version. A 2026 American Journal of Epidemiology paper sets out the anatomy of a causal estimand for population health research, which is the vocabulary a lineage would be written in. Neither supplies the decomposition the entry asks for: a formal accounting that attributes total discrepancy across the four transitions, with a computable measure of estimand distance. The claim survives with its citation corrected and its neighbors named. Cites 10.1097/ede.0000000000001933: The peer-reviewed version of the framing the entry cites as a preprint. The entry’s citation should move to this.. Cites 10.1093/aje/kwag079: Decomposes a causal estimand into its parts, which is the representation an estimand lineage would build on..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / overstated. A structured estimand lineage is a defensible reporting objective, but the proposed decomposition is not mathematically defined. The statement names four objects but enumerates only three transitions. Under valid identification, the observed-data functional equals the target causal estimand and is not a separate loss term. If identification assumptions fail, the resulting causal bias is generally not identified from the same data. Effects defined using different populations, interventions, outcomes, or scales also have no canonical additive distance. Differences in intervention support or population composition neither decompose nor necessarily bound the difference between effects without bridge and effect-heterogeneity assumptions. This is therefore an open reporting and formalization item, not a universally available decomposition whose absence prevents interpretation, and its asserted high severity is inflated.

Grok 4.5, recency lens

open / supported. Inverted prior: searched for a formal four-step discrepancy decomposition (ideal→target→identified functional→estimator) in TTE. Own prior_work (Moreno-Betancur arXiv:2405.10026) frames ideal/target/actual trials and urges explicit discrepancies but does not supply a quantitative decomposition of total discrepancy into scientific-target mismatch, mapping loss, and estimation error. Hernán–Robins 2016 and Hansford 2026 are design/guidance, not decomposition. Searches for estimand lineage, estimand distance, and four-transition decomposition in AJE/Epidemiology/IJE/Sim/BMJ/JAMA and arXiv 2024–2026 returned framing and reporting proposals (ICH E9(R1), TARGET) but no operational metric or software that separates those four transitions. Still open as stated.

GLM-5.2, third independent lens

open / overstated. The claim asserts that a decomposition ‘does not exist,’ which wears the language of impossibility. However, the reason given for it being open notes that the common space required for comparison ‘has to be constructed rather than estimated,’ implying that the decomposition is structurally possible but simply has not been developed or standardized in current practice. The claim is thus a statement about the current state of the field framed as an absolute.

Decision path

R5:default-open → R8:overstated-majority(n=2/4)

title: Registrations record the final protocol and not the alternatives that were rejected
text: PRO-03 Partially addressed High priority Promising Tractability 4/5

title: Registrations record the final protocol and not the alternatives that were rejected
text:
Statement
An emulation makes many defensible decisions: active comparator, washout period, time zero, grace period, how treatment episodes are constructed, censoring rules, follow-up length and outcome definition. Each has more than one reasonable answer, and the set of answers is the researcher’s degrees of freedom. Design guidance now exists and states plainly that the operational methods remain scenario dependent, which means the guidance narrows the set without closing it. Registrations, where they exist, record only the specification that was finally run; they do not record the alternatives considered, the order in which decisions were made, or which decisions were revised after the data were inspected. A reader therefore cannot distinguish a protocol written once from one converged upon.

title: Registrations record the final protocol and not the alternatives that were rejected
text:
Why it is open
The information that would settle it is destroyed rather than merely unrecorded: once a decision log is not kept, no later audit can reconstruct it, and there is no artifact to demand. Registration systems were designed for randomized trials, where the protocol precedes the data, and have no natural slot for a design that is necessarily developed against an existing dataset. Requiring a full multiverse imposes a cost proportional to the number of decisions, which for a longitudinal emulation is large, so the honest practice is also the expensive one.

title: Registrations record the final protocol and not the alternatives that were rejected
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Hansford HJ, et al. Design and implementation of observational studies emulating a target trial. JAMA Netw Open 2026
Sets out the design decisions and acknowledges that operational methods remain scenario dependent, which is the residual this problem names.


Cashin AG, Hansford HJ, Hernán MA, et al. Transparent reporting of observational studies emulating a target trial: the TARGET statement. JAMA 2025;334(12):1084
A 21-item checklist covering what the study did. It reports the final specification and is explicitly a reporting rather than a design instrument.

title: Registrations record the final protocol and not the alternatives that were rejected
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Require version-controlled protocols, dated decision logs and outcome-blinded feasibility reports, so that the chronology of decisions is an artifact rather than a memory. Prespecify a primary emulation plus a principled design multiverse over the decisions known to move estimates, and report the distribution rather than the chosen point. Hash the executable specification before outcome analysis, which makes the claim of prespecification checkable by a third party instead of taken on trust.

title: Registrations record the final protocol and not the alternatives that were rejected
text:
Verification

Verdict. Partially addressed. Auditors found the problem open. At least one qualified how it is stated; the qualification and who made it are in the trail below. Moved by the full-text reading: 3 findings from 3 papers naming work that covers part of this problem survived both the reader and an independent second reviewer, so the verdict moves from confirmed-open to partially-addressed. A further 15 findings in the same reading restate the problem as open; the two are consistent, and the part that is covered is named above.
Dissent. literature dissented (supported): Nothing in the corpus records a decision log, a dated chronology of design choices, or the alternatives rejected during protocol development. […]
Revised by the full-text reading. Applied full-text reading of the consolidated library.

Verdict changed

confirmed-open -> partially-addressed 3 surviving findings from: Illustrating an Adaptive Prespecification Framework for Obse; Improving the validity of noninterventional comparative effe; Transparency in real-world evidence (RWE) studies to build c. New citations: 10.1093/aje/kwae317, 10.1097/ede.0000000000001901, 10.1111/dom.13918

Literature and prior-art check

open / supported. Nothing in the corpus records a decision log, a dated chronology of design choices, or the alternatives rejected during protocol development. Quality-assessment tools for observational comparative effectiveness studies, and comprehensive analyses of emulation practice in oncology, evaluate the specification that was published rather than the process that produced it. The entry’s claim is about an artifact nobody keeps, which is consistent with its absence from a literature search: the evidence for it is the absence of any paper reporting one. Cites 10.1016/s1473-3099(26)00058-7: An appraisal instrument for exactly these studies, which assesses the reported design and not the chronology by which it was reached..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / overstated. A final, unversioned protocol cannot reveal unlogged alternatives or their chronology, so an auditability gap can remain. However, this is primarily a governance and implementation problem rather than an unsolved inferential method. Prospective version control, amendment records, decision logs, and trusted timestamps can preserve the history directly. The categorical assertion that registrations retain only the final protocol is not established by technical reasoning, and an unlogged history is unavailable to an auditor but not necessarily destroyed. A full multiverse is neither required for provenance nor automatically interpretable: changing populations, comparators, strategies, or outcomes creates different estimands, so their estimates do not constitute an uncertainty distribution for one parameter. A hash establishes integrity only when paired with a trusted timestamp and does not prove that no alternative analysis existed. This is a roadmap and reporting-standard item rather than a high-severity statistical gap.

Grok 4.5, recency lens

open / supported. Registrations and TARGET record the final specification. Multiverse/specification-curve methods (e.g. Simonsohn et al.) and some observational-study preregistration guidance exist, but EU PAS / ClinicalTrials-style registries and TARGET do not require rejected alternatives, decision chronology, or outcome-blinded feasibility logs as first-class artifacts. Version-controlled hashed executable specs before outcome analysis are not standard. Cost of full multiverse remains unsolved. Open as stated.

GLM-5.2, third independent lens

open / supported. The claim is coherent and proportionate. It states that registrations record only the final specification and not the alternatives considered or the chronology of decisions. The reason given—that registration systems were designed for randomized trials where the protocol precedes the data and have no natural slot for a design developed against an existing dataset—directly entails that the artifact required to settle the issue is not currently produced or demanded by these systems.

Decision path

R5:default-open → R9:substantiated-overstatement(n=1/4):codex → R17:reading-moved(confirmed-open->partially-addressed)

title: Emulation is proposed for non-pharmaceutical and policy interventions whose treatment versions and assignment units are not defined
text:
Statement
Interference, combination therapies, multiple treatment versions and non-pharmaceutical interventions all violate the two-arm, individually assigned, well-defined-intervention assumptions that the standard emulation protocol makes. Non-pharmaceutical and policy interventions are the sharpest case: the intervention is delivered to a place or an organization rather than a person, its content varies by implementer, its timing is gradual rather than dated, and there is often no version of not receiving it that is comparable. Emulation is nonetheless being applied to such questions, with the protocol components filled in by analogy. What is missing is a statement of which protocol components a policy intervention can actually satisfy and what estimand results when several cannot.

title: Emulation is proposed for non-pharmaceutical and policy interventions whose treatment versions and assignment units are not defined
text:
Why it is open
A well-defined intervention is a requirement of the causal framework and not of the emulation framework specifically, so this is inherited rather than introduced, and the emulation literature has no special claim on solving it. The assignment unit for a policy is usually a jurisdiction, which reduces the effective sample to the number of jurisdictions and makes the analysis a small-n problem regardless of how many patients it contains. Version variation is intrinsic to implementation rather than incidental, so the consistency assumption fails by construction rather than by accident.

title: Emulation is proposed for non-pharmaceutical and policy interventions whose treatment versions and assignment units are not defined
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Papadogeorgou G, Mealli F, Zigler CM. Causal inference with interfering units for cluster and population level treatment allocation programs. Biometrics 2019;75(3):778-787
Provides the estimand framework for cluster and population-level allocation, which is the setting a policy emulation is in whether or not it says so.


Hernán MA, Robins JM. Using big data to emulate a target trial when a randomized trial is not available. Am J Epidemiol 2016;183(8):758-764
States the well-defined-intervention requirement that policy questions strain, and the protocol components a policy emulation has to fill.

title: Emulation is proposed for non-pharmaceutical and policy interventions whose treatment versions and assignment units are not defined
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Write protocol templates for cluster and policy target trials in which the assignment unit, the exposure mapping and the treatment-version class are explicit components rather than assumed, and state which components a given policy question can satisfy. Where versions cannot be unified, define the estimand over the observed distribution of versions and say so, rather than naming an intervention that no jurisdiction implemented. Establish minimum unit counts for credible inference at the jurisdiction level, since a study with millions of patients and eleven jurisdictions has eleven units of assignment.

title: Emulation is proposed for non-pharmaceutical and policy interventions whose treatment versions and assignment units are not defined
text:
Verification

Verdict. Unverifiable. Auditors disagreed and the disagreement was evidence-bearing on both sides.
Dissent. literature dissented (open): The corpus contains policy and service-level emulations, including chronic disease management programs and national incentive schemes evaluated with the target trial approach, and contains no protocol template stating which components a policy intervention can satisfy or what estimand results when several cannot. […]
4 of the 4 independent auditors returned an opinion on this entry.

Literature and prior-art check

open / supported. The corpus contains policy and service-level emulations, including chronic disease management programs and national incentive schemes evaluated with the target trial approach, and contains no protocol template stating which components a policy intervention can satisfy or what estimand results when several cannot. A 2026 substance-use workshop proceedings discusses methodological innovation for emulation in that setting, which is the nearest thing to the templates the entry asks for. The claim that policy emulations are published with individual-level precision and jurisdiction-level information is supported by the applied papers in the corpus rather than by a methodological source, which is why the confidence is moderate. Cites 10.1016/j.josat.2026.210065: Addresses emulation in a service and policy setting where the intervention is delivered at more than the individual level..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

partially-solved / overstated. Target trial emulation is not intrinsically restricted to two arms or individual assignment. Combination therapies can be defined as multicomponent strategies; policies can be assigned at cluster level; and interference can be handled through explicit exposure mappings and cluster or population-level estimands. Multiple versions do not make consistency fail by construction when versions are specified, shown irrelevant, or incorporated into a well-defined stochastic intervention. The defect arises when a vague treatment label, assignment unit, version rule, timing, or interference structure is left unspecified. Cluster-level treatment variation makes the number and adoption patterns of independent clusters central to precision, but the effective sample size is not literally always the number of jurisdictions, and no universal minimum count is defensible without the design, dependence structure, and inferential method. Averaging over an observed version distribution is causal only after that stochastic intervention and its identification assumptions are defined. The cited cluster-allocation framework already resolves the alleged absence of an estimand framework, while standardized emulation protocols and finite-cluster guidance remain open. Cites 10.1111/biom.13049: As characterized in the supplied record, it provides estimands for cluster and population-level allocation under interference, resolving the claim that these settings inherently lack a causal estimand framework. It does not by itself supply a target-trial protocol template or solve finite-cluster inference..

Grok 4.5, recency lens

partially-solved / supported-with-caveat. Interference and cluster/population allocation have estimand frameworks (Papadogeorgou et al. 2019 Biometrics and related interference literature). Policy and NPI emulations appear increasingly, sometimes with cluster assignment made explicit. Still missing: standard protocol templates stating which seven components a policy/NPI can satisfy, estimands over observed version distributions when versions cannot be unified, and minimum jurisdiction-unit counts for credible assignment-level inference. Partial prior art on identification; gap on TTE protocol templates and unit-count guidance remains open. Cites 10.1111/biom.13049: Partial: estimand framework for cluster and population-level allocation with interference; does not supply TTE protocol templates for policy/NPI, version-distribution estimands as default reporting, or minimum jurisdiction-level sample-size rules..

GLM-5.2, third independent lens

open / supported. The claim is coherent and proportionate. It identifies a gap in applying emulation to non-pharmaceutical and policy interventions where treatment versions and assignment units are not well-defined. The reason given—that the well-defined intervention requirement is inherited from the causal framework, assignment units reduce to small-n problems, and version variation is intrinsic—supports the claim that the emulation literature lacks a statement of which components can be satisfied and what estimand results when they cannot.

Decision path

R3:partially-solved(n=2/4) → R7:counter-and-support-both-present(support=1/counter=1)
