title: There is no assumption dashboard, so diagnosable and undiagnosable assumptions are reported alike
text:
Statement
Exchangeability and consistency cannot be established from the observed data. Positivity, model behavior, balance and measurement validity can at least be diagnosed. Current reports blur the distinction: a propensity-score overlap plot is offered, and the reader is left to infer that the assumptions have been checked, when the plot bears on one of them and is silent on the rest. No standard set of diagnostics exists for an emulation, so what appears varies by author and by journal, and the absence of a diagnostic cannot be distinguished from a diagnostic that was run and not reported.

title: There is no assumption dashboard, so diagnosable and undiagnosable assumptions are reported alike
text:
Why it is open
A dashboard is a convention rather than a discovery, and conventions require an adopting body. Several of the components are not yet standardized as measurements, since balance at each time, support by history and phenotype validity have no agreed summary statistic in the longitudinal setting. Separating the testable from the untestable also makes the untestable ones conspicuous, which is uncomfortable and is exactly the point.

title: There is no assumption dashboard, so diagnosable and undiagnosable assumptions are reported alike
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Cashin AG, Hansford HJ, Hernán MA, et al. Transparent reporting of observational studies emulating a target trial: the TARGET statement. JAMA 2025;334(12):1084
Establishes what must be reported about the protocol and its emulation, and is explicitly not a risk-of-bias or diagnostic standard.


Hansford HJ, et al. Reporting of observational studies explicitly aiming to emulate randomized trials: a systematic review. JAMA Netw Open 2023
Across 200 published emulations, 43% did not describe all key emulation components and 57% did not describe both the target protocol and its emulation, which is the measured baseline of reporting practice.

title: There is no assumption dashboard, so diagnosable and undiagnosable assumptions are reported alike
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Define an assumption dashboard reporting covariate balance at each time, effective sample size, weight tails, support by treatment history, censoring rates, missingness, phenotype validity and sensitivity contours, arranged so that the empirically testable diagnostics are visibly separated from the untestable assumptions. Standardize a summary statistic for longitudinal balance and for support by history, since those are the two components that currently have no agreed form. Pair the dashboard with the reporting checklist so that a missing panel is a visible omission rather than an inference.

title: There is no assumption dashboard, so diagnosable and undiagnosable assumptions are reported alike
text:
Verification

Verdict. Partially addressed. Auditors found the problem open. At least one qualified how it is stated; the qualification and who made it are in the trail below. Moved by the full-text reading: 13 findings from 13 papers naming work that covers part of this problem survived both the reader and an independent second reviewer, so the verdict moves from confirmed-open to partially-addressed. A further 96 findings in the same reading restate the problem as open; the two are consistent, and the part that is covered is named above.
Dissent. literature dissented (supported): No assumption dashboard appears in the corpus. Methodological quality assessment tools for observational comparative effectiveness studies exist and score reported design features rather than requiring a standard diagnostic panel, and none separates empirically testable diagnostics from untestable assumptions in its output. […]
Revised by the full-text reading. Applied full-text reading of the consolidated library.

Verdict changed

confirmed-open -> partially-addressed 13 surviving findings from: Addressing treatment switching in the ALTA-1L trial with g-m; An Empirical Method of Detecting Time-Dependent Confounding:; Analysis of Longitudinal Studies With Repeated Outcome Measu; Raising the bar for causal inference: PLOS Medicine adopts t; Randomized Trials Built on Sand: Examples from COPD, Hormone; Revisiting the g-null Paradox.; Start with the Target Trial Protocol, Then Follow the Roadma; Statistical Methods to Adjust for Treatment Switching in Rea; Strength of evidence for paternal influence on offspring epi; TREATMENT SWITCHING: STATISTICAL AND DECISION-MAKING CHALLEN; The GRACE Checklist: A Validated Assessment Tool for High Qu; The Reporting and Methodological Recommendations for Observa; Transparent reporting of observational studies emulating a t. New citations: 10.1002/cpt.70013, 10.1002/pds.70255, 10.1017/s026646231600026x, 10.1080/15592294.2025.2594322, 10.1093/aje/kwx311, 10.1097/ede.0000000000001431, 10.1097/ede.0000000000001637, 10.1136/bmj-2025-087179, 10.1186/s12874-024-02437-6, 10.1371/journal.pmed.1004796, 10.18553/jmcp.2016.22.10.1107, 10.5041/rmmj.10082, 10.6000/1929-6029.2016.05.01.4


4 of the 4 independent auditors returned an opinion on this entry.

Literature and prior-art check

open / supported. No assumption dashboard appears in the corpus. Methodological quality assessment tools for observational comparative effectiveness studies exist and score reported design features rather than requiring a standard diagnostic panel, and none separates empirically testable diagnostics from untestable assumptions in its output. The entry’s claim that a missing diagnostic cannot be distinguished from an unreported one follows from the absence of a required panel and is supported by the reporting review showing that 43% of 200 emulations did not describe all key components. Cites 10.1016/s1473-3099(26)00058-7: An appraisal instrument in this space, which scores what was reported rather than requiring a diagnostic panel.. Cites 10.1001/jamanetworkopen.2023.36023: Measures how incompletely emulations report their components, which is the baseline the entry’s claim rests on..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / overstated. A standardized reporting convention remains a legitimate open implementation issue, but the proposed testable versus untestable division is too coarse. Observed data cannot establish exchangeability or consistency. Empirical positivity problems, nuisance-model behavior, and measured-covariate balance can be investigated, but finite-sample diagnostics cannot establish population positivity or model correctness. Measurement validity normally requires labeled, replicated, or external validation data, and balance is a property of the fitted analysis rather than a causal assumption. A dashboard would improve transparency but would not certify identification, so this is a reporting roadmap item rather than a solution to a decision-critical methodological gap.

Grok 4.5, recency lens

open / supported. No adopted, author-facing assumption dashboard that separates diagnosable diagnostics from undiagnosable identifying assumptions for target trial emulations was found. TARGET (Hansford/Cashin et al., JAMA 2025; also BMJ co-publication) is a 21-item reporting guideline for observational studies that explicitly emulate a target trial: it requires statement of the target protocol, mapping to data, identifying assumptions, and sensitivity analyses. It is deliberately not a risk-of-bias tool and not a standardized diagnostic panel; its own positioning matches the report’s prior-work note. Hansford et al. JAMA Netw Open 2023 documents uneven reporting of emulation components, which is baseline practice, not a dashboard. ROBINS-I and ROBINS-I V2 (launch materials 2024) structure reviewer risk-of-bias judgments relative to a specified target trial; that is systematic-review assessment, not a publication convention that forces authors to display balance over time, weight tails, effective sample size, support by treatment history, phenotype validity, and sensitivity contours in a fixed layout with testable panels visually separated from exchangeability and consistency. STaRT-RWE and HARPER improve protocol prespecification and reproducibility; they do not standardize longitudinal diagnostic summaries. Software ecosystems (cobalt, WeightIt, MatchIt, ipw, gfoRmula, lmtp, ltmle, adjustedCurves) supply balance, overlap, and weight diagnostics for specific designs, including some longitudinal use, but there is no field-wide agreed summary statistic for longitudinal balance or support-by-history, and no journal or regulator-mandated dashboard that makes omission of a panel a visible reporting failure. Method papers that propose or apply QBA, negative controls, or multi-panel diagnostics remain proposals or local practice, not an adopting-body convention. The core structural claim remains: conventions require adoption, and none has closed the reported gap. Queries included: assumption/diagnostic dashboard target trial; TARGET as diagnostic standard; longitudinal balance standardization cobalt WeightIt; ROBINS-I TTE diagnostics; STaRT-RWE HARPER assumption reporting 2024–2026; arXiv/medRxiv causal diagnostic checklist.

GLM-5.2, third independent lens

abstain / supported. The claim is coherent and proportionate. It identifies a real gap in current reporting practice (no standard dashboard) and the rationale correctly identifies the structural reasons (lack of standardized measurements for longitudinal balance, need for an adopting body). This is a claim about current practice. I abstain on the status axis because verifying the current state of reporting practice requires evidence I cannot reach.

Decision path

R5:default-open → R9:substantiated-overstatement(n=1/4):codex → R17:reading-moved(confirmed-open->partially-addressed)

title: Sequential emulation creates repeated participation and calendar-time confounding that its efficiency gain conceals
text: SEQ-01 Overstated High priority Promising Tractability 4/5

title: Sequential emulation creates repeated participation and calendar-time confounding that its efficiency gain conceals
text:
Statement
Sequential emulation exploits repeated eligibility: a new trial is emulated at each decision point, and a person who is eligible at many points contributes to many trials. This uses the data better than a single baseline emulation and it introduces three complications together. The same person appears in many nested trials, so the observations are dependent in a way the pooled analysis must handle. Trials begun at different calendar times occur under different treatment availability, guidelines and background risk, so calendar time confounds the pooled contrast unless it is modeled. And a person’s later eligibility is itself a consequence of earlier untreated survival, which links the trials causally rather than merely statistically. The efficiency gain is real and it is what makes these complications easy to overlook.

title: Sequential emulation creates repeated participation and calendar-time confounding that its efficiency gain conceals
text:
Why it is open
Pooling across trials requires an assumption that the effect is common across start times, which is exactly what calendar-time variation in practice makes doubtful, and testing it costs the efficiency the design was adopted for. The dependence is induced by the design rather than present in the data, so it has no natural clustering variable other than the person. Later eligibility conditional on earlier survival is a selection process, and whether it is innocuous depends on the outcome model being correct, which is the thing under test.

title: Sequential emulation creates repeated participation and calendar-time confounding that its efficiency gain conceals

What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Caniglia EC, et al. Emulating target trials to avoid immortal time bias: an application to antibiotic initiation. Epidemiology 2023
A worked sequential emulation showing how repeated decision points remove immortal time bias in a setting where treatment can begin at many times.


Su L, et al. TrialEmulation: an R package to emulate target trials for causal analysis of observational time-to-event data. arXiv 2024

title: Sequential emulation creates repeated participation and calendar-time confounding that its efficiency gain conceals
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Model calendar time explicitly as an effect modifier rather than adjusting it away, and report the trial-specific estimates alongside the pooled one so that a pooled effect resting on incompatible start times is visible. Derive variance estimators that account for repeated participation by the same person across nested trials, and check their coverage against a bootstrap over persons. Establish whether the efficiency gain survives the correct variance treatment, since the case for the design rests on a comparison that has usually been made under the naive variance.

title: Sequential emulation creates repeated participation and calendar-time confounding that its efficiency gain conceals
text:
Verification

Verdict. Overstated. 2 independent auditors judged the claim as stated too strong. Pooling across sequentially emulated trials assumes an effect common to start times that differ in treatment availability, guidelines and background risk, and trial-specific estimates are not conventionally reported alongside the pooled one.
Dissent. grok dissented (supported-with-caveat): Inverted-prior search finds substantial 2024–2025 work on two of the three complications the entry bundles, so the problem is not open as a blank slate. On repeated participation and design-induced dependence, Limozin, Seaman and Su (arXiv 2407.08317; […]
4 of the 4 independent auditors returned an opinion on this entry.

Literature and prior-art check

partially-solved / overstated. The entry asks for variance estimators that account for repeated participation across nested trials and for a check of their coverage against a bootstrap over persons. That work has been done. A 2025 Statistical Methods in Medical Research paper compares confidence intervals for sequential trial emulation with survival outcomes across the sandwich variance estimator, nonparametric bootstrap, jackknife and a linearized estimating function bootstrap, and finds the last has better coverage in the small-sample, low-event-rate, low-treatment-prevalence regime that motivates the design. Sequential trials and marginal structural models were compared for survival outcomes in 2023. The dependence half of the entry is therefore substantially answered and should not be published as open. The calendar-time half, that pooling across start times assumes a common effect and that trial-specific estimates are not reported, is untouched by this work and survives. Cites 10.1177/09622802251356594: Directly supplies and evaluates variance estimation for sequential trial emulation, including a computationally feasible bootstrap alternative, which is what the entry asks for as future work.. Cites 10.1002/sim.9718: Sets out the sequential-trials estimator alongside marginal structural models for survival outcomes, establishing the analysis the entry describes..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

partially-solved / overstated. Repeated eligibility does create within-person dependence, but the pinned implementation already addresses the standard version of that problem: TrialEmulation clusters its sandwich covariance by the original person identifier. It also includes trial start period in the pooled outcome model by default and accepts user-specified trial-period formulas, including interactions for effect heterogeneity. Calendar time confounds a pooled person-trial contrast only when it predicts both treatment and outcome; treatment-effect variation across start times is a separate effect-modification issue. Likewise, only a pooled model constrained to one treatment coefficient assumes a common effect. Later eligibility changes the eligible survivor population, but this is part of the sequence of trial-specific protocols and does not make validity depend specifically on outcome-model correctness. The efficiency gain is also not guaranteed after accounting for correlation and variable weights. Remaining work concerns coverage when weights are estimated, finite-sample behavior, diagnostics for treatment-by-start-time heterogeneity, and clearly defined standardization across changing eligible populations. Those are legitimate methodological and reporting questions, but they do not support the asserted high-severity claim that basic variance and calendar-time methods are missing. Cites CRAN TrialEmulation 0.0.4.11: Confirms that the pinned package exports the sequential expansion and pooled marginal structural model interfaces.. Cites CRAN TrialEmulation 0.0.4.11: The pooled marginal structural model includes trial start period by default and exposes the term for flexible specification.. Cites CRAN TrialEmulation 0.0.4.11: Implements person-clustered sandwich covariance, directly addressing dependence from repeated participation..

Grok 4.5, recency lens

partially-solved / supported-with-caveat. Inverted-prior search finds substantial 2024–2025 work on two of the three complications the entry bundles, so the problem is not open as a blank slate. On repeated participation and design-induced dependence, Limozin, Seaman and Su (arXiv 2407.08317; Stat Methods Med Res 2025) run a dedicated simulation comparing sandwich, nonparametric bootstrap, linearised estimating-function bootstrap and jackknife CIs for marginal risk differences under sequential trial emulation (STE), explicitly because the same patient can enter many nested trials. They report that sandwich/bootstrap/jackknife can account for that correlation, that sandwich is conservative when weight uncertainty is ignored, and that LEF bootstrap has the best small/moderate-sample coverage. That is exactly the variance and person-level bootstrap coverage work the agenda’s “direction” asks for; TrialEmulation is the implementation vehicle they use. On calendar-time confounding of pooled contrasts, DeMonte, Shook-Sa and Hudgens (arXiv 2403.18115) formalize nested trial emulation when the effect is allowed to vary over calendar time and/or time since treatment, provide a trial-effect-homogeneity test, and estimate trial-specific as well as calendar-time-varying vaccine effectiveness. That is the “model calendar time as effect modifier and report trial-specific estimates alongside the pooled one” program, at least in the vaccine setting where calendar-time heterogeneity is most obvious. Keogh et al. (Stat Med 2023) already recommended formal tests of trial-by-covariate interactions and compared sequential-trial efficiency to MSM-IPTW. What remains open, and why this is only partial: (1) Limozin evaluates CI coverage and computation, not a definitive redesign verdict that the efficiency case for STE survives person-clustered variance in general applications; sandwich conservatism means naive SEs can still overstate precision relative to person-level resampling. (2) DeMonte’s calendar-time-varying MSMs are developed and simulated for nested vaccine trials; they do not close the problem for arbitrary sustained pharmacoepidemiologic strategies or for routine non-VE sequential emulations that still pool under a common-effect assumption. (3) The third arm (later eligibility as a consequence of earlier untreated survival, so that trials are causally linked and the selection process depends on the outcome model being correct) is not resolved by either paper; no 2024–2026 work found identifies that selection away or shows it is innocuous under weak conditions. Package activity (TrialEmulation, SEQTaRget on CRAN) implements expansion and weighting but does not by itself close the identification/inference gaps. Cited prior work (Caniglia 2023; Su arXiv 2402.12083) illustrates and software-izes the design rather than solving the three complications. Queries that returned no full solution: “sequential trial emulation selection later eligibility untreated survival”; “efficiency gain sequential nested trial person-cluster sandwich vs naive”; general-journal 2024–2026 searches for a single paper closing all three arms together. Net: variance and calendar-time arms are partially methodologically addressed with evaluated tools; the bundled “still open and easy to overlook” framing is still useful but overstates residual openness if it ignores Limozin 2025 and DeMonte 2024. Cites arxiv:2407.08317: Derives and simulates person-level sandwich, nonparametric bootstrap, LEF bootstrap and jackknife inference for STE marginal risk differences when the same individual contributes to multiple nested trials; gives practical guidance on which CI method has near-nominal coverage by sample size, event rate and treatment prevalence. Partially closes the repeated-participation variance arm and the agenda’s call to check coverage against bootstrap over persons.. Cites doi:10.1177/09622802251356594: Peer-reviewed Statistical Methods in Medical Research version of the same STE variance comparison (PubMed 40631395); same resolving role as arXiv:2407.08317 for the dependence/variance complication.. Cites arxiv:2403.18115: Provides NTE IPW estimators and MSMs that allow the effect to vary over calendar time and/or time since treatment, plus a formal test of trial effect homogeneity; estimates trial-specific and calendar-time-varying effects rather than only a pooled common effect. Partially closes the calendar-time confounding / pooled-contrast arm for nested trials (vaccine effectiveness setting)..

GLM-5.2, third independent lens

open / supported. The claim is internally consistent and proportionate. It identifies three genuine complications of sequential target trial emulation—design-induced dependence from repeated participation, calendar-time confounding across start times, and survival-conditioned later eligibility—and frames them as overlooked rather than impossible to address. The reasoning for openness is coherent: pooling requires a common-effect assumption that calendar-time variation challenges; the dependence has no natural clustering variable beyond the person; and the selection process depends on outcome-model correctness, which is the inferential target. None of these are asserted as structural impossibilities; they are framed as current-practice gaps, which is the correct register. The proposed directions (model calendar time as effect modifier, derive person-level variance estimators, compare efficiency under correct variance) are constructive and imply the problems are solvable, reinforcing that the claim is about practice rather than principle. The scope is appropriate: the claim does not say sequential emulation should be abandoned, only that its efficiency gain conceals complications that need methodological attention. The severity is proportionate to the cost of a wrong pooled estimate in a treatment-effect decision. I cannot verify whether specific software or recent papers already resolve all three complications together, so I do not downgrade from open, but the claim as stated does not depend on any software capability assertion.

Decision path

R3:partially-solved(n=3/4) → R8:overstated-majority(n=2/4)

title: Generative models are evaluated on distributional fidelity and used for causal work
text:
Statement
Generative patient models would support privacy-preserving code development, power planning and method stress testing, and synthetic patient data have shown value as a benchmark environment. The evaluation practice does not match the use. A model optimized for marginal or temporal fidelity can reproduce every observed association while generating wrong counterfactuals, wrong overlap and wrong time ordering, because none of those quantities appears in the loss. Privacy mechanisms compound this by suppressing rare patterns, and rare patterns are often exactly the causally important ones. Synthetic data are not evidence about treatment effects unless the generating model is causally valid, and current benchmarks do not test whether it is.

title: Generative models are evaluated on distributional fidelity and used for causal work
text:
Why it is open
Causal fidelity is not identifiable from the observed data the generator was trained on: two structural models that agree on every observational distribution can disagree on every interventional one. Evaluating it therefore requires a gold-standard structural model rather than a real dataset, which changes the object being validated. Privacy and causal fidelity are also in direct tension, since the mechanisms that protect rare individuals remove the rare strata that carry the overlap.

title: Generative models are evaluated on distributional fidelity and used for causal work
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Shi, et al. Generating high-fidelity privacy-conscious synthetic patient data for causal effect estimation with multiple treatments. Front Artif Intell 2022
Builds synthetic patient generation aimed specifically at causal effect estimation with multiple treatments, which is where the fidelity question becomes sharp.

title: Generative models are evaluated on distributional fidelity and used for causal work
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Create causally annotated synthetic trials in which both observed and counterfactual outcomes are generated from a known structural model, so that interventional distributions have a ground truth to be scored against. Evaluate generative models on intervention response error, average and conditional effect fidelity, positivity preservation and disclosure risk, not only on distributional similarity. State as a standing rule that synthetic-effect estimates are not clinical evidence, and confine synthetic data to code development, power planning and method benchmarking.

Verification

Verdict. Partially addressed. Part of this problem is addressed by existing work; the entry names which part.
Dissent. literature dissented (open): The corpus contains synthetic patient generation aimed at causal effect estimation and generative approaches to causal graphs, and contains no evaluation of a generative model against a known structural model’s interventional distributions. […]
4 of the 4 independent auditors returned an opinion on this entry.

Literature and prior-art check

open / supported. The corpus contains synthetic patient generation aimed at causal effect estimation and generative approaches to causal graphs, and contains no evaluation of a generative model against a known structural model’s interventional distributions. The entry’s claim, that fidelity evaluation does not test causal validity, is consistent with the absence, and the confidence is capped because the generative-model literature sits mostly in venues these eight phrases would not retrieve. Cites 10.3389/frai.2022.918813: Targets synthetic generation at causal estimation, which is where the fidelity question becomes consequential..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / overstated. The central warning is correct: observational distributional fidelity alone does not establish counterfactual fidelity. The impossibility argument is nevertheless too broad. Observationally equivalent causal models can disagree on some interventions, not necessarily every intervention. Interventional distributions can also be identified under explicit causal assumptions or evaluated using randomized or other interventional data, so a known structural simulator is not the only possible benchmark. Positivity and treatment overlap are properties of the observed longitudinal law; a generator that exactly preserves the full joint law preserves them, although marginal-fidelity metrics can miss serious conditional-support errors. Temporal ordering is likewise observable and testable. Privacy protection creates a utility tradeoff for rare strata but does not invariably remove them or create a direct mathematical conflict with causal fidelity.

Grok 4.5, recency lens

partially-solved / supported. Inverted prior: assume causal evaluation of synthetic patients is already standard. The report’s own prior work (Shi et al. 2022) already builds privacy-conscious synthetic data with ground-truth multi-treatment effects, so the agenda’s proposed direction (causally annotated synthetic trials) has a published instance rather than a blank slate. Amad et al. (arXiv 2510.18768; NeurIPS 2025) explicitly diagnose evaluation on distributional resemblance while treatments invite causal analysis, state desiderata (covariate distribution, treatment assignment mechanism, outcome generation mechanism), propose metrics (precision/recall on covariates, propensity JSD, PEHE utility), and introduce STEAM to factor generation along that DGP. That is substantive prior art on evaluation design and generation, not mere marginal fidelity.


It does not solve the problem as a field practice claim. STEAM and Shi are proposals/datasets, not industry standard. Causal fidelity of a generator trained only on observational data remains non-identifiable without a structural gold standard; two SCMs can match all observational margins and disagree on interventions. Privacy mechanisms that erase rare strata still conflict with positivity-relevant tails. Hernandez et al. (Front Digit Health 2025) still frame synthetic tabular evaluation around fidelity/utility/privacy without interventional ground truth. Queries run: causal fidelity synthetic evaluation; STEAM treatment effect synthetic data; Shi 2022 ground truth; PEHE synthetic medical; synthetic patient counterfactual evaluation 2024–2026. No evidence that clinical or regulatory use treats synthetic-effect estimates as non-evidence by default, nor that mainstream generators are scored on intervention response error. Partial solve of evaluation methodology; the practice mismatch remains open. Cites 10.3389/frai.2022.918813: Provides a large synthetic patient resource with explicit ground-truth effects for many hypertension treatments, showing that causally annotated synthetic data for multi-treatment effect estimation already exists as prior art (partial instance of the agenda’s proposed direction).. Cites arxiv:2510.18768: Formalizes that standard synthetic evaluation ignores treatment-specific causal structure; defines causal-use desiderata and metrics (propensity fidelity, PEHE utility); proposes STEAM generation aligned to those metrics. Partially closes the evaluation-design gap without making causal scoring universal practice..

GLM-5.2, third independent lens

open / supported. The claim is structurally sound and proportionate. The core identifiability argument—that two structural models agreeing on every observational distribution can disagree on every interventional one—is a well-established result in causal inference and correctly grounds the claim that causal fidelity cannot be assessed from observational data alone. The claim does not assert that causally valid generators are impossible to build; it asserts that current benchmarks do not test for causal validity, which is a claim about practice, not about impossibility. The tension between privacy mechanisms and causal fidelity (suppression of rare patterns that carry overlap) is a genuine practical tradeoff, correctly framed as tension rather than impossibility. The standing rule proposed—that synthetic-effect estimates are not clinical evidence—is proportionate to the severity of the error (clinical decisions based on non-causally-valid synthetic data). The scope is right: the claim is about evaluation practice, not about the existence of generative models per se.

Decision path

R3:partially-solved(n=1/4) → R9:substantiated-overstatement(n=1/4):codex

text: STR-01 Partially addressed High priority Emerging Tractability 3/5

title: No procedure defines clinically defensible equivalence classes of treatment versions
text:
Statement
A per-protocol effect requires censoring at deviation and weighting for the informative censoring that censoring creates. Beneath that mechanics sits a question the mechanics assume away: what counts as the same treatment. Real treatments differ by dose, route, provider, formulation, combination and adherence pattern, and two regimens sharing a label may not satisfy consistency. Clone-censor-weight handles the case where baseline assignment is genuinely ambiguous, at the cost of data expansion, artificial censoring and sensitivity to the censoring model, but it takes the strategy definition as given. There is no guidance for constructing defensible equivalence classes of treatment versions, and none for overlapping combination therapies where a patient is simultaneously compatible with more than one labeled strategy.

title: No procedure defines clinically defensible equivalence classes of treatment versions
text:
Why it is open
Consistency is an assumption about the world rather than about the data, so no amount of data adjudicates whether two versions are the same treatment. The clinical judgment that would adjudicate it is specific to the drug, the indication and the era, which makes a general criterion the wrong shape for the problem. Making the versions explicit also multiplies the strategies, and each additional strategy costs positivity, so the honest specification is often the one the data cannot support.

title: No procedure defines clinically defensible equivalence classes of treatment versions
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Gaber CE, Ghazarian AA, Strassle PD, et al. De-mystifying the clone-censor-weight method for causal research using observational data. Cancer Med 2024
A didactic account of cloning, artificial censoring and censoring weights, including the computational cost and the sensitivity to the censoring model.


Cain LE, Robins JM, Lanoy E, Logan R, Costagliola D, Hernán MA. Using observational data to emulate a randomized trial of dynamic treatment-switching strategies. Int J Epidemiol 2016;45(6):2038-2049
Defines dynamic switching strategies precisely enough to emulate, which is the closest existing template for specifying what a strategy includes.


lmtp: Non-Parametric Causal Effects of Feasible Interventions Based on Modified Treatment Policies. CRAN
Supports continuous and multivariate treatments, which is the representation a dose-and-adherence strategy needs.

title: No procedure defines clinically defensible equivalence classes of treatment versions
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Use hierarchical treatment ontologies and latent treatment-version models so that the equivalence class is an explicit, versioned object rather than an implicit one, and estimate the joint effect of initiation, dose and adherence through longitudinal modified treatment policies rather than through a single binary strategy. Use causal discovery only to generate hypotheses about which versions are consequential; final strategy definitions must stay clinically specified, because a version set chosen to maximize the apparent effect is a result rather than a design. Quantify, by simulation, how much bias a wrong equivalence class induces relative to the positivity cost of the correct one, since that trade is the actual decision.

title: No procedure defines clinically defensible equivalence classes of treatment versions
text:
Verification

Verdict. Partially addressed. Part of this problem is addressed by existing work; the entry names which part.
Dissent. codex dissented (overstated): Treatment-version ambiguity is real: collapsing causally different doses, formulations, routes, combinations, or adherence patterns can make the named intervention ill-defined. However, the report overstates both the required mechanics and the remaining gap. Estimating a per-protocol effect does not require artificial censoring plus inverse-probability weighting; […]
4 of the 4 independent auditors returned an opinion on this entry.

Literature and prior-art check

partially-solved / supported-with-caveat. The treatment-versions problem has a longer literature than the entry credits. Confounding adjustment in the presence of multiple versions of treatment was worked out for an organ-transplant application in 2019, and marginal structural models for partial exposure regimes date to 2008. A 2026 iScience paper shows that changing the exposure definition unmasks confounding in an applied emulation, which is empirical evidence for the entry’s premise and also evidence that the field is examining it. What remains genuinely absent is guidance for constructing defensible equivalence classes and for overlapping combination therapies, which is the constructive half of the entry rather than the diagnostic half. Cites 10.1007/s10654-019-00484-8: Works out what adjustment means when a labeled treatment covers several versions, which the entry treats as unaddressed.. Cites 10.1093/biostatistics/kxn012: Provides estimation for regimes that specify treatment only partially, which is the representation an underspecified strategy needs.. Cites 10.1016/j.isci.2026.116584: Shows empirically that the exposure definition changes the answer in an emulation, which is the consequence the entry predicts..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

partially-solved / overstated. Treatment-version ambiguity is real: collapsing causally different doses, formulations, routes, combinations, or adherence patterns can make the named intervention ill-defined. However, the report overstates both the required mechanics and the remaining gap. Estimating a per-protocol effect does not require artificial censoring plus inverse-probability weighting; the longitudinal g-formula and targeted or sequential-regression estimators can estimate sustained-strategy effects under their respective identification and modeling conditions. Clone-censor-weight already provides the bookkeeping for individuals compatible with multiple prespecified strategies, although it cannot choose those strategies or determine which versions are equivalent. Observed data cannot prove treatment-version irrelevance, but version-specific data can reveal heterogeneity and inform clinical judgment. Finer definitions may worsen practical support and precision, but every additional strategy does not mechanically violate positivity. Pinned lmtp 1.5.4 is correctly described: its NAMESPACE exports lmtp_tmle and lmtp_sdr, while its source accepts list-valued treatment nodes and applies analyst-specified multivariate shifts. It therefore supports estimation after a joint policy has been defined, not construction of clinical equivalence classes. Moreover, a longitudinal modified treatment policy generally targets a natural-value-dependent policy estimand, not automatically the per-protocol effect of a fixed sustained strategy. The issue is decision-critical when collapsed versions have materially different effects; a universal treatment ontology or latent-version model is a roadmap item rather than a prerequisite for every well-specified emulation. Cites 10.1002/cam4.70461: Provides the cloning, artificial-censoring, and weighting procedure for individuals whose observed histories are simultaneously compatible with multiple predefined strategies. It does not determine which treatment versions should constitute a strategy.. Cites CRAN:lmtp@1.5.4: Pinned source exports longitudinal TMLE and sequentially doubly robust estimators and implements analyst-specified multivariate treatment shifts. This resolves the joint-policy estimation component after treatment variables and the intervention have been defined, but not equivalence-class construction..

Grok 4.5, recency lens

open / supported. Inverted-prior search does not find a procedure that constructs clinically defensible equivalence classes of treatment versions for consistency in sustained-strategy target-trial emulation. The report’s own cited works do not close the gap: Gaber et al. (2024, 10.1002/cam4.70461) is a didactic CCW primer that takes the strategy as given; Cain et al. (2016, 10.1093/ije/dyv295) is the closest specification template for dynamic switching but does not adjudicate dose, route, formulation, provider, or combination-version equivalence; lmtp supplies estimation for continuous and multivariate modified treatment policies once an intervention is defined, not a clinical rule for which versions may be labeled the same treatment. Classic prior art formalizes the identification problem without solving clinical construction: VanderWeele and Hernán (2013, J Causal Inference; multiple versions) and Hernán and VanderWeele (2011, compound treatments) show when version-mixed averages versus version-specific effects are identifiable, which strengthens rather than resolves the claim that consistency is a world assumption adjudicated by clinical judgment specific to drug, indication, and era. 2024–2026 work remains proposal-level or off-scope. Yoshikawa and Kawano (arXiv:2601.00287, 2026) propose mixture-of-experts estimation of latent versions under point treatment; the number of versions is pre-specified, versions are data-driven latent classes rather than clinically specified equivalence classes, and the paper itself notes that version-specific methodology was previously underdeveloped. That is a partial advance along the report’s proposed latent-version direction, not a solved clinical procedure, and it does not cover sustained or dynamic strategies or overlapping multi-drug regimens. Ostropolets et al. (2024) ATC–RxNorm hierarchies improve drug coding and retrieval; they are not causal equivalence classes for consistency. Fu et al. (BMJ 2026) and related CCW guidance clarify cloning when baseline data are compatible with more than one labeled strategy; that is the mechanics the report already credits, still leaving strategy definition as input. Practical TTE guides (e.g. Fridén 2026) restate “define interventions so relevant multiple versions do not exist” without a constructive algorithm. Package release notes and GitHub activity for TrialEmulation, gfoRmula, gfoRmulaICE, lmtp, ltmle, WeightIt, MatchIt, and related tools implement estimation given a user-defined regimen; none encode an equivalence-class constructor. 2025–2026 FDA RWE / externally controlled trial materials, EMA/HMA registry guidance, HARPER/STaRT-RWE, ENCePP, and TARGET-style reporting require explicit treatment-strategy specification but do not supply a general method for building clinically defensible version sets or for adjudicating simultaneous multi-strategy compatibility beyond cloning. Because consistency is structurally untestable from data alone, sensitivity analyses and latent-mixture recoveries quantify consequences or statistical heterogeneity; they do not identify clinical sameness. Queries that returned nothing closing the gap included combinations of: treatment version equivalence class + target trial; clinically defensible versions of treatment + consistency; hierarchical ontology + causal strategy definition + sustained treatment; overlapping combination therapy + clone-censor equivalence; and journal-restricted 2024–2026 searches in AJE, Epidemiology, IJE, Stat Med, Biometrics, BMJ, JAMA, plus arXiv stat.ME and medRxiv. Residual risk is a narrowly scoped clinical protocol for one drug class that was not indexed under causal-inference terms; that would at most partially narrow the problem for that class, not the general gap as stated.

GLM-5.2, third independent lens

abstain / supported-with-caveat. The claim is internally consistent and identifies a genuine structural tension: consistency is an assumption about the world, not the data, so clinical adjudication of treatment-version equivalence is inherently context-specific (drug, indication, era). The report’s own reasoning—that ‘a general criterion [is] the wrong shape for the problem’—supports a structural impossibility for a universal procedure, which is a stronger and more defensible claim than the empirical assertion that ‘no guidance exists.’ The latter is a negative existential about the current literature that I cannot verify without search. Additionally, the report itself cites Cain et al. 2016 as ‘the closest existing template for specifying what a strategy includes,’ which suggests related guidance exists even if it does not directly address equivalence-class construction. The claim is pitched at a level that conflates a structural limitation (no general procedure can work) with an empirical gap (no guidance has been written), and the proposed direction (ontologies, latent models, modified treatment policies) implies that partial frameworks are possible, undercutting the implication that the problem is permanently intractable. The severity is proportionate: a wrong equivalence class induces bias, and the positivity trade-off is a real decision cost. I abstain on status because confirming the absence of all guidance requires literature search I cannot perform.

Decision path

R3:partially-solved(n=2/3) → R9:substantiated-overstatement(n=1/4):codex

title: Negative controls, proxies and validation data are not integrated into a standard emulation workflow
text:
Statement
Specifying a target trial prevents the temporal biases an analyst inflicts on themselves; it does not create randomization. Active-comparator new-user designs, high-dimensional propensity scores and richer clinical measurements all reduce residual confounding without guaranteeing exchangeability. The tools that address what remains, negative control outcomes and exposures, instrumental variables, proximal causal learning and external validation samples, exist separately and are not part of any standard emulation workflow: there is no agreed order in which to apply them, no convention for reporting what each one bought, and no accepted way to combine their answers when they disagree. Covariate balance continues to be reported as though it bore on unmeasured confounding, which it does not.

title: Negative controls, proxies and validation data are not integrated into a standard emulation workflow
text:
Why it is open
Each of these tools identifies under assumptions that are themselves untestable and that differ from one another, so combining them is not a matter of adding evidence but of reconciling incompatible identification stories. A negative control shares only some of the confounding mechanisms of the primary outcome, and how much is not knowable from the data. Proximal methods need proxies satisfying completeness-type conditions that cannot be checked, and weak proxies produce unstable estimates that look like precision loss rather than assumption failure. Validation subsamples are rarely random, which imports a second selection problem into the correction for the first.

title: Negative controls, proxies and validation data are not integrated into a standard emulation workflow
text:
What has been tried




Work
What it contributes




Hubbard RA, Hernán MA. “Target trial emulation” for observational studies: potential and pitfalls. N Engl J Med 2024
States plainly that emulation removes design-induced bias and leaves confounding, which is the boundary this problem sits on.


Hernán MA, Robins JM. Using big data to emulate a target trial when a randomized trial is not available. Am J Epidemiol 2016;183(8):758-764
The foundational framework: it specifies the seven protocol components and their observational mapping, and locates confounding outside what the framework itself resolves.

title: Negative controls, proxies and validation data are not integrated into a standard emulation workflow
text:
Probable solution or research direction
Develop a proximal emulation in which treatment-inducing and outcome-inducing proxies are declared in the protocol alongside the negative controls, and estimate the primary effect under the proximal identification conditions as well as the conventional ones. Report the conventional estimate next to E-values, bias functions, Rosenbaum-style sensitivity models, tipping-point analyses and priors on unmeasured confounding, all keyed to the same estimand so the reader sees one quantity under several assumption sets. Establish, by simulation, how far negative-control calibration transfers when the control shares only part of the confounding structure, because that is the assumption the method makes and never states.

title: Negative controls, proxies and validation data are not integrated into a standard emulation workflow
text:
Verification

Verdict. Partially addressed. Auditors found the problem open. At least one qualified how it is stated; the qualification and who made it are in the trail below. Moved by the full-text reading: 20 findings from 20 papers naming work that covers part of this problem survived both the reader and an independent second reviewer, so the verdict moves from confirmed-open to partially-addressed. A further 69 findings in the same reading restate the problem as open; the two are consistent, and the part that is covered is named above.
Dissent. literature dissented (supported): Searching for an integrated workflow combining negative controls, proxies, instrumental variables and validation data within an emulation returned applied studies that use one of these tools, not a workflow that orders or combines them. […]
Revised by the full-text reading. Applied full-text reading of the consolidated library.

Verdict changed

confirmed-open -> partially-addressed 20 surviving findings from: Adjacent spillover efficacy of Wolbachia for control of deng; Antiretroviral Therapy and Mortality in Rural South Africa: ; Assessing Wolbachia-mediated sterility for dengue control: e; Association of Medication Use and 8-Year Mortality Risk in P; Comparison of the Test-negative Design and Cohort Design Wit; Controlling Time-Dependent Confounding by Health Status and ; Effectiveness of a Covid mRNA Vaccine Against Two Early Vari; Emulating target trials of postexposure vaccines using obser; Emulating the LEADER trial in China: a regulatory science ca; Estimating cardiovascular effects of influenza vaccination i; Estimating the Effects of Lifestyle Interventions on Mortali; Exposure definition sensitivity unmasks hidden confounding i; Incorporating genetic data improves target trial emulations ; Making fair comparisons in pregnancy medication safety studi; Observational methods for COVID-19 vaccine effectiveness res; Simultaneously Dealing With Immortal Time Bias and Residual ; Strengthening inferential studies in the FDA Sentinel initia; Target Trial Emulation Using Cohort Studies: Estimating the ; The Impact of Unemployment on Antidepressant Purchasing: Adj; Trial Emulation Methods.. New citations: 10.1002/pds.4336, 10.1002/pds.70174, 10.1016/j.eclinm.2025.103449, 10.1016/j.isci.2026.116584, 10.1038/s41588-025-02229-8, 10.1038/s41746-025-02234-5, 10.1053/j.ajkd.2023.07.024, 10.1093/aje/kwae350, 10.1093/aje/kwu485, 10.1093/aje/kwy065, 10.1093/ije/dyad138, 10.1093/jtm/taae103, 10.1097/ede.0000000000000985, 10.1097/ede.0000000000001709, 10.1097/ede.0000000000001802, 10.1097/ede.0000000000001889, 10.1186/s12916-025-03941-2, 10.1212/wnl.0000000000213783, 10.3389/fendo.2026.1777954, 10.7759/cureus.90666


4 of the 4 independent auditors returned an opinion on this entry.

Literature and prior-art check

open / supported. Searching for an integrated workflow combining negative controls, proxies, instrumental variables and validation data within an emulation returned applied studies that use one of these tools, not a workflow that orders or combines them. A 2026 iScience paper shows exposure-definition sensitivity unmasking hidden confounding in a crystalloid emulation, which is a diagnostic in the family the entry describes and is a single-tool example. Proximal causal inference has been applied within an emulation for influenza vaccination and cardiovascular events, again as one method rather than as part of a standard sequence. The entry’s claim is about integration and reporting convention rather than about any missing method, and nothing in the corpus supplies that. Cites 10.1016/j.isci.2026.116584: Demonstrates one diagnostic for residual confounding inside an emulation, showing the tools are reaching applied work individually..

GPT-5.6 Sol, technical and source-code lens

open / overstated. The integration and reporting problem is legitimate, but several technical absolutes are wrong. Merely specifying a target trial does not prevent temporal bias; correct time-zero alignment and implementation can prevent particular design-induced biases. Active-comparator new-user designs, high-dimensional propensity scores, and richer measurements are not guaranteed to reduce confounding and can introduce bias through poor comparator or variable selection. Negative controls often diagnose or falsify rather than identify a corrected effect. Instrument relevance and some proxy-strength or rank features are assessable even though exclusion, proxy validity, and completeness relative to latent confounding are not fully testable. IV, proximal, and conventional analyses can also target different estimands, so E-values, Rosenbaum analyses, bias functions, and causal estimates are not automatically commensurate answers about one quantity. Balance on ordinary measured covariates cannot establish balance on unmeasured confounders, although validated proxies can provide indirect information. Residual confounding is decision-critical, but the absence of one universal integration workflow is primarily a standardization and triangulation problem; the asserted very-high severity and claim that the framework does nothing to secure exchangeability are inflated. No R or Python package capability is asserted here.

Grok 4.5, recency lens

open / supported-with-caveat. Inverted-prior search treated the gap as already closed and looked for a field-standard emulation pipeline that declares negative controls, treatment/outcome proxies, proximal identification, instruments, and validation samples in the protocol, reports what each tool bought on a shared estimand, and reconciles disagreements. That standard was not found. The cited works (Hubbard–Hernán 2024; Hernán–Robins 2016) correctly locate residual confounding outside protocol design; they do not integrate residual-confounding tools into a workflow. Recent literature and software add components and occasional applications, not a consensus order or combination rule. Guo et al. (2025) run a target trial emulation under proximal causal inference with declared NCE/NCO proxies and sensitivity swaps of those controls: that is a serious applied fusion of TTE and PCI, not a field standard or a protocol template for combining PCI with E-values, bias functions, Rosenbaum models, tipping points, and external validation on one estimand. BenchExCal (Wang et al. 2025) proposes a structured benchmark–expand–calibration process that uses negative-control calibration in an emulation pipeline; the paper is a design and planned evaluation, not an established convention. Practical TTE checklists and operational EHR frameworks (e.g., Tran 2026; Nature Digital Medicine operational TTE 2026) recommend negative-control diagnostics, which softens the claim that residual tools are invisible in guidance, but still treat them as optional diagnostics rather than protocol-declared primary analyses. TARGET (JAMA 2025) is a reporting checklist for emulations; it does not prescribe proximal protocols or multi-tool reconciliation. CRAN task-view and package checks (TrialEmulation, gfoRmula, gfoRmulaICE, lmtp, ltmle, WeightIt, MatchIt, cobalt, PCL) show no merged standard that wires NCO panels, proximal estimation, validation-sample correction, and conventional estimands into one emulation API. Distributional NCO diagnosis/calibration work on medRxiv (2026) is a proposal. Sensitivity and proximal methods still rest on untestable, non-identical identification stories; papers that propose or apply methods do not solve combination under disagreement. Covariate balance remains widely reported without claiming identification of unmeasured confounding in the sources retrieved. Queries run: TTE+proximal; NCO calibration/BenchExCal/TARGET; PCI software (PCL, regression-based PCI); package/CRAN activity for TrialEmulation/gfoRmula/lmtp; guidance (TARGET, ENCePP, ICH). Net: the problem as stated (no agreed integrated residual-confounding workflow for emulations) remains open; the caveat is that TTE+PCI applications and NCO-centric calibration proposals now exist and should be cited as prior art, not as closure.

GLM-5.2, third independent lens

open / supported. The claim is internally consistent and correctly scoped as a problem of current practice (lack of standardization and integration) rather than a structural impossibility. The reasons given for it being open (incompatible identification stories, untestable assumptions differing across tools) genuinely support the claim that these tools are not currently integrated into a standard emulation workflow. The severity is proportionate to the methodological gap.

Decision path

R5:default-open → R9:substantiated-overstatement(n=1/4):codex → R17:reading-moved(confirmed-open->partially-addressed)

89 papers in the reviewed corpus bear on this problem, published 2013 to 2026. Progress and a fresh assertion of openness land in the same year.
